## techqa_DEV_Q252#row-0006

Question:
How to resolve the StaleConnectionException in WebSphere Application Server? I see this exception in WebSphere Application Server J2c and RRA traces:

WSRdbManagedC > preTestConnection Entry WSRdbManagedConnectionImpl@51a507f2 query: SELECT 1 FROM DUAL WSRdbManagedC 3 Exception java.sql.SQLException: ORA-02396: exceeded maximum idle time, please connect again DSRA0010E: SQL State = 61000, Error Code = 2,396 at oracle.jdbc.driver.T4CTTIoer.processError(T4CTTIoer.java:440) at 
...
Entry java.sql.SQLException: ORA-01012: not logged on ..... OracleDataSto < findMappingClass return Exit class com.ibm.websphere.ce.cm.StaleConnectionException

Reference / gold answer:
To resolve the StaleConnectionException in WebSphere Application Server, you need to set the "Validate on Reserve" property to true for the connection pool associated with the data source in WebSphere Application Server. This setting will ensure that the connections are validated before being returned to the application to prevent stale connections. 

Additionally, you may need to adjust the maximum idle time setting in the Oracle database to prevent the ORA-02396 error. This can be done by modifying the SQLNET.ORA file on the Oracle server to increase the value of the SQLNET.EXPIRE_TIME parameter. 

By setting "Validate on Reserve" to true in the connection pool and adjusting the maximum idle time in the Oracle database, you should be able to resolve the StaleConnectionException in WebSphere Application Server.

- `E1.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When WebSphere Application Server attempts to recover Oracle database transactions, the following exception is issued:
- `E1.S3`: WTRN0037W: The transaction service encountered an error on an xa_recover operation. The resource was com.ibm.ws.rsadapter.spi.WSRdbXaResourceImpl@1114a62. The error code was XAER_RMERR. The exception stack trace follows: javax.transaction.xa.XAException
at oracle.jdbc.xa.OracleXAResource.recover(OracleXAResource.java:726)
at com.ibm.ws.rsadapter.spi.WSRdbXaResourceImpl.recover(WSRdbXaResourceImpl.java:954)
at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.XARminst.recover(XARminst.java:137)
at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.XARecoveryData.recover(XARecoveryData.java:609)
at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.PartnerLogTable.recover(PartnerLogTable.java:511)
at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.RecoveryManager.resync(RecoveryManager.java:1784)
at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.RecoveryManager.run(RecoveryManager.java:2241)
- `E1.S4`: CAUSE
Oracle requires that you have special permissions to attempt to perform the recovery.
If there is a system crash during a distributed transaction, the WebSphere Application Server transaction manager will attempt to clean up any failed transactions which it finds in the transaction logs. 
When the recovery involves an Oracle XAResource, the Oracle JDBC driver 
oracle.jdbc.xa.OracleXAResource.recover function will make a call to DIST_TXN_SYNC.
- `E1.S5`: The above error occurs when the user trying to execute the .recover method does not have sufficient privileges to make a call to DIST_TXN_SYNC.
- `E1.S6`: ENVIRONMENT
This problem can occur with all versions of Oracle: 10g, 11g, and 12g.
- `E1.S7`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Run the following commands as user SYS:
- `E1.S8`: grant select on pending_trans$ to <user>; 
grant select on dba_2pc_pending to <user>;
grant select on dba_pending_transactions to <user>;
grant execute on dbms_system to <user>; (If using Oracle 10.2.0.3 or lower JDBC driver)
grant execute on dbms_xa to <user>; (If using Oracle 10.2.0.4 or higher JDBC driver)
- `E1.S9`: Where <user> is the username configured in the Oracle datasource's authentication alias.
- `E1.S10`: This problem is mentioned under Oracle bug: 3979190. Running the preceding commands solve the problem.
- `E1.S11`: Update: Since the SYS.DBMS_SYSTEM package contains many procedures, granting execute privileges to that package gives access to all of them. In Oracle patch 5892995 (JDBC driver) and 5945463 (server), Oracle has moved the DIST_TXN_SYNC procedure to a new package called DBMS_XA. These patches are available in 10.2.0.4 and higher. By using the new DBMS_XA package, it will reduce the security risk which DBMS_SYSTEM might cause.
- `E1.S12`: If the recovery of the inflight transactions is not important, then one possible workaround to this problem is to remove the transaction logs. (Does NOT apply to WebSphere Process Server and IBM Business Process Manager, please see note below for details)
- `E1.S13`: The transaction logs are stored in the following folder:
<WebSphere Application Server_install_root>\profiles\<PROFILE_NAME>\tranlog\<CELL_NAME>\<NODE_NAME>\<SERVER_NAME>\transaction
- `E1.S14`: To remove the transaction logs, do the following:
(1) Stop the server.
(2) Delete the '\transaction' folder and all subdirectories.
(3) Restart the server. 
The above exceptions will no longer occur.
- `E1.S15`: NOTE: Transaction logs should NOT be deleted if running in a WebSphere Process Server or IBM Business Process Manager environment. 
The WebSphere Process Server and IBM Business Process Manager systems can get into an inconsistent state because the logs are tightly coupled with information in other places like BPEDB, WPSDB, SIB messages and MQ, if it is configured.
- `E1.S16`: If WebSphere Process Server or IBM Business Process Manager is being used, follow the information in this document:
- `E1.S17`: How to resolve Transaction- and Partnerlog recovery issues in WebSphere Process Server (WPS) and IBM Business Process Manager (BPM)

- `E2.S1`: v61rnotes; SQLException ORA-01483; v612rnotes TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E2.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 If WebSphere® Process Server is configured with Oracle 9i as the database, and Oracle Thin Driver as the database driver, failed events are not saved to the database if the event size is larger than 4 KB.
- `E2.S3`: SYMPTOM
The following exception is written to the logs:
- `E2.S4`: java.sql.SQLException: ORA-01483: invalid length for DATE or NUMBER bind variable
DSRA0010E: SQL State = 72000, Error Code = 1,483 
CAUSE
The Oracle 9i Thin Driver limits the size of data to no more than 4 KB for VARCHAR2, NVARCHAR2, BLOB, and CLOB types.
- `E2.S5`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Use either of the following solutions to solve the problem:
- `E2.S6`: * Use the Oracle 10g driver file.  1. Log on to the administrative console and navigate to Environment > WebSphere Variables.
- `E2.S7`: 2. Select the variable ORACLE_JDBC_DRIVER_PATH.
- `E2.S8`: 3. Change the variable value to the folder that contains the Oracle 10g driver (ojdbc14.jar).
- `E2.S9`: 4. Save the configuration.
- `E2.S10`: 5. Restart the server.
- `E2.S11`: Note: In a network deployment environment, change the variable value at the cell level and in all of the nodes scopes, and restart all of the servers and deployment manager processes.
- `E2.S12`: * If the Oracle server or client is installed and configured correctly on the same system as WebSphere Process Server, change the data source to use the Oracle 9i OCI driver.  1. Log on to the administrative console and navigate to Resources > JDBC > Data sources.
- `E2.S13`: 2. Select the data source with the JNDI name jdbc/WPSDB.
- `E2.S14`: 3. Change the URL format from Thin to OCI. For example, if the original URL is jdbc:oracle:thin:@localhost:1521:WPRCSDB, change it to jdbc:oracle:oci:@WPRCSDB.
- `E2.S15`: 4. Save the configuration.
- `E2.S16`: 5. Restart the server.
- `E3.S1`: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 The embedded WebSphere Application Server that is installed with IBM InfoSphere Content Collector can use only the Oracle ojdbc6.jar JDBC driver to connect to an Oracle data store.
- `E3.S3`: SYMPTOM
Errors like the following are logged:
- `E3.S4`: J2CA0036E: An exception occurred while invoking method setDataSourceProperties on com.ibm.ws.rsadapter.spi.WSManagedConnectionFactoryImpl used by resource jdbc/afuConfigurationDatabase : com.ibm.ws.exception.WsException: DSRA0023E: The DataSource implementation class "oracle.jdbc.xa.client.OracleXADataSource" could not be found.
- `E3.S5`: CAUSE
You can specify the directory of the JDBC driver in the IBM InfoSphere Content Collector Configuration Manager. However, you cannot specify a specific JDBC driver file.
- `E3.S6`: If you connect to an Oracle data store, Content Collector uses the value of the WebSphere environment variable ORACLE_JDBC_DRIVER_PATH to locate the Oracle JDBC driver and assumes that the driver file name is ojdbc6.jar. If ojdbc6.jar is not found, the Content Collector WebApplications service cannot connect to the Oracle data store. Various connectivity errors are logged.
- `E3.S7`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
Check the resources.xmlfile in the directory
- `E3.S8`: <ContentCollector>\AFUWeb\profiles\<profile name>\config\cells\<CellName>\nodes\<nodename>
- `E3.S9`: Resolve the problem as mentioned below if it contains the following class path element:
<classpath>${ORACLE_JDBC_DRIVER_PATH}/ojdbc6.jar</classpath>
Do not modify the resources.xml file.
- `E3.S10`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
To resolve the problem:
- `E3.S11`: 1. Create a copy of the Oracle JDBC driver that is installed on the IBM InfoSphere Content Collector system in the same location where the current driver resides (for example, copy ojdbc14.jar for Oracle 10g). 
 2. Rename the copy as ojdbc6.jar. 
 3. Restart the IBM InfoSphere Content Collector WebApplications service.

   *                  Server V7.0 and V8.0                        *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: Syncrhonization between FFDC            *
   *                      incidents can cause a server hang       *
   *                      when an unrecoverable problem           *
   *                      occurs in a given incident.             *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   Syncrhonization between FFDC incidents can cause a server hang
   when an unrecoverable problem occurs in a given incident.
- `E4.S18`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  FFDC has been modified to ensure that incidents can continue
   to be logged from other components when a given component's
   incident-handling hangs a thread.  The impact to this is that
   the FFDC summary log may indicate that the incident file of a
   bad thread was created, while the thread may not have returned
   so the incident file will not exist.  Therefore, a missing
   incident entry that might have appeared in a summary file is
   an indication that the component logging to FFDC did not
   return control.

- `E2.S1`: v61rnotes; SQLException ORA-01483; v612rnotes TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E2.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 If WebSphere® Process Server is configured with Oracle 9i as the database, and Oracle Thin Driver as the database driver, failed events are not saved to the database if the event size is larger than 4 KB.
- `E2.S3`: SYMPTOM
The following exception is written to the logs:
- `E2.S4`: java.sql.SQLException: ORA-01483: invalid length for DATE or NUMBER bind variable
DSRA0010E: SQL State = 72000, Error Code = 1,483 
CAUSE
The Oracle 9i Thin Driver limits the size of data to no more than 4 KB for VARCHAR2, NVARCHAR2, BLOB, and CLOB types.
- `E2.S5`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Use either of the following solutions to solve the problem:
- `E2.S6`: * Use the Oracle 10g driver file.  1. Log on to the administrative console and navigate to Environment > WebSphere Variables.
- `E2.S7`: 2. Select the variable ORACLE_JDBC_DRIVER_PATH.
- `E2.S8`: 3. Change the variable value to the folder that contains the Oracle 10g driver (ojdbc14.jar).
- `E2.S9`: 4. Save the configuration.
- `E2.S10`: 5. Restart the server.
- `E2.S11`: Note: In a network deployment environment, change the variable value at the cell level and in all of the nodes scopes, and restart all of the servers and deployment manager processes.
- `E2.S12`: * If the Oracle server or client is installed and configured correctly on the same system as WebSphere Process Server, change the data source to use the Oracle 9i OCI driver.  1. Log on to the administrative console and navigate to Resources > JDBC > Data sources.
- `E2.S13`: 2. Select the data source with the JNDI name jdbc/WPSDB.
- `E2.S14`: 3. Change the URL format from Thin to OCI. For example, if the original URL is jdbc:oracle:thin:@localhost:1521:WPRCSDB, change it to jdbc:oracle:oci:@WPRCSDB.
- `E2.S15`: 4. Save the configuration.
- `E2.S16`: 5. Restart the server.

   to get a key results in a null pointer exception. To the
   caller this wrapped up exception shows up as an IO Exception.

   web service and web service operation nodes, if they exist use
   them to fetch the workclasses and perform further request
   classification as necessary, otherwise, use the original
   request mapping to route request.

## techqa_DEV_Q126#row-0066

Question:
Why is WebSphere MQ connection failing when enabling SSL with AMQ9640 SSLPEER peer name error? Why is WebSphere MQ connection failing when enabling SSL with AMQ9640 SSLPEER peer name error?
example client side error:com.ibm.mq.jmqi.JmqiException: CC=2;RC=2399;
 
AMQ9640: SSL invalid peer name, channel '?',
 
attribute 'OID.0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.3 (x2)'.

Reference / gold answer:
The WebSphere MQ connection is failing when enabling SSL with the AMQ9640 SSLPEER peer name error because there is a discrepancy in how the SSL peer name information is handled. The distinguished name (DN) of the certificate is being set as the SSLPEERNAME property on the client side when establishing an SSL connection to a Queue Manager. However, this results in an error since the SSLPEERNAME property is not matching the expected value. This error is likely causing the SSL handshake to fail, resulting in the connection error mentioned (CC=2;RC=2399; AMQ9640: SSL invalid peer name).

To resolve this issue, the WebSphere MQ Classes for JMS have been updated to not set the SSLPEERNAME property from the distinguished name of the certificate during the JMS Session connect, thus preventing the mismatch error and enabling a successful SSL connection.

Reference evidence:
- `3g`: This fails with a
- `3h`:    JMSException, with reason code MQRC_SSL_PEER_NAME_ERROR.
- `3i`:    The exception is similar to:
- `3l`:    peer name, channel '?
- `3m`: ', attribute 'DC (x2)'. [5=DC (x2)]

=== CANDIDATE A ===

Model-visible evidence:
- `E1.S1`: 720limitation; MQ; CERTLABL; 2539; 0x000009eb; MQRC_CHANNEL_CONFIG_ERROR TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E1.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 After setting CERTLABL for an SSL channel on MQ Server, DataPower can no longer connect to that channel.
- `E1.S3`: SYMPTOM
When CERTLABL is configured on the channel that DataPower is using to connect to queue manager, the connection would fail and DataPower MQ Queue Manager object would be down.
- `E1.S4`: The following errors will be seen in the DataPower logs:
- `E1.S5`: * [mq][error] mq-qm(mqqm): tid(238161): test connection failed (2539) 
   [mq][error] mq-qm(mqqm): tid(238161): Queue Manager Error: 'mq-server.ibm.com:1111' ''. Reason code - 2539 
   The reason code is: 2539 0x000009eb MQRC_CHANNEL_CONFIG_ERROR
- `E1.S6`: On MQ Server, there will be error logs explaining this connection failure:  * 
 * 
 *
- `E1.S7`: * 
 * The SSL or TLS channel 'SSL.SVRCONN.2' is configured to use certificate label 
   'SSL.SVRCONN.2'. However, the remote peer did not send the necessary 
   information to allow the local channel to use the correct certificate. The 
   remote host is 'datapower (xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx)'.
- `E1.S8`: * This error occurs when the local channel definition has a certificate label and 
   the remote peer does not support selection of certificates. 
   The channel did not start.
- `E1.S9`: * 
 * Ensure that the remote peer supports certificate label configuration. Refer to 
   the Security section of the WebSphere MQ Information Center for details of 
   certificate label requirements. Alternatively, alter the local channel 
   definition so that it does not specify a certificate label.
- `E1.S10`: CAUSE
MQ version 8 and the later version provides a new parameter "CERTLABL" for administrators to specify a certificate to be used when making a SSL connection to a channel. This allows multiple certificates to be configured, one for each channel. All certificates are managed in the same queue manager on MQ Server. In order to utilize this function, both ends of the channel must be running MQ version 8 or the later version and must support Server Name Indication (SNI). 
Although DataPower version 7.2.0 runs MQ version 8 client and also supports SNI for the rest of the services, it does not support SNI for MQ Queue Manager object.
- `E1.S11`: ENVIRONMENT
MQ Server version 8, DataPower version 7.2.0
- `E1.S12`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
In order for DataPower to connect to the queue manager, the CERTLABL must be removed from the channel, which means you must not configure the CERTLABL on the MQ Server. After removing the CERTLABL from the channel, the channel would use the default certificate as configured in queue manager's properties.
- `E1.S13`: RELATED INFORMATION
 IBM MQ V8 Features and Enhancements [http://www.redbooks.ibm.com/redbooks/pdfs/sg248218.pdf]
- `E2.S1`: SUBSCRIBE
You can track all active APARs for this component.

- `E2.S11`: - WebSphere MQ v7.5 classes for JMS

 *  ****************************************************************

   migrate certificates using keys over a certain size.
- `E3.S8`: Platforms affected:
   Windows
- `E3.S9`: ****************************************************************
   PROBLEM SUMMARY:
   WMQ 6.0.2.1 for Windows uses a Java runtime environment to run
   the GSkit SSL certificate administration commands (amqtcert,
   runmqckm/gsk7cmd). The Java runtime has some JCE policy files
   which control what strength of cryptography is permitted for use
   with GSkit administration commands.
- `E3.S10`: 6.0.2.1 erroneously shipped an incorrect set of JCE policy
   files. Instead of shipping the unlimited strength files (as with
   previous fixpacks), only the standard files were shipped. This
   prevents certain certificates with large keys from being
   imported or migrated.
- `E3.S11`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  WMQ for Windows has been changed such that the correct policy
   files will be shipped in future fixpacks. Meanwhile, 6.0.2.1
   users affected by this issue may use the following work-around:
- `E3.S12`: 1. Download the unrestricted Java policy files (or obtain
   them from a WMQ 6 version before 6.0.2.1). The relevant files
   are local_policy.jar and US_export_policy.jar and they are
   installed by default in C:\Program Files\IBM\WebSphere
   MQ\gskit\jre\lib\security
- `E3.S13`: 2. Replace the two 6.0.2.1 gskit\jre\lib\security policy
   files with the unrestricted ones obtained in step 1.
- `E3.S14`: The certificate administration command will then work the same
   as in previous versions.

   classes for JMS, and the WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 Resource Adapter,

   classes for JMS, and the WebSphere MQ Resource Adapter,to
   specify:
- `E4.S30`: 00000000
- `E4.S31`: as the version number being used.

- `E4.S34`: within the MANIFEST.MF file contained within the JAR file:
- `E4.S35`: com.ibm.mq.jmqi.jar

   manager.
- `E4.S37`: Applications using the WebSphere MQ Resource Adapter or Java
   and JMS clients which have this APAR applied will report
   their version information correctly to the queue manager,
   which will be reflected in the information returned by

- `E5.S1`: 2035; JMS; java; MQRC_NOT_AUTHORIZED; client application; upgrade TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E5.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 You upgrade from WebSphere MQ V5.3 to V6 or V7 on the box where your client application is running. Now the client application fails with a reason code of 2035 (MQRC_NOT_AUTHORIZED).
- `E5.S3`: However, you have a client application that uses the WebSphere MQ V5.3 classes for Java™ or JMS and it is working as expected.
- `E5.S4`: SYMPTOM
MQRC 2035 2035 MQRC_NOT_AUTHORIZED
- `E5.S5`: CAUSE
Starting with MQ V6, changes were done to the MQ JMS client code to provide to the MQ server the userid of the process (application) that is connecting to the MQ server using the MQ JMS client.
- `E5.S6`: In this case, the MQ queue manager has received a username which either:
- `E5.S7`: * Does not exist in the host of the MQ queue manager. 
 * Does exist, but it does not have the proper authority to access the MQ queue manager.
- `E5.S8`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
Trace the failure to find the userid that is being sent by the MQ client to the MQ queue manager, it is necessary to capture the concurrent trace. This section provides more details.
- `E5.S9`: From the JMS Trace (trace.log) you can see the userid that is sent by the MQ Client
- `E5.S10`: For example, the trace.log for the JMS client may have strings such as these:
- `E5.S11`: com.ibm.mq.jms.MQQueueConnectionFactory connecting as user: JohnDoe
com.ibm.mq.jms.MQQueueConnection Setting username = JohnDoe
com.ibm.mq.MQv6InternalCommunications userID = 'JohnDoe '
com.ibm.mq.MQv6InternalCommunications UID :JOHNDOE
- `E5.S12`: From the MQ server trace you can see the userid that is received by the queue manager
- `E5.S13`: It is very likely that one of the MQ trace files (*.FMT) will have the following string indicating that the value (username) is not a user ID in the system (unknown principal). Search for the string: UnknownPrincipal
- `E5.S14`: UnknownPrincipal(johndoe)
- `E5.S15`: Also, in case that the userid does exist, another possible cause is that the user does not have all the proper authorizations, thus, check for the following phrase in the trace:
- `E5.S16`: The following requested permissions are unauthorized
- `E5.S17`: Obtaining traces:
- `E5.S18`: For information on how to gather the traces:
- `E5.S19`: MQ: WebSphere MQ Queue Manager Trace (Example for Linux)
http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?&uid=swg21174924#UNIXlt [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?&uid=swg21174924#UNIXlt]
- `E5.S20`: WAS JMS: Enabling JMS trace for releases of WebSphere Application Server V5.1, V6.0, V6.1, and V7.0
http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?&uid=swg21199176 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?&uid=swg21199176]
- `E5.S21`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Check which user ID the application is being run under and then check to see if that user ID either is in the "mqm" group (if the user is going to be an MQ Administrator) or in some other group with sufficient authority.
- `E5.S22`: After adding the userid to the group with sufficient authority, issue a runmqsc command:
REFRESH SECURITY(*)
- `E5.S23`: The user ID associated with the program when it runs must have authority to access certain resources of the queue manager. Grant the following authorities to the user ID:
- `E5.S24`: * The authority to connect to the queue manager, and the authority to inquire on the attributes of the queue manager object. 
 * The authority to put and get messages on the desired queue.
- `E5.S25`: For information about how to grant authorities, see the following

Model-visible evidence:
- `E1.S1`: 720limitation; MQ; CERTLABL; 2539; 0x000009eb; MQRC_CHANNEL_CONFIG_ERROR TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E1.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 After setting CERTLABL for an SSL channel on MQ Server, DataPower can no longer connect to that channel.
- `E1.S3`: SYMPTOM
When CERTLABL is configured on the channel that DataPower is using to connect to queue manager, the connection would fail and DataPower MQ Queue Manager object would be down.
- `E1.S4`: The following errors will be seen in the DataPower logs:
- `E1.S5`: * [mq][error] mq-qm(mqqm): tid(238161): test connection failed (2539) 
   [mq][error] mq-qm(mqqm): tid(238161): Queue Manager Error: 'mq-server.ibm.com:1111' ''. Reason code - 2539 
   The reason code is: 2539 0x000009eb MQRC_CHANNEL_CONFIG_ERROR
- `E1.S6`: On MQ Server, there will be error logs explaining this connection failure:  * 
 * 
 *
- `E1.S7`: * 
 * The SSL or TLS channel 'SSL.SVRCONN.2' is configured to use certificate label 
   'SSL.SVRCONN.2'. However, the remote peer did not send the necessary 
   information to allow the local channel to use the correct certificate. The 
   remote host is 'datapower (xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx)'.
- `E1.S8`: * This error occurs when the local channel definition has a certificate label and 
   the remote peer does not support selection of certificates. 
   The channel did not start.
- `E1.S9`: * 
 * Ensure that the remote peer supports certificate label configuration. Refer to 
   the Security section of the WebSphere MQ Information Center for details of 
   certificate label requirements. Alternatively, alter the local channel 
   definition so that it does not specify a certificate label.
- `E1.S10`: CAUSE
MQ version 8 and the later version provides a new parameter "CERTLABL" for administrators to specify a certificate to be used when making a SSL connection to a channel. This allows multiple certificates to be configured, one for each channel. All certificates are managed in the same queue manager on MQ Server. In order to utilize this function, both ends of the channel must be running MQ version 8 or the later version and must support Server Name Indication (SNI). 
Although DataPower version 7.2.0 runs MQ version 8 client and also supports SNI for the rest of the services, it does not support SNI for MQ Queue Manager object.
- `E1.S11`: ENVIRONMENT
MQ Server version 8, DataPower version 7.2.0
- `E1.S12`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
In order for DataPower to connect to the queue manager, the CERTLABL must be removed from the channel, which means you must not configure the CERTLABL on the MQ Server. After removing the CERTLABL from the channel, the channel would use the default certificate as configured in queue manager's properties.
- `E1.S13`: RELATED INFORMATION
 IBM MQ V8 Features and Enhancements [http://www.redbooks.ibm.com/redbooks/pdfs/sg248218.pdf]

 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
- `E4.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS V7.0.1.5 (or later): Failure
   Data Capture (FDC) files
   with Probe
   ID JO076001 and JO205001 are generated following a remote
   connection to a Queue Manager that has conversation sharing
   disabled:
- `E4.S5`: | Probe Id     :- JO076001
   | Component    :- RemoteFAP.MQOPEN(Hconn,MQOD,int,Phobj,Pi
   | Probe Type   :- INCORROUT
   | Comment1     :- MQOPEN reply expected
- `E4.S6`: | Probe Id     :- JO205001
   | Component    :- RemoteConnection.removeHconn(RemoteTls,R
   | Probe Type   :- INCORROUT
   | Comment1     :- Hconn is not associated with this connection
- `E4.S7`: LOCAL FIX
- `E4.S8`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   USERS AFFECTED:
   This issue affects users of the WebSphere MQ V7.0.1.5 Classes
   for Java/JMS (or later) who have established a remote connection
   to a Queue Manager via a channel that has Conversation Sharing
   disabled (SHARECNV=0 or SHARECNV=1).
- `E4.S9`: This includes users of:
- `E4.S10`: - The WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 Classes for JMS
   - The WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 Resource Adapter.
   - The WebSphere Application Server V7.0 and V8.0 WebSphere MQ
   messaging provider.
   - The WebSphere Application Server V6.1 WebSphere MQ messaging
   provider who have configured the WebSphere variable
   MQ_INSTALL_ROOT to point to a WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 installation.
- `E4.S11`: Platforms affected:
   All Distributed (iSeries, all Unix and Windows)
   ****************************************************************
   PROBLEM SUMMARY:
   By default in the WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS,
   conversation
   sharing is enabled and set to 10 on the client side. The client
   only discovers that Conversation Sharing is disabled following
   negotiation with a Queue Manager on the completion of a
   connection over a Channel that has SHARECNV=0 or SHARECNV=1.
- `E4.S12`: When a WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS application requests a
   remote connection to a Queue Manager the client first attempts
   to find an already established TCP/IP connection which can be
   shared. As part of this process the list of known TCP/IP
   connections are matched for their suitability, this list
   includes connections which are in the process of being
   established (MQCONN reply not received from the Queue Manager).
- `E4.S13`: When a WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS application requested a
   remote connection it was matched for sharing with a connection
   that was still in the process of being established. The
   WebSphere MQ Client waited for the connection to complete and
   due to a small timing window began incorrectly sharing the
   connection without confirming the connection's suitability. If
   the connection's suitability had been checked then the
   connection
   would have been marked unsuitable due to the Negotiated Channel
   specifying that Conversation Sharing was disabled (SHARECNV=0 or
   SHARECNV=1).
   As the connection (which did not support conversation sharing)
   was now shared by two threads, packets destined for one thread
   were erroneously received by the other, this led to the client
   being in an inconsistent state and the two FDCs being generated.
- `E4.S14`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  The WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS have been modified to
   correctly restrict conversation sharing when using a connection
   that does not support conversation sharing (SHARECNV=0 or
   SHARECNV=1).
- `E4.S15`: ---------------------------------------------------------------
   The fix is targeted for

- `E5.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  Customers using runmqckm or amqtcert on Windows systems may
   find that they are unable to migrate or import some SSL
   certificates when WMQ 6.0.2.1 is installed.
- `E5.S5`: The most likely error message is "the specified database has
   been corrupted", for a certificate which can be imported
   using a version of WMQ prior to 6.0.2.1.
- `E5.S6`: LOCAL FIX
- `E5.S7`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   USERS AFFECTED:
   Customers using WMQ 6.0.2.1 for Windows who need to import or
   migrate certificates using keys over a certain size.
- `E5.S8`: Platforms affected:
   Windows
- `E5.S9`: ****************************************************************
   PROBLEM SUMMARY:
   WMQ 6.0.2.1 for Windows uses a Java runtime environment to run
   the GSkit SSL certificate administration commands (amqtcert,
   runmqckm/gsk7cmd). The Java runtime has some JCE policy files
   which control what strength of cryptography is permitted for use
   with GSkit administration commands.
- `E5.S10`: 6.0.2.1 erroneously shipped an incorrect set of JCE policy
   files. Instead of shipping the unlimited strength files (as with
   previous fixpacks), only the standard files were shipped. This
   prevents certain certificates with large keys from being
   imported or migrated.
- `E5.S11`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  WMQ for Windows has been changed such that the correct policy
   files will be shipped in future fixpacks. Meanwhile, 6.0.2.1
   users affected by this issue may use the following work-around:
- `E5.S12`: 1. Download the unrestricted Java policy files (or obtain
   them from a WMQ 6 version before 6.0.2.1). The relevant files
   are local_policy.jar and US_export_policy.jar and they are
   installed by default in C:\Program Files\IBM\WebSphere
   MQ\gskit\jre\lib\security
- `E5.S13`: 2. Replace the two 6.0.2.1 gskit\jre\lib\security policy
   files with the unrestricted ones obtained in step 1.
- `E5.S14`: The certificate administration command will then work the same
   as in previous versions.

## techqa_DEV_Q112#row-0100

Question:
Why does nco_confpack -export fail with the message "Tool in menu but not found"? I tried to export OMNIbus configuration using nco_confpack command and I get the following message:
Tool in menu but not found, menu: AlertsMenu, tool: Close
I've also tried using it with -list command and I get the same error. 

Reference / gold answer:
The nco_confpack -export command fails with the message "Tool in menu but not found" because the menu AlertsMenu has a tool in it called "Close," however, the tool no longer exists. To resolve this issue, you would need to recreate the tool and associate it with the menu to successfully run the nco_confpack command for exporting the OMNIbus configuration.

Reference evidence:
- `4b`:  Migrating to a new version of Omnibus, running nco_confpack:
- `4e`: The command fails and the following error is received: Tool in menu but not found, menu: AlertsMenu, tool: CLEAR_LWY. CAUSE
- `4f`: The menu AlertsMenu has a tool in it called CLEAR_LWY, however the tool no longer exists.
- `4g`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM

=== CANDIDATE A ===

- `E3.S1`: Pub Sub; Publish Subscribe; JMS; MustGather; MustGathers; Must Gather; Collect Troubleshooting Data; MustGatherDocument; Collecting; Trouble; Shooting TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 You are designing an application solution with WebSphere Message Broker (WMB) and IBM Integration Bus (IIB) and are having problems with JMS.
- `E3.S3`: This MustGather document explains how to troubleshoot this problem by yourself, how to generate diagnostic data when the problem is happening, how to collect the available data from your system, and how to share that data with IBM support.
- `E3.S4`: ENVIRONMENT
These instructions are for WebSphere Message Broker or IBM Integration Bus on Windows systems.
Return to the WMB / IIB MustGather index [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21209857] for other systems.
- `E3.S5`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
- `E3.S6`: STEP 1: SELF-GUIDED TROUBLESHOOTING
- `E3.S7`: 1. Consider Using the Test Client in trace and debug mode [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSKM8N_8.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/af52260_.htm].
 2. 
 3. A user level trace [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=849&uid=swg21177321#1] is intended to assist users with understanding how their ESQL is processed.
    It will also show a high level view of the message flow behavior.
 4. 
 5. Check for known issues:
    Troubleshooting JMS nodes [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSMKHH_9.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/ac24877_.htm]
    developerWorks Forums: WebSphere Message Broker: JMS [https://www.ibm.com/developerworks/community/forums/html/forum?id=11111111-0000-0000-0000-000000000281&query=jms]
    WebSphere Message Broker support site [http://www.ibm.com/support/entry/portal/Overview/Software/WebSphere/WebSphere_Message_Broker]
- `E3.S8`: STEP 2: COLLECT DATA
- `E3.S9`: 1. mqsidc See: mqsidc usage instructions [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSKM8N_8.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/bu46012_.htm]
- `E3.S10`: * When running the tool, select the option for 'Broker Collector', when prompted.
- `E3.S11`: 2. 
 3. JMS details
    Export a current view of your JMS configuration with these items:  * mqsireportproperties <broker> -c JMSProviders -o <JMSProvider> -r
     * the contents of the jarsURL directory
     * the JNDI bindings file
- `E3.S12`: 4. 
 5. Project Interchange files for the problematic flow/set/ESQL/model
     * You can export your Message Flow and Message Set project(s) into an archive file for easy transmission to IBM Support.
       See: Exporting your message flow projects from the Toolkit [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21418121]
- `E3.S13`: 6. 
 7. Traces If the problem occurs during a runtime test or with the Toolkit test facility, WMB execution group traces [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=849&uid=swg21177321] can be used to gain a better understanding of the problem.  * A user level trace [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=849&uid=swg21177321#1] is intended to assist users with understanding how their ESQL is processed. It will also show a high level view of the message flow behavior.
     * A service level trace [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=849&uid=swg21177321#2] is intended to be provided to IBM Support to assist in the diagnosis of your issue.
- `E3.S14`: 8. 
 9. General Broker information
    If the mqsidc tool was not run, then capture this information manually  * Record the WebSphere Message Broker version, release, and maintenance level.
       This can be captured using the command 'mqsiservice -v'.
     * Record the operating system version, release, and maintenance level.
     * Record the version, release, and maintenance level of any related products and components for the problematic application.
     * Collect the local error log.
       On Window systems, the local error log is the Windows Application Event Log.
       You can find the Event Viewer from the Windows Control Panel.
       See: Event viewer logs [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=849&uid=swg21295454]
     * Collect the Standard Output/Error logs.
       On Window systems, WMB writes information to a 'console.out' file.
       This file is located under the Message Broker workpath.
       See: Standard System Logs [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSMKHH_9.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/au14165_.htm]
- `E3.S15`: ATTENTION: A good problem description is one of the most important tools IBM needs to analyze your data!
- `E3.S16`: You can find the Event Viewer from the Windows Control Panel.
       See: Event viewer logs [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=849&uid=swg21295454]
     * Collect the Standard Output/Error logs.
       On Window systems, WMB writes information to a 'console.out' file.

       See: Standard System Logs [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSMKHH_9.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/au14165_.htm]
- `E3.S17`: ATTENTION: A good problem description is one of the most important tools IBM needs to analyze your data!
When sending data to IBM, be sure to update your PMR or send a note with the following information:

- `E3.S1`: ABENDs - Dumps TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E3.S2`: QUESTION
 Why am I receiving ABEND AKEA in IODM module EKCCMTOM at offset x'1A68' when trying to run in a CICS Version 3.3.0 region? The error occurs shortly after restarting IODM without the cycling region.
- `E3.S3`: In the CICS system initialization table (SIT), STGPROT is set to "No" and RENTPGM is set to NOPROTECT. System modifications (sysmods), UN54096 and UN60897, have been applied.
- `E3.S4`: ANSWER
Refer to authorized program analysis report (APAR) PN56650 for information about IODM module EKCCMTOM and program DFHZNEP. Set both programs to the EXECKEY parameter of CICS® and give them a datalocation value of "Any." Also, change the queue status field (QUESTAT) of the IDPARMTB table from 'E' to 'D'. The IDPARMTB table defines system-wide Object Distribution Manager parameters vital to the system's operation. Making this change frees you from relying on the use of the send queue processing operator commands, OAQM and OAQC, that are between OID1 and OID2. OID1 is the ImagePlus Object Distribution Manager first-stage, and OID2 the second-stage, shutdown CICS transaction. OID2 completes the Object Distribution Manager shutdown.
- `E3.S5`: The mode settings for program DFHZNEP state that DFHZNEP must be RMODE=any, AMODE=31. Relink your DFHZNEP as 31 bit so that DFHZNAC can link to ZNEP.
- `E3.S6`: When you relink DFHZNEP as 31 bit, expect to receive error message: IEW2646 for modules DFHZNEP, EKCCVECT, and EKCCFMSG. Error message: IEW2646I is issued when an RMODE value that is specified in the PARM statement is different than the one in the electrostatic discharge (ESD) record. Included is a binder message, which warns of a conflict. As a result, the RMODE value in the PARM statement will be used, based on the hierarchy specified in the Program Management Manual.
- `E3.S7`: You might get intermittent failures in OID1 in IODM module EKCCMTOM. Continue to try the failing transaction until you receive a normal completion.
- `E3.S8`: Another element to this error was revealed during its testing. The abend appears after cycling ODM but without cycling the CICS region. For example, you might first start the CICS region, then OIUP, OID1, OID2, OIUP, OID1 (which fails), OID2 (which also fails). By cycling the CICS region, the first OID1 and OID2 will function normally.
- `E3.S9`: In this situation, the second OIUP, which initializes the Object Distribution Manager, and all other functions (DISP and so on), function without incident.
- `E3.S10`: * If you use the LMODs from EKCPSTLK with the CICS330 libraries (instead of with the CICS211 libraries), OID1 and OID2 fail after the first shutdown of ODM. 
 * If you cycle the whole region, OID1 and OID2 work the first time after an OIUP. 
 * If you bring ODM up and then try to shut it down again, you will get the abends. 
 * With the CICS330 links, the failure is consistent. 
 * With the CICS211 links, the failure is intermittent. 
 * Additionally, with the CICS330 modules: 
 * DFHECI links clean 
 * error message: IEW2646I is not produced 
 * the offset of the abend moves about 8 bytes
- `E3.S11`: Note: The error described in this document was accompanied by error message: EKC0304A return code 8 reason code 00070017 after restarting IODM without a cycling region.
- `E3.S12`: * With the CICS330 links, the failure is consistent. 
 * With the CICS211 links, the failure is intermittent. 
 * Additionally, with the CICS330 modules: 
 * DFHECI links clean 
 * error message: IEW2646I is not produced 
 * the offset of the abend moves about 8 bytes
- `E3.S13`: Note: The error described in this document was accompanied by error message: EKC0304A return code 8 reason code 00070017 after restarting IODM without a cycling region. If you have an earlier release of IODM, see APAR PN14003 regarding the error message: EKC0304A 00070017.
- `E3.S14`: HISTORICAL NUMBER
 APAR PN56650

- `E5.S1`: nco_g_jdbc; manageIU; RootIU; UUID TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E5.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 After uninstalling JDBC Gateway using uninstall command from $NCHOME/_uninst/nco_g_jdbc, the reinstallation is failing with a message that features already exist on the system.
- `E5.S3`: SYMPTOM
"No new features to install" window is displayed with message "You haven't selected any new features to install as the selected features already exist on the system."
- `E5.S4`: CAUSE
The output of listIU is still showing the JDBC Gateway as installed.
- `E5.S5`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
1. Back up existing DE by zipping/tarring the entire DE directory
- `E5.S6`: e.g. for root install, tar up "/usr/ibm/common/acsi" directory and keep it in another location. Alternatively, use de_backupdb.sh script to create the backup.
- `E5.S7`: 2. Run de_lsrootiu.sh script and review the output to determine the discriminant information.
- `E5.S8`: e.g. <discriminant>/opt/IBM/tivoli/netcool</discriminant>
- `E5.S9`: The discriminant would be /opt/IBM/tivoli/netcool
- `E5.S10`: 3. Run listIU.cmd or listIU.sh and in the output look for a line which has "RootIU UUID:" and the component name and version
- `E5.S11`: e.g. IU RootIU UUID: 060A90E184C84B7A98E25EC426B44288 Name: gateway-nco-g-jdbc Version: 1.5.1.0
- `E5.S12`: 4. Remove the uninstalled component from the listIU, by running
- `E5.S13`: manageIU.sh -o delete -r <discriminant> -d RootIUTypeID ,
- `E5.S14`: Based on the example above, for root install with discriminant of "/opt/IBM/tivoli/netcool" the command to run would be: 
/usr/ibm/common/acsi/bin/manageIU.sh -o delete -r /opt/IBM/tivoli/netcool -d RootIUTypeID[060A90E184C84B7A98E25EC426B44288, 1.5.1.0]
- `E5.S15`: 5. Run listIU.sh again and make sure that JDBC gateway is no longer listed.
- `E5.S16`: The reinstallation of JDBC gateway should now work. If the problem with reinstallation persists, please contact IBM Support.
- `E5.S17`: PRODUCT ALIAS/SYNONYM
 OMNIbus gateway

## techqa_DEV_Q277#row-0042

Question:
Is transient user support available for SAML integration with WebSphere Portal 8.0? I am looking to leverage the SAML TAI provided by WebSphere Application Server for my WebSphere Portal 8.0 environment. Is transient user support available so that I do not have to maintain a local account in my Portal user registry for every external user which is verified and trusted by my identity provider? 

Reference / gold answer:
Yes, transient user support for SAML integration is available for WebSphere Portal starting with Cumulative Fix (CF) #8 for version 8.5. However, there are no plans to backport this functionality to Portal 7.0 or Portal 8.0.

Reference evidence:
- `0r`: Transient user support [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSHRKX_8.5.0/mp/overview/new_cf08.dita?lang=en] has been introduced for SAML TAI [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSHRKX_8.5.0/mp/wcm/wcm_secure_int_tai_auth.dita?lang=en] starting with Cumulative Fix (CF) #8 for 8.5.
- `0s`: Refer to the WebSphere Portal Security blog [https://www.ibm.com/developerworks/community/blogs/8f2bc166-3bdc-4a9d-bad4-3620dbb3e46c/entry/portal_transient_user_support_with_was_saml_tai_business_case_clarification?lang=en] for more details regarding the business case and implementation details.

=== CANDIDATE A ===

- `E4.S1`: SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E4.S2`: SUMMARY
 There is a potential bypass security restriction vulnerability in IBM WebSphere Application Server. This will only occur in environments that have the webcontainer custom property HttpSessionIdReuse enabled. There is a potential denial of service with IBM WebSphere Application Server when using SIP services. IBM WebSphere Application Server Liberty could allow a remote attacker to conduct phishing attacks, caused by an open redirect vulnerability. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to redirect a victim to arbitrary Web sites. IBM WebSphere Application Server Liberty is vulnerable to cross-site scripting in OpenID Connect clients caused by improper validation of input. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability using a specially-crafted URL to execute script in a victim's Web browser within the security context of the hosting Web site, once the URL is clicked. An attacker could use this vulnerability to steal the victim's cookie-based authentication credentials. There is an Information Disclosure Vulnerability in IBM WebSphere Application Server Liberty. Apache Commons Fileupload vulnerability affects WebSphere Application Server. There is a potential information disclosure in WebSphere Application Server.

- `E1.S2`: QUESTION
 What is changing in the Infosphere Information Server support experience?
- `E1.S3`: CAUSE
We are always striving to seek new and better ways to improve our communications and the support we offer. With that in mind, we’re excited to announce we’re launching a new Support Community/Experience for a select number of IBM products, Information Server will be one of these products going live with this new technology in the coming weeks.
- `E1.S4`: ANSWER
Our new community will provide you enhance transparency into your ticket resolution workflow along with improved self-service options. You can see a quick video overview of the initial experience here: https://mediacenter.ibm.com/media/t/1_hjcvgybl [https://mediacenter.ibm.com/media/t/1_hjcvgybl]
- `E1.S5`: The move to this new support experience should be seamless for you. Specifically:
· Your bookmarks and existing access methods will automatically connect to the new Support Community once you’ve selected Information Server as a product.
· The same URLs you currently use will continue to work, or you can use a new URL to reach the new Support experience directly: https://www.ibm.com/mysupport [https://www.ibm.com/mysupport]
· Any existing PMRs will be automatically converted to “Cases” in the new tool. Simply choose “cases” from the Information Server support landing page to see status or make updates
- `E1.S6`: We know you may have other IBM products and those too will be migrating to this new experience over time. Please note that you may receive other communications notifying you of the plans for other IBM products. Your experience with Information Server support will continue to evolve as well. Among other improvements, we’re incorporating IBM Watson technology, and providing a truly “one-stop shop” for Customer Support related information for Information Server.
- `E1.S7`: You will know Information Server has migrated once it appears in the product selection area on the new Support Community. 
To access the Community: 
1) Go to www.ibm.com/mysupport [http://www.ibm.com/mysupport%5Ch] , where you can select your product.
2) For a personalized experience, you can login with your IBM ID. 
If you do not have an IBM ID, go here to sign up for one https://www.ibm.com/account/us-en/signup/register.html [https://www.ibm.com/account/us-en/signup/register.html%5Ch]. 
Note: You can also start in the legacy Service Request Tool (https://www-947.ibm.com/support/servicerequest/ [https://www-947.ibm.com/support/servicerequest/]), which will automatically redirected to the new experience.
- `E1.S8`: If you are experiencing a problem with the portal (such as a login issue, etc.), we are here to help. You can submit your issue via our Support Community [https://www.ibm.com/mysupport/s/] by clicking “Email IBM Support”, or emailing spe@us.ibm.com [spe@us.ibm.com] and we will get back to you as quickly as possible.

- `E2.S1`: ClearCase; ALBD; 1296744 TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E2.S2`: QUESTION
 Is it possible to use two different IBM® Rational® ClearCase® privileged user (clearcase_albd) accounts for accessing the VOB server?
- `E2.S3`: CAUSE
- `E2.S4`: You want to use two different albd accounts for accessing your VOB server.
- `E2.S5`: You want to change the albd account and during the transition phase there will be two accounts present.
- `E2.S6`: Review the ClearCase Administrators Guide on the topic of The Rational ClearCase server process user [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/cchelp/v7r0m1/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.rational.clearcase.cc_admin.doc/topics/c_access_usr_grp_privileged_ccspu.htm]for more information about this account.
- `E2.S7`: ANSWER
- `E2.S8`: Yes this is possible.
- `E2.S9`: When using multiple ALBD user accounts, the key consideration is that the accounts need to be as close to identical as possible as described below.
- `E2.S10`: Key Considerations
- `E2.S11`: * If the VOBs are on a UNIX®/Linux® server, then the Microsoft® Windows® albd accounts need to map over to the same VOB-owner account that is using Samba or TAS. If for some reason this is not possible, see Note 3 below.
- `E2.S12`: Review the ClearCase Administrators Guide on the topic of Mapping the Rational ClearCase server process user [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/cchelp/v7r0m1/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.rational.clearcase.cc_admin.doc/topics/t_pcnfssmb_smb_samba_mapccspu.htm] for more information.
- `E2.S13`: * The albd accounts must be members of the same groups. Especially the "ClearCase Server Process Group," also known as the "ClearCase" or "ClearCase Administrators' group."
- `E2.S14`: Two common use cases for multiple albd accounts 
 1. Security policies require ALL accounts to change their passwords every "n" days, including service accounts.
- `E2.S15`: In this case, the albd account is "rotated" every "n-7" days from a workstation logged in with domain administration rights. This can be done using a simple script.

IBM is providing the Program on an "AS IS" basis without warranty of any kind. - `E2.S20`: Note 2: This script makes no allowance for machines that are not currently active. A "production-ready" script would include the ability to account for this and also keep track of which ClearCase hosts have had their albd account "rotated" in order to avoid the problem. 
    Refer to the sc Windows on-line help for the "sc qc" command for more information on how to verify the account information for a service.
- `E2.S21`: Review the ClearCase Command Reference Guide on the topic of lsclients [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/cchelp/v7r0m1/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.rational.clearcase.cc_ref.doc/topics/ct_lsclients.htm](cleartool man lsclients) for more information.

- `E4.S1`: SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E4.S2`: SUMMARY
 There is a potential bypass security restriction vulnerability in IBM WebSphere Application Server. This will only occur in environments that have the webcontainer custom property HttpSessionIdReuse enabled. There is a potential denial of service with IBM WebSphere Application Server when using SIP services. IBM WebSphere Application Server Liberty could allow a remote attacker to conduct phishing attacks, caused by an open redirect vulnerability. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to redirect a victim to arbitrary Web sites. IBM WebSphere Application Server Liberty is vulnerable to cross-site scripting in OpenID Connect clients caused by improper validation of input. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability using a specially-crafted URL to execute script in a victim's Web browser within the security context of the hosting Web site, once the URL is clicked. An attacker could use this vulnerability to steal the victim's cookie-based authentication credentials. There is an Information Disclosure Vulnerability in IBM WebSphere Application Server Liberty. Apache Commons Fileupload vulnerability affects WebSphere Application Server. There is a potential information disclosure in WebSphere Application Server.

## techqa_DEV_Q157#row-0153

Question:
How do I configure TLS/SSL for an IIB web service provider and consumer? I'm investigating ways and technologies for use with IIB to run a web service that runs as both a provider and consumer. I'm looking at HTTP and SOAP messages/nodes. At a high level it might look like this:
HTTPInput (TLS over HTTPS) -> Compute -> HTTPRequest (SSL over HTTPS) -> Compute -> HTTPReply
or
SOAPInput (TLS over HTTPS) -> Compute -> SOAPRequest (SSL over HTTPS) -> Compute -> SOAPReply
Does anyone have more details/references beyond the knowledge center on how to configure the TLS/SSL portions?

Reference / gold answer:
Based on the provided context, you can configure TLS/SSL for an IIB web service provider and consumer by following these general steps:

1. Verify that you have a valid SSL certificate installed on your IIB server.
2. Ensure that the necessary components for TLS/SSL communications are properly configured in your IIB environment.
3. For HTTP services, configure the HTTPInput and HTTPRequest nodes to use TLS over HTTPS. For SOAP services, configure the SOAPInput and SOAPRequest nodes to use TLS over HTTPS.
4. Update the Compute nodes in your message flow to handle any necessary data transformations or processing.
5. Ensure that the URL endpoints in your HTTP or SOAP requests are using HTTPS protocol.
6. Make sure that the security settings for TLS/SSL are correctly set for both the provider and consumer sides of your web service.
7. Optionally, follow best practices for securing communications, such as using strong encryption algorithms and ensuring certificate validation.

For detailed configuration steps specific to IIB and TLS/SSL, you can refer to the IBM Knowledge Center documentation for IBM Integration Bus (IIB) or consult with IBM support for more in-depth assistance. Additionally, you may also find relevant information in security bulletins related to SSL/TLS vulnerabilities and remediation steps provided by IBM.

- `E3.S1`: SSL ; TLS/SSL; TLS 1.0; TLS 1.1; BEAST; Vulnerability; CVE-2011-3389 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING) PROBLEM(ABSTRACT) A known SSL/TLS vulnerability, CVE-2011-3389 (also known as BEAST), exists in the SSLv3 and TLS 1.0 protocols. To eliminate this vulnerability, please review the specific configuration recommendations below. SYMPTOM Refer to CVE-2011-3389 RESOLVING THE PROBLEM The following describes how to prevent the CVE-2011-3389 vulnerability on any firmware version of the IBM WebSphere DataPower appliance. The protocol problem in this case is the use of a predictable IV (initialization vector) when block cipher CBC mode is used. There are two ways to prevent the attack. 1. use TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 The protocol problem that allows the attack was fixed completely starting in TLS 1.1 which changed the spec to use a new, random IV in each encrypted SSL record. DataPower firmware release 6.0.0 added support for TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 by default. To protect the appliance against the vulnerability enable support for TLS 1.1 and TLS 1.2 in the Crypto Profile while disabling support for TLS 1.0, SSLv3, and SSLv2. DataPower firmware releases prior to 6.0.0 do not support TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 and therefore must use option #2 below to avoid the vulnerability. 2. Enable the empty data record counter measure (CLI only) This counter measure can only be enabled using the command line interface (it is not available in the WebGUI). This counter measure is to send empty data records between the usual data records to effectively randomize the IV value. This behavior is legal according to the SSL/TLS specifications, but some SSL/TLS stacks are not fully compliant to this specification and will reject connections that send such records. Therefore use of this setting may result in incompatibility with SSL/TLS stacks that are not standards compliant such as the one in some versions of Microsoft Internet Explorer (IE). The Crypto Profile has a property called Options. - `E4.S1`: TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E4.S2`: QUESTION
How do you replace an expired SSL certificate on the Sametime Gateway?
- `E4.S3`: SSL/TLS certificates are used on the Gateway to associate trust between external instant messaging services. These certificates have an expiration date when they no longer can provide the associated trust.
- `E4.S4`: ANSWER
The Sametime Gateway application uses the WebSphere Application Server Java keystores to maintain the SSL/TLS certificates. You have the following options when replacing the expired certificate:
- `E4.S5`: * Create a new certificate request 
 * Receive a renewed certificate request from your CA
- `E4.S6`: More information on each option is provided below.
- `E4.S7`: Create a new certificate request
- `E4.S8`: Create a new certificate request and apply that certificate by following the procedures in the Sametime product documentation:
- `E4.S9`: For a single server > Requesting a certificate signed by a Certificate Authority [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/sametime/v8r5/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.help.sametime.v85.doc/config/config_gw_ssl_request_cert.html]
- `E4.S10`: For a cluster server> Creating a certificate request [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/sametime/v8r5/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.help.sametime.v85.doc/config/config_gw_ssl_request_cert_clus.html]
- `E4.S11`: Receive a renewed certificate request from your CA
- `E4.S12`: You can receive a renewed certificate from your certificate authority (CA) without recreating the request by using these steps:
- `E4.S13`: 1.  Locate the keystore in use  1.  For a single server the keystore (key.p12 or STGWKS.p12) will be located in the following directory path:
- `E4.S14`: \WebSphere\Appserver\profiles\[RTCGWServer]\config\cells\[CellName]\nodes\[NodeName] 
     2. For a cluster the keystore (key.p12 or STGWKS.p12) will be located in the following directory path:
- `E4.S15`: \WebSphere\Appserver\profiles\[RTCGWServer]\config\cells\[CellName]\nodes\[SIP Proxy Node Name]
- `E4.S16`: 2. Load IBM Key Manager, iKeyman, by running the following script:
- `E4.S17`: \WebSphere\Appserver\bin\ikeyman.bat
- `E4.S18`: 3. Once loaded, click open, then change the keystore type to PKCS12, and browse to the keystore you located above. The default keystore password is "WebAS"; you will need to enter this password to open the keystore.
- `E4.S19`: 4. Once the keystore is opened within ikeyman, you can "receive" the renewed certificate that was delivered by your CA. This step can be achieved by selecting the "Receive" button and browsing to the renewed certificate on the file system.
- `E4.S20`: 5. Next confirm that you successfully received the renewed certificate by selecting "View Details" within ikeyman. This task shows you the validity of the certificate so that you can confirm that the expired certificate has been replaced with the renewed certificate.
- `E4.S21`: 6. Launch the Integrated Solutions Console for the Sametime Gateway server, and navigate to the SSL Configurations.
- `E4.S22`: Security -> SSL certificate and key management -> Manage Endpoint Security configurations  1. For a single server select the inbound node name (for example, STGWNode)
- `E4.S23`: For a cluster expand the ProxyNode and select the SIPProxyServer
- `E4.S24`: Screen capture of SIPProxyServer node:
        [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21442836&amp;aid=1] 
     2. You will be brought to "Specific SSL configurations for this endpoint." Do not change anything on this page; simply select "Update certificate aliases." This step loads the newly received certificate into memory. 
     3. Repeat this procedure on the outbound node on the Manage Endpoint Security configurations page.
- `E4.S25`: 7. Now your Sametime Gateway has been configured to use your renewed certificate. In some cases, it might be required to restart the environment.

- `E2.S1`: SSL ; TLS/SSL; TLS 1.0; TLS 1.1; BEAST; Vulnerability; CVE-2011-3389 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E2.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 A known SSL/TLS vulnerability, CVE-2011-3389 (also known as BEAST), exists in the SSLv3 and TLS 1.0 protocols. To eliminate this vulnerability, please review the specific configuration recommendations below.
- `E2.S3`: SYMPTOM
Refer to CVE-2011-3389
- `E2.S4`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
The following describes how to prevent the CVE-2011-3389 vulnerability on any firmware version of the IBM WebSphere DataPower appliance.
- `E2.S5`: The protocol problem in this case is the use of a predictable IV (initialization vector) when block cipher CBC mode is used. There are two ways to prevent the attack.
- `E2.S6`: 1. use TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2
- `E2.S7`: The protocol problem that allows the attack was fixed completely starting in TLS 1.1 which changed the spec to use a new, random IV in each encrypted SSL record.
- `E2.S8`: DataPower firmware release 6.0.0 added support for TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 by default. To protect the appliance against the vulnerability enable support for TLS 1.1 and TLS 1.2 in the Crypto Profile while disabling support for TLS 1.0, SSLv3, and SSLv2.
- `E2.S9`: DataPower firmware releases prior to 6.0.0 do not support TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 and therefore must use option #2 below to avoid the vulnerability.
- `E2.S10`: 2. Enable the empty data record counter measure (CLI only)
- `E2.S11`: This counter measure can only be enabled using the command line interface (it is not available in the WebGUI).
- `E2.S12`: This counter measure is to send empty data records between the usual data records to effectively randomize the IV value. This behavior is legal according to the SSL/TLS specifications, but some SSL/TLS stacks are not fully compliant to this specification and will reject connections that send such records. Therefore use of this setting may result in incompatibility with SSL/TLS stacks that are not standards compliant such as the one in some versions of Microsoft Internet Explorer (IE).
- `E2.S13`: The Crypto Profile has a property called Options. Using the command line interface, set the Options field by entering crypto mode and using the profile command with an options mask of 0x10007FF:
- `E2.S14`: profile name idCred [ssl name] [ciphers cipher-string] [options mask]
- `E2.S15`: For example, a Crypto Profile named "alice-cp" uses an Identification Credential named "alice-idcred". The following CLI commands will enable the empty data record counter measure for this Crypto Profile:
- `E2.S16`: top
configure terminal
crypto
profile alice-cp alice-idcred options 0x10007FF
- `E2.S17`: This counter measure only protects one half of the duplex (outgoing data from DataPower). It is up to the SSL peer to protect the other half of the duplex with the same counter measure. If this is undesirable then use #1 or #3 instead.
- `E2.S18`: 3. Use SSL Server Profile or SSL SNI Server Profile with firmware version 7.2.0 or later
- `E2.S19`: In 7.2.0 release, IBM DataPower Gateways introduced SSL Server Profile and SSL SNI Server Profile. These 2 profiles are not vulnerable to this advisory, as they will always send empty data records between the usual data records.
- `E2.S20`: Cross reference information Segment Product Component Platform Version Edition Business Integration WebSphere DataPower B2B Appliance XB60 4.0.2, 4.0.1,
- `E2.S21`: Gateways introduced SSL Server Profile and SSL SNI Server Profile. These 2 profiles are not vulnerable to this advisory, as they will always send empty data records between the usual data records.

 You are developing an application solution with WebSphere Message Broker (WMB) or IBM Integration Bus (IIB) and are having problems with the Global Cache feature.
- `E5.S3`: This MustGather document explains how to troubleshoot this problem by yourself, how to generate diagnostic data when the problem is happening, how to collect the available data from your system, and how to share that data with IBM support.
- `E5.S4`: ENVIRONMENT

Return to the WMB / IIB MustGather index [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21209857] for other systems.

- `E5.S7`: 1. Understand the problem that is occurring.  * Consider using the Test Client in trace and debug mode [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSKM8N_8.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/af52260_.htm].
     * A user level trace [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=849&uid=swg21177321#1] is intended to assist users with understanding how their ESQL is processed.
       It will also show a high level view of the message flow behavior.
     * The product documentation contains several suggestions for Monitoring the Global Cache [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSMKHH_9.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/bn23786_.htm].
- `E5.S8`: 2. 
 3. Locate the errors.  * Global Cache interactions are logged in the Global Cache Activity Log [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSMKHH_9.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/bj23784_.htm].
     * Informational messages and unhandled exceptions are written to the IIB Syslog [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSKM8N_8.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/an04230_.htm]. This will also contain a number of BIP71** messages relating to startup/connection of cache components, and whether any of them have failed.
     * Some messages may be written to the 'stderr' and 'stdout' files [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSKM8N_8.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/au14165_.htm], located under the Broker's (Integration Node's) workpath.
- `E5.S9`: 4. 
 5. Check for known issues and solutions.  * General information regarding the Global Cache [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSMKHH_9.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/bc23789_.htm] is available in the product documentation, as well as instructions on how to configure the cache [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSMKHH_9.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/bn23780_.htm] via the provided tooling.
     * Review how to access the Global Cache from a JavaCompute node [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSMKHH_9.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/bc23770_.htm].
     * The IIB development and support teams regularly update the IIB DeveloperWorks Blog with Global Cache solutions [https://developer.ibm.com/integration/blog/].
     * Your problem may have been discussed on the IIB dWAnswers forum [https://developer.ibm.com/answers/?community=iib].

## techqa_DEV_Q250#row-0012

Question:
Help with Security Bulletin: IIB is affected by Node.js security vulnerability ( CVE-2017-1000381 and CVE-2017-11499 ) I need to understand details regarding Security Bulletin: IBM Integration Bus is affected by Node.js security vulnerability ( CVE-2017-1000381 and CVE-2017-11499 ). Where can I find this information? 

Reference / gold answer:
You can find the information regarding the security bulletin for IBM Integration Bus being affected by Node.js security vulnerabilities CVE-2017-1000381 and CVE-2017-11499 by referring to the security bulletins provided in the context above. Specifically, you can review the Security Bulletins for IBM SDK for Node.js provided in the context to understand the details of the vulnerabilities and the remediation steps taken. Additionally, you can also visit the IBM Secure Engineering Web Portal and IBM Product Security Incident Response Blog for related information on security bulletins and incidents.

Reference evidence:
- `3x`: CVEID: CVE-2017-1000381 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2017-1000381]
- `3y`: DESCRIPTION: c-ares could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information, caused by an out-of-bounds read in the ares_parse_naptr_reply() function when parsing NAPTR responses.
- `3z`: By sending specially crafted DNS response packet, an attacker could exploit this vulnerability to read memory outside of the given input buffer and cause a denial of service.
- `3ae`: CVEID: CVE-2017-11499 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2017-11499]
- `3af`: DESCRIPTION: Node.js is vulnerable to a denial of service, caused by a flaw related to constant HashTable seeds.
- `3ag`: A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to flood the hash and cause a denial of service.

=== CANDIDATE A ===

Model-visible evidence:

- `E5.S1`: WMB IIB SECURITY BULLETIN SUMMARY WebSphere Message Broker and IBM Integration Bus using the IBM Dojo Toolkit and providing the dojox/form/resources/fileuploader.swf, dojox/form/resources/uploader.swf, dojox/av/resources/audio.swf or dojox/av/resources/video.swf files are subjected to a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability. VULNERABILITY DETAILS CVEID:CVE-2014-8917 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2014-8917] DESCRIPTION: IBM Dojo Toolkit is vulnerable to cross-site scripting, caused by improper validation of user-supplied input. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability using a specially-crafted URL to execute scripts in a victim's Web browser within the security context of the hosting Web site, when the URL is clicked. An attacker could use this vulnerability to steal the victim's cookie-based authentication credentials CVSS Base Score: 4.3 CVSS Temporal Score: Seehttp://xforce.iss.net/xforce/xfdb/99303 [http://xforce.iss.net/xforce/xfdb/99303] for the current score CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined CVSS Vector: AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:N/I:P/A:N AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND VERSIONS IBM WebSphere Message Broker V8 IBM Integration Bus V9 REMEDIATION/FIXES Follow the steps outlined in the workarounds and mitigations section. APAR IT06833 is targeted for availability in WebSphere Message Broker V8.0.0.6 and IBM Integration Bus V9.0.0.4 which will remove the affected files. WORKAROUNDS AND MITIGATIONS The files affected by this vulnerability are not used by the WebSphere Message Broker or IBM Integration Bus web user interface (web UI) and can be deleted. ## techqa_DEV_Q206#row-0057

Question:
Why does nco_confpack -export fail with the message "Tool in menu but not found"? 

I tried to export OMNIbus configuration using nco_confpack command and I get the following message:

Tool in menu but not found, menu: AlertsMenu, tool: Close

I've also tried using it with -list command and I get the same error.

Why is this happening?

Reference / gold answer:
The error "Tool in menu but not found" occurs because the menu AlertsMenu contains a tool called Close that no longer exists. The nco_confpack command is trying to export the configuration which includes this tool but since it is not found, the export fails. To resolve this issue, the tool Close needs to be recreated and associated with the menu AlertsMenu before trying to run the nco_confpack command again for exporting the configuration successfully.

Reference evidence:
- `4d`: Received this error: Tool in menu but not found, menu: AlertsMenu, tool: CLEAR_LWY. SYMPTOM
- `4e`: The command fails and the following error is received: Tool in menu but not found, menu: AlertsMenu, tool: CLEAR_LWY. CAUSE
- `4f`: The menu AlertsMenu has a tool in it called CLEAR_LWY, however the tool no longer exists.
- `4g`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
- `4h`: Recreate the tool and associate it with the menu and try to run the command again.

=== CANDIDATE A ===

- `E2.S1`: nco_g_jdbc; manageIU; RootIU; UUID TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E2.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 After uninstalling JDBC Gateway using uninstall command from $NCHOME/_uninst/nco_g_jdbc, the reinstallation is failing with a message that features already exist on the system.
- `E2.S3`: SYMPTOM
"No new features to install" window is displayed with message "You haven't selected any new features to install as the selected features already exist on the system."
- `E2.S4`: CAUSE
The output of listIU is still showing the JDBC Gateway as installed.
- `E2.S5`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
1. Back up existing DE by zipping/tarring the entire DE directory
- `E2.S6`: e.g. for root install, tar up "/usr/ibm/common/acsi" directory and keep it in another location. Alternatively, use de_backupdb.sh script to create the backup.
- `E2.S7`: 2. Run de_lsrootiu.sh script and review the output to determine the discriminant information.
- `E2.S8`: e.g. <discriminant>/opt/IBM/tivoli/netcool</discriminant>
- `E2.S9`: The discriminant would be /opt/IBM/tivoli/netcool
- `E2.S10`: 3. Run listIU.cmd or listIU.sh and in the output look for a line which has "RootIU UUID:" and the component name and version
- `E2.S11`: e.g. IU RootIU UUID: 060A90E184C84B7A98E25EC426B44288 Name: gateway-nco-g-jdbc Version: 1.5.1.0
- `E2.S12`: 4. Remove the uninstalled component from the listIU, by running
- `E2.S13`: manageIU.sh -o delete -r <discriminant> -d RootIUTypeID ,
- `E2.S14`: Based on the example above, for root install with discriminant of "/opt/IBM/tivoli/netcool" the command to run would be: 
/usr/ibm/common/acsi/bin/manageIU.sh -o delete -r /opt/IBM/tivoli/netcool -d RootIUTypeID[060A90E184C84B7A98E25EC426B44288, 1.5.1.0]
- `E2.S15`: 5. Run listIU.sh again and make sure that JDBC gateway is no longer listed.
- `E2.S16`: The reinstallation of JDBC gateway should now work. If the problem with reinstallation persists, please contact IBM Support.

    If the mqsidc tool was not run, then capture this information manually  * Record the WebSphere Message Broker version, release, and maintenance level.

     * Record the operating system version, release, and maintenance level.
     * Record the version, release, and maintenance level of any related products and components for the problematic application.
     * Collect the local error log.
       On Window systems, the local error log is the Windows Application Event Log.

- `E3.S1`: nco_g_jdbc; manageIU; RootIU; UUID TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 After uninstalling JDBC Gateway using uninstall command from $NCHOME/_uninst/nco_g_jdbc, the reinstallation is failing with a message that features already exist on the system.
- `E3.S3`: SYMPTOM
"No new features to install" window is displayed with message "You haven't selected any new features to install as the selected features already exist on the system."
- `E3.S4`: CAUSE
The output of listIU is still showing the JDBC Gateway as installed.
- `E3.S5`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
1. Back up existing DE by zipping/tarring the entire DE directory
- `E3.S6`: e.g. for root install, tar up "/usr/ibm/common/acsi" directory and keep it in another location. Alternatively, use de_backupdb.sh script to create the backup.
- `E3.S7`: 2. Run de_lsrootiu.sh script and review the output to determine the discriminant information.
- `E3.S8`: e.g. <discriminant>/opt/IBM/tivoli/netcool</discriminant>
- `E3.S9`: The discriminant would be /opt/IBM/tivoli/netcool
- `E3.S10`: 3. Run listIU.cmd or listIU.sh and in the output look for a line which has "RootIU UUID:" and the component name and version
- `E3.S11`: e.g. IU RootIU UUID: 060A90E184C84B7A98E25EC426B44288 Name: gateway-nco-g-jdbc Version: 1.5.1.0
- `E3.S12`: 4. Remove the uninstalled component from the listIU, by running
- `E3.S13`: manageIU.sh -o delete -r <discriminant> -d RootIUTypeID ,
- `E3.S14`: Based on the example above, for root install with discriminant of "/opt/IBM/tivoli/netcool" the command to run would be: 
/usr/ibm/common/acsi/bin/manageIU.sh -o delete -r /opt/IBM/tivoli/netcool -d RootIUTypeID[060A90E184C84B7A98E25EC426B44288, 1.5.1.0]
- `E3.S15`: 5. Run listIU.sh again and make sure that JDBC gateway is no longer listed.
- `E3.S16`: The reinstallation of JDBC gateway should now work. If the problem with reinstallation persists, please contact IBM Support.

 OMNIbus gateway
