- `E5.S1`: ABENDs - Dumps TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E5.S2`: QUESTION
 Why am I receiving ABEND AKEA in IODM module EKCCMTOM at offset x'1A68' when trying to run in a CICS Version 3.3.0 region? The error occurs shortly after restarting IODM without the cycling region.
- `E5.S3`: In the CICS system initialization table (SIT), STGPROT is set to "No" and RENTPGM is set to NOPROTECT. System modifications (sysmods), UN54096 and UN60897, have been applied.
- `E5.S4`: ANSWER
Refer to authorized program analysis report (APAR) PN56650 for information about IODM module EKCCMTOM and program DFHZNEP. Set both programs to the EXECKEY parameter of CICS® and give them a datalocation value of "Any." Also, change the queue status field (QUESTAT) of the IDPARMTB table from 'E' to 'D'. The IDPARMTB table defines system-wide Object Distribution Manager parameters vital to the system's operation. Making this change frees you from relying on the use of the send queue processing operator commands, OAQM and OAQC, that are between OID1 and OID2. OID1 is the ImagePlus Object Distribution Manager first-stage, and OID2 the second-stage, shutdown CICS transaction. OID2 completes the Object Distribution Manager shutdown.
- `E5.S5`: The mode settings for program DFHZNEP state that DFHZNEP must be RMODE=any, AMODE=31. Relink your DFHZNEP as 31 bit so that DFHZNAC can link to ZNEP.
- `E5.S6`: When you relink DFHZNEP as 31 bit, expect to receive error message: IEW2646 for modules DFHZNEP, EKCCVECT, and EKCCFMSG. Error message: IEW2646I is issued when an RMODE value that is specified in the PARM statement is different than the one in the electrostatic discharge (ESD) record. Included is a binder message, which warns of a conflict. As a result, the RMODE value in the PARM statement will be used, based on the hierarchy specified in the Program Management Manual.
- `E5.S7`: You might get intermittent failures in OID1 in IODM module EKCCMTOM. Continue to try the failing transaction until you receive a normal completion.
- `E5.S8`: Another element to this error was revealed during its testing. The abend appears after cycling ODM but without cycling the CICS region. For example, you might first start the CICS region, then OIUP, OID1, OID2, OIUP, OID1 (which fails), OID2 (which also fails). By cycling the CICS region, the first OID1 and OID2 will function normally.
- `E5.S9`: In this situation, the second OIUP, which initializes the Object Distribution Manager, and all other functions (DISP and so on), function without incident.
- `E5.S10`: * If you use the LMODs from EKCPSTLK with the CICS330 libraries (instead of with the CICS211 libraries), OID1 and OID2 fail after the first shutdown of ODM. 
 * If you cycle the whole region, OID1 and OID2 work the first time after an OIUP. 
 * If you bring ODM up and then try to shut it down again, you will get the abends. 
 * With the CICS330 links, the failure is consistent. 
 * With the CICS211 links, the failure is intermittent. 
 * Additionally, with the CICS330 modules: 
 * DFHECI links clean 
 * error message: IEW2646I is not produced 
 * the offset of the abend moves about 8 bytes
- `E5.S11`: Note: The error described in this document was accompanied by error message: EKC0304A return code 8 reason code 00070017 after restarting IODM without a cycling region.
- `E5.S12`: * With the CICS330 links, the failure is consistent. 
 * With the CICS211 links, the failure is intermittent. 
 * Additionally, with the CICS330 modules: 
 * DFHECI links clean

## techqa_DEV_Q018#row-0112

Question:
Why am I getting error SqlIntegrityConstraintViolationException when deploying a process application? After reinstalling Process Center (or using separate Process Centers to deploy to one Process Server) you get a deployment failure error on the Process Server:
java.lang.Exception: java.lang.Exception:com.lombardisoftware.client.delegate.BusinessDelegateException:PreparedStatementCallback; SQL [update LSW_SNAPSHOT set CREATED_ON =?,NAME = ?,ACRONYM = ?,DESCRIPTION = ?,SEQ_NUM = ?,ERROR_COUNTER =?,ORIG_CREATED_ON = ?,ACTIVATED_ON = ?,STATUS = ?,ARCHIVED_ON =?,LAST_MODIFIED = ?,REPOSITORY_BRANCH_ID = ?,CREATED_BY_USER_ID =?,BRANCH_ID = ?,PROJECT_ID = ?,LAST_MODIFIED_BY_USER_ID = ?,CHANGE_DATA= ?,IS_ACTIVE = ?,IS_BLA_ACTIVE = ?,IS_STARTED = ?,IS_INSTALLED =?,IS_BLA_INSTALLED = ?,IS_TIP_DEPLOYED = ?,IS_DEFAULT =?,TIP_DEPLOYMENT_IN_PROGRESS = ?,IS_ARCHIVED = ? where SNAPSHOT_ID = ?]; Error for batch element # 1: DB2 SQL Error: SQLCODE=-803, SQLSTATE=23505, SQLERRMC=2;BPMBDBA.LSW_SNAPSHOT, DRIVER=4.11.69; nested exception iscom.ibm.db2.jcc.am.SqlIntegrityConstraintViolationException: Error forbatch element # 1: DB2 SQL Error: SQLCODE=-803, SQLSTATE=23505,SQLERRMC=2;BPMBDBA.LSW_SNAPSHOT, DRIVER=4.11.69
How can I deploy my application?

Reference / gold answer:
You are getting the error SqlIntegrityConstraintViolationException when deploying a process application because the acronym generation code in BPM 7501 did not take into consideration the acronym of archived snapshots. This resulted in non-unique acronym generation and subsequent Constraint Violations exceptions in the database.

To resolve this issue and successfully deploy your application, you need to apply a fix for BPM 7501. You can download the fix package from Fix Central by searching for JR44672. Follow the instructions provided in the fix readme file for installation and apply the fix to your BPM environment. Once the fix is applied, the acronym generation will check for all existing acronyms in archived or unarchived state while generating a unique acronym, thereby preventing the Constraint Violation exceptions during deployment.

- `E2.S7`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: All users of IBM MQ for z/OS Version 8       *
   *                 Release 0 Modification 0 using DB2 V12.      *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: Sample job CSQ45CTB to create DB2       *
   *                      tables for a new QSG fails with message *
   *                      DSNT408I SQLCODE = -876, ERROR: INDEX   *
   *                      CANNOT BE CREATED OR ALTERED, REASON 6  *
   *                      SQLSTATE = 53092 when run against DB2   *
   *                      V12.                                    *
   ****************************************************************
   In DB2 V12 the PREVENT_NEW_IXCTRL_PART subsystem parameter has
   changed to a default value of YES which disallows the creation
   of new index-controlled partitioned tables. The sample JCL in
   CSQ45CTB attempts to create table CSQ.ADMIN_B_MESSAGES of this
   type, which leads to the error seen.
- `E2.S8`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  New sample JCL, with prefix CSQ4X, is provided for use with DB2
   V12.

- `E4.S1`: v61rnotes; SQLException ORA-01483; v612rnotes TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E4.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 If WebSphere® Process Server is configured with Oracle 9i as the database, and Oracle Thin Driver as the database driver, failed events are not saved to the database if the event size is larger than 4 KB.
- `E4.S3`: SYMPTOM
The following exception is written to the logs:
- `E4.S4`: java.sql.SQLException: ORA-01483: invalid length for DATE or NUMBER bind variable
DSRA0010E: SQL State = 72000, Error Code = 1,483 
CAUSE
The Oracle 9i Thin Driver limits the size of data to no more than 4 KB for VARCHAR2, NVARCHAR2, BLOB, and CLOB types.
- `E4.S5`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Use either of the following solutions to solve the problem:
- `E4.S6`: * Use the Oracle 10g driver file.  1. Log on to the administrative console and navigate to Environment > WebSphere Variables.
- `E4.S7`: 2. Select the variable ORACLE_JDBC_DRIVER_PATH.
- `E4.S8`: 3. Change the variable value to the folder that contains the Oracle 10g driver (ojdbc14.jar).
- `E4.S9`: 4. Save the configuration.
- `E4.S10`: 5. Restart the server.
- `E4.S11`: Note: In a network deployment environment, change the variable value at the cell level and in all of the nodes scopes, and restart all of the servers and deployment manager processes.
- `E4.S12`: * If the Oracle server or client is installed and configured correctly on the same system as WebSphere Process Server, change the data source to use the Oracle 9i OCI driver.  1. Log on to the administrative console and navigate to Resources > JDBC > Data sources.
- `E4.S13`: 2. Select the data source with the JNDI name jdbc/WPSDB.
- `E4.S14`: 3. Change the URL format from Thin to OCI. For example, if the original URL is jdbc:oracle:thin:@localhost:1521:WPRCSDB, change it to jdbc:oracle:oci:@WPRCSDB.
- `E4.S15`: 4. Save the configuration.
- `E4.S16`: 5. Restart the server.

- `E1.S1`: v61rnotes; SQLException ORA-01483; v612rnotes TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E1.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 If WebSphere® Process Server is configured with Oracle 9i as the database, and Oracle Thin Driver as the database driver, failed events are not saved to the database if the event size is larger than 4 KB.
- `E1.S3`: SYMPTOM
The following exception is written to the logs:
- `E1.S4`: java.sql.SQLException: ORA-01483: invalid length for DATE or NUMBER bind variable
DSRA0010E: SQL State = 72000, Error Code = 1,483 
CAUSE
The Oracle 9i Thin Driver limits the size of data to no more than 4 KB for VARCHAR2, NVARCHAR2, BLOB, and CLOB types.
- `E1.S5`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Use either of the following solutions to solve the problem:
- `E1.S6`: * Use the Oracle 10g driver file.  1. Log on to the administrative console and navigate to Environment > WebSphere Variables.
- `E1.S7`: 2. Select the variable ORACLE_JDBC_DRIVER_PATH.
- `E1.S8`: 3. Change the variable value to the folder that contains the Oracle 10g driver (ojdbc14.jar).
- `E1.S9`: 4. Save the configuration.
- `E1.S10`: 5. Restart the server.
- `E1.S11`: Note: In a network deployment environment, change the variable value at the cell level and in all of the nodes scopes, and restart all of the servers and deployment manager processes.
- `E1.S12`: * If the Oracle server or client is installed and configured correctly on the same system as WebSphere Process Server, change the data source to use the Oracle 9i OCI driver.  1. Log on to the administrative console and navigate to Resources > JDBC > Data sources.
- `E1.S13`: 2. Select the data source with the JNDI name jdbc/WPSDB.
- `E1.S14`: 3. Change the URL format from Thin to OCI. For example, if the original URL is jdbc:oracle:thin:@localhost:1521:WPRCSDB, change it to jdbc:oracle:oci:@WPRCSDB.
- `E1.S15`: 4. Save the configuration.
- `E1.S16`: 5. Restart the server.

   nknown Source)
- `E5.S13`: Eclipse ant creates a different classloader to run the ant
   scripts. The problem is that with WID, the JRE contains xerces,
   during builds the plugins use the xerces plugin to load the
   xmls. The problem occurs when the is run on the main thread, the
   classloader does not pick up the xerces plugin rather uses the
   xerces that comes with the JRE, causing a class case exception
   that's wrapped in the CoreException.
- `E5.S14`: The solution is the create our own classloader that uses the
   plugin classloading first before loading the classes from the
   JRE.
- `E5.S15`: The code changes are in com.ibm.wbit.comptest.ant.
   There are 2 new classes RunAntWidPreferences.java and
   WidAntClassloader.java
   The RunAntWid.java class was updated to use those classes.

## techqa_DEV_Q275#row-0091

Question:
Jobtask long description How do I modify the JP sheet to include the JOBTASK Long description in the query.  I have tried JOBTASK.DESCRIPTION.DESCRIPTION_LONGDESCRITION and other combinations but they do not seem to work. 

Reference / gold answer:
To modify the JP sheet to include the JOBTASK Long description in the query, you can use the following steps:

1. Select the JOBPLANID from the JOBPLAN table where JPNUM='IT-ISSUE'.
2. Take the output JOBPLANID from the query above.
3. Use the following query to retrieve the long description for the job tasks in the JOBTASK table:
   
   ```
   SELECT LDTEXT FROM LONGDESCRIPTION 
   WHERE LDOWNERTABLE='JOBTASK' AND LDOWNERCOL='DESCRIPTION' 
   AND LDKEY IN (SELECT JOBTASK.JOBTASKID FROM JOBTASK WHERE JOBTASK.JOBPLANID = <JOBPLANID>)
   ```

Replace `<JOBPLANID>` with the actual JOBPLANID you obtained from the first query. This will retrieve the long description for the job tasks associated with the specific job plan. 

Using this query structure should help you successfully modify the JP sheet to include the JOBTASK Long description in the query.

Reference evidence:
- `3k`: SELECT JOBPLANID FROM JOBPLAN WHERE JPNUM='IT-ISSUE'
- `3l`: output: JOBPLANID = 51
- `3m`: Then take output from the query above and put it in the query below:
- `3n`: SELECT LDTEXT FROM LONGDESCRIPTION WHERE LDOWNERTABLE='JOBTASK' AND LDOWNERCOL='DESCRIPTION'
- `3o`: AND LDKEY IN (SELECT JOBTASK.JOBTASKID FROM JOBTASK WHERE jobtask.jobplanid= 51)
- `3p`: output: LDTEXT = task10 LDTEXT

- `E2.S3`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  When  attempting to issue a long-running command scheduler
   command using lrcmd.[bat|sh] through the On-Demand Router (ODR),
   an IOException will be returned as follows:
- `E2.S4`: C:\IBM\WebSphere\AppServer\bin>lrcmd -cmd=submit
   -xJCL=C:\SimpleCIxJCL.xml -port=<ODR port> -host=<ODR hostname>
- `E2.S5`: CWLRB4940I: com.ibm.ws.batch.wsbatch : -cmd=submit
   -xJCL=C:\SimpleCIxJCL.xml -port=<ODR port> -host=<ODR hostname>
- `E2.S6`: CWLRB4880E: -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\SimpleCIxJCL.xml -port=<ODR
   port>
   -host=<ODR hostname> failed:
              com.ibm.ws.batch.wsbatch: java.io.IOException:

- `E2.S7`: LOCAL FIX

- `E2.S8`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: All users of WebSphere Extended Deployment   *
   *                 version 6.0.1.1.                             *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: When  attempting to issue a             *
   *                      long-running scheduler command using    *
   *                      lrcmd.[bat|sh] through the On-Demand    *
   *                      Router (ODR), an IOException will be    *
   *                      returned as follows:                    *
   *                                                              *
   *                      C:\IBM\WebSphere\AppServer\bin>lrcmd    *
   *                      -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\SimpleCIxJCL.xml   *
   *                      -port=<ODR port> -host=<ODR hostname>   *
   *                                                              *
   *                      CWLRB4940I: com.ibm.ws.batch.wsbatch :  *
   *                      -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\SimpleCIxJCL.xml   *
   *                      -port=<ODR port> -host=<ODR hostname>   *
   *                                                              *
   *                      CWLRB4880E: -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\Simple *
   *                      CIxJCL.xml -port=<ODR port>             *
   *                      -host=<ODR hostname> failed:            *
   *                      com.ibm.ws.batch.wsbatch: java.io.      *
   *                      IOException:Connection close: Read      *
   *                      failed.  Possible end of stream         *
   *                      encountered.                            *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   The problem was caused by assuming in the code the every SOAP
   request will have a web module with web service and operation
   node defined. Therefore for the cases where web service and
   operation nodes do not exist, trying to use the operation map
   to get a key results in a null pointer exception. To the
   caller this wrapped up exception shows up as an IO Exception.
- `E2.S9`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  For each SOAP over HTTP request, check for the definition of
   web service and web service operation nodes, if they exist use
   them to fetch the workclasses and perform further request
   classification as necessary, otherwise, use the original
   request mapping to route request.

- `E3.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  After updating a model from an earlier version of Rhapsody to
   Rhapsody 8.2, There are  some instances where the code is
   incorrect.
   When a constructor initializer contains a boolean expression
   with a greater-than (>) symbol, this is causing Rhapsody to
   generate what appears to be garbled code.
   For example, if the ctor initializer in the model contains the
   following:
- `E3.S5`: itsClass(argument_0, argument_0 > 0, argument_0, argument_0),
   attribute_0(argument_0)
- `E3.S6`: the resulting code is:
- `E3.S7`: class_with_gt_initializer::class_with_gt_initializer(int
   argument_0) :
   itsClass(argument_0, argument_0 > 0,
   argument_0),
   attribute_0(argument_0),
   argument_0),
   attribute_0(argument_0) {
- `E3.S8`: I have tried setting CPP_CG::Class::MultiLineInitializerList to
   false to see if the feature to format the initializer list on
   multiple lines is causing the issue, but that does not resolve
   it.
- `E3.S9`: LOCAL FIX
- `E3.S10`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED:                                              *
   * Rhapsody                                                     *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION:                                         *
   * ISSUE WITH NON-TRIVIAL CONSTRUCTOR INITIALIZER               *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
- `E3.S11`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  constructor initializer with the chanracters '>','<' sometimes
   not Roundtriped, generated correctly
   problem fixed.
- `E3.S12`: one limitation stay, if initializer contain generalization to
   template class the strig in the template  <> section must not
   contain the charcters   '>','<' (exept as template brackets)
   posible work around this limitations:
   - brackets around the template  expresions, exapmples:
   superclass<(template_expersion > 1)>(init_expression)
    superclass<<(expe1 >1)>,<(expe2 <1)>>(init expression)
   -use property CPP_CG::Operation::OrderedConstructorInitializer
   for correct none reorder code generation
   -use property
   CPP_CG::Operation::DisableAutoGeneratedInitializer
   for simpler code generation and Roundtrip of constructor
   initialaizer, in this case the initialazer is a simple string
   that copied as is from the initializer field to the code in code
   generation and to the model in roundtrip

- `E2.S1`: plug-in; plugin; GSKIT; GSKIT5; GSKIT6; GSKIT7; recommendations was app server TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E2.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Which version of Plug-in can be used with which version of WAS?
- `E2.S3`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
- `E2.S4`: Supported combinations of IBM HTTP Server, WebSphere Application Server, and the WebSphere WebServer Plug-in
There are a variety of issues surrounding support of mixed releases of IBM HTTP Server (IHS), WebSphere Application Server (WAS), and the WebSphere Web Server Plug-in (WAS Plugin). This document only refers to the IBM HTTP Server (powered by Apache) on AIX, HP-UX, Linux, Solaris, Windows, and z/OS (not "IBM i").
- `E2.S5`: In general, the recommended configuration is to use all three components from the same release. However, there are a variety of situations where using other combinations is required.
- `E2.S6`: Note: Customer and product support is only provided when all components in use have a support entitlement.
- `E2.S7`: Terminology
- `E2.S8`: * 
 * Versioning
 *  
   WebSphere Application Server uses the following naming scheme: V.R.M.F 
    * V = version 
    * R = release 
    * M = modification 
    * F = fix pack
- `E2.S9`: * Supported, UnSupported, and other configurations
 *  
   For reference, we categorize support into three categories: supported, unsupported, and other: WebSphere Application Server Support Statement [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg27004311]
- `E2.S10`: Supported combinations of the Application Server and WebServer Plug-in A release (such as 9.0, 8.5, 8.0, or 7.0) of the WebServer Plug-in can be used with the corresponding release and any previous releases of the application server, as long as the application server version (in terms of V.R.M.F) is not more
than two versions older than the WebServer Plug-in.
- `E2.S11`: Any release of WebSphere Application Server Liberty ("Liberty Profile") is supported with any release of the WAS Plug-in from 8.5.5 or later. This include Liberty Profile continuous delivery releases (such as 16.0.0.x or 17.0.0.x) as well as Beta releases.
- `E2.S12`: * For example, an 8.0 Plugin can front-end servers from 8.0, 7.0, 6.1, and 6.0 whether they're all from a single release or in a mixed cell. Application servers from 8.5 or 8.5.5 would not be a supported configuration, because they are later releases. Similarly, application servers from 5.1/5.0 would not be supported because they are more than two versions (in terms of V.R.M.F) older.
- `E2.S13`: Examples of N-2 Version support:  *  WAS Plugin 9.0: WAS 7.0, WAS 8.0, WAS 8.5, WAS 8.5.5, WAS 9.0 WAS Plugin 8.5.5: WAS 6.0, WAS 6.1, WAS 7.0, WAS 8.0, WAS 8.5, WAS 8.5.5 WAS Plugin 8.0: WAS 6.0, WAS 6.1, WAS 7.0, WAS 8.0 WAS Plugin 7.0: WAS 5.0, WAS 5.1, WAS 6.0, WAS 6.1, WAS 7.0
- `E2.S14`: Exceptions: 
 * IHS 7.0 + Plugin 7.0 is supported with WAS 8.0, 8.5, and 8.5.5 as a transitional measure for users of third-party IHS modules that did not support IHS 8.0 or later in a timely manner. It is important to note that IHS 7.0 was released in 2008 and lacks support for important security protocols like TLS1.2, ECDHE, and AES-GCM. (IHS 8.0 was released in 2011)
- `E2.S15`: Notes: 
 * Refer to the following URL for considerations and frequently asked questions related to using the version
- `E2.S16`: timely manner. It is important to note that IHS 7.0 was released in 2008 and lacks support for important security protocols like TLS1.2, ECDHE, and AES-GCM. (IHS 8.0 was released in 2011)
- `E2.S17`: Notes: 
 * Refer to the following URL for considerations and frequently asked questions related to using the version 8 WAS Plug-in with a version 7 application server:
- `E2.S18`: http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/httpserv/ihsdiag/ihs8was7.html [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/httpserv/ihsdiag/ihs8was7.html]
- `E2.S19`: Supported configurations of Web Servers and the WAS Plugin Given a compatible Plugin has been selected based on WAS release requirements, The release (V.R.M.F) of IBM HTTP Server used must match the Plugin release exactly.
- `E2.S20`: Third-party webservers are only a supported configuration if they are explicitly listed in the supporting software documentation for the WAS release.
- `E2.S21`: Exceptions:
- `E2.S22`: * IBM HTTP Server 8.5 used as part of z/OS Ported Tools is additionally supported with the 8.0 Plug-in. While this combination is supported, using the corresponding release is strongly recommended. 
 * IBM HTTP Server 9.0 included with z/OS V2R2 (and later) is additionally supported with the 8.0 and 8.5 Plugins. While this combination is supported, using the corresponding release is strongly recommended (when available).
- `E2.S23`: Unsupported combinations These are combinations with known technical problems.
- `E2.S24`: * IHS 8.0 or later cannot be used with Plugin 7.0 or earlier (distributed platforms, incompatible GSKit major release) 
 * IHS 7.0 or earlier cannot be used with Plugin 8.0 or later (distributed platforms, incompatible GSKit major release)
- `E2.S25`: Other configurations 
Any combination not explicitly addressed above is an "other configuration". These configurations are not tested or recommended. 
 * If WAS is a higher releases than the Plugin, the generated XML might trigger warnings at startup.
- `E2.S26`: Other recommendations 
There is no required relationship between IHS, Plugin, and WAS fixpack (V.R.M. F) levels, but staying current is strongly recommended. Furthermore, using levels contemporary (but not necessarily identical) with one another is also strongly recommended.
- `E2.S27`: History 
 * 20150812: Clarify V7 transitional support and "VRMF" terminology 
 * 20150511: Previous versions of this document were ambiguous with respect to mixed cells vs cells from a previous release. 
 * 20150511: Previous versions of this document permitted future releases of IHS + Plugin only under specific enumerated circumstances. 
 * 20150511: Permit IHS on z/OS to use previous releases of the WAS Plug-in. 
 * 20160316: Emphasize Version as the differentiator, provide examples of N-2 versions. 
 * 20160624: Mention relationship to Liberty.

   port>

- `E3.S7`: LOCAL FIX
 *  N/A
- `E3.S8`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: All users of WebSphere Extended Deployment   *
   *                 version 6.0.1.1.                             *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: When  attempting to issue a             *
   *                      long-running scheduler command using    *
   *                      lrcmd.[bat|sh] through the On-Demand    *
   *                      Router (ODR), an IOException will be    *
   *                      returned as follows:                    *
   *                                                              *
   *                      C:\IBM\WebSphere\AppServer\bin>lrcmd    *
   *                      -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\SimpleCIxJCL.xml   *
   *                      -port=<ODR port> -host=<ODR hostname>   *
   *                                                              *
   *                      CWLRB4940I: com.ibm.ws.batch.wsbatch :  *
   *                      -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\SimpleCIxJCL.xml   *
   *                      -port=<ODR port> -host=<ODR hostname>   *
   *                                                              *
   *                      CWLRB4880E: -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\Simple *
   *                      CIxJCL.xml -port=<ODR port>             *
   *                      -host=<ODR hostname> failed:            *
   *                      com.ibm.ws.batch.wsbatch: java.io.      *
   *                      IOException:Connection close: Read      *
   *                      failed.  Possible end of stream         *
   *                      encountered.                            *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   The problem was caused by assuming in the code the every SOAP
   request will have a web module with web service and operation
   node defined. Therefore for the cases where web service and
   operation nodes do not exist, trying to use the operation map
   to get a key results in a null pointer exception. To the
   caller this wrapped up exception shows up as an IO Exception.
- `E3.S9`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  For each SOAP over HTTP request, check for the definition of
   web service and web service operation nodes, if they exist use
   them to fetch the workclasses and perform further request
   classification as necessary, otherwise, use the original
   request mapping to route request.

## techqa_DEV_Q218#row-0137

Question:
Why is MQ pattern showing installed MQ version as 8.0.0.2, instead of 8.0.0.4 when client tries to deploy pattern at the MQ 8.0.0.4 version in PureApplication System? In the pattern, it was clearly showing MQ version 8.0.0.4. After deployment, client checked the MQ version on the Virtual Machine and it shows 8.0.0.2 instead.


Reference / gold answer:
The issue occurred because of an interface change in IBM Pure Application System 2.1.2.0 and later. Even though the client tried to deploy the pattern at MQ version 8.0.0.4, due to this change, the installation and upgrade of IBM MQ at the latest maintenance level contained in the pattern-type failed. The installation appeared to succeed, but IBM MQ 8.0.0.2 was installed instead and the subsequent fixpack update was not applied. This restriction affected IBM MQ Pure Application System pattern-types 1.0.0.2 and earlier, preventing the installation of versions later than 8.0.0.2.

Reference evidence:
- `1b`:  Users observe errors when attempting to install or migrate to IBM MQ 8.0.0.4 using IBM Pure Application System. SYMPTOM
- `1g`: Because of an interface change in IBM Pure Application System 2.1.2.0, and in 2.2.0.0 and greater, installation and upgrade of IBM MQ at the latest maintenance level contained in the pattern-type fails.
- `1h`: The installation appears to succeed, but IBM MQ 8.0.0.2 is installed and the subsequent fixpack update is not applied.
- `1m`: You cannot install later versions e.g., 8.0.0.4.

=== CANDIDATE A ===

- `E3.S13`: INSTALLATION INSTRUCTIONS
To install a Unix Client:
1. Logon as root, create an empty directory (with sufficient space to receive the download file) and make it current. 
2. Download mqc8_platform to this directory. (Where 'platform' is replaced with a specific platform name e.g. AIX, Linux-x86)
3. Uncompress mqc8_platform.
4. Execute tar -xvf mqc8_platform.
5. Execute rm mqc8_platform.
6. Follow the instructions provided in the IBM MQ V8 Knowledge Center to complete the installation of the client.

- `E4.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  An application using the WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 classes for JMS is
   connected to a WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 queue manager using the
   CLIENT transport.
- `E4.S5`: When the runmqsc command:
- `E4.S6`: DISPLAY CHSTATUS(channel name)
- `E4.S7`: is run on the queue manager for the channel that the
   application has used to connect to the queue manager, the
   following output is displayed:
- `E4.S8`: RVERSION(00000000)
   RPRODUCT(MQJM)
- `E4.S9`: LOCAL FIX
- `E4.S10`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   USERS AFFECTED:
   This issue affects two categories of user:
- `E4.S11`: 1. Users of the WebSphere MQ command runmqsc who run:
- `E4.S12`: DISPLAY CHSTATUS(channel name)
- `E4.S13`: to display the status of a channel.
- `E4.S14`: 2. Users of the WebSphere MQ Explorer who display the status of
   a Channel by highlighting a Channel in the Channels pane, right
   clicking and selecting Status->Channel Status... from the pop-
   up menu.
- `E4.S15`: Platforms affected:
   All Distributed (iSeries, all Unix and Windows)
   ****************************************************************
   PROBLEM SUMMARY:
   Applications that connect to WebSphere MQ using the CLIENT
   transport provide version information to the queue manager
   about the level of WebSphere MQ Client code that the
   application is running. This version information is in the
   format:
- `E4.S16`: VVRRMMFF
- `E4.S17`: where:
- `E4.S18`: - VV = Version
   - RR = Release
   - MM = Maintenance level
   - FF = Fix level
- `E4.S19`: The runmqsc command:
- `E4.S20`: DISPLAY CHSTATUS(channel name)
- `E4.S21`: will report this version information in the RVERSION attribute.
- `E4.S22`: The WebSphere MQ Explorer shows the version information in the:
- `E4.S23`: Remote Version
- `E4.S24`: column in the Channel Status window.
- `E4.S25`: In order to determine the version information to pass to a
   queue manager, the WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 classes for Java and
   classes for JMS, and the WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 Resource Adapter,
   looked inside the MANIFEST.MF file contained within the file:
- `E4.S26`: com.ibm.mq.jmqi.jar
- `E4.S27`: for the property:
- `E4.S28`: version
- `E4.S29`: However, the MANIFEST.MF file did not contain an entry for this
   property. This caused the WebSphere MQ classes for Java and
   classes for JMS, and the WebSphere MQ Resource Adapter,to
   specify:
- `E4.S30`: 00000000
- `E4.S31`: as the version number being used.
- `E4.S32`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  The WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 classes for Java and classes for JMS,
   and the WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 Resource Adapter, have been updated
   to use the information in the property:
- `E4.S33`: com.ibm.mq.jmqi
- `E4.S34`: within the MANIFEST.MF file contained within the JAR file:
- `E4.S35`: com.ibm.mq.jmqi.jar
- `E4.S36`: to determine what version information to pass to the queue
   manager.
- `E4.S37`: Applications using the WebSphere MQ Resource Adapter or Java
   and JMS clients which have this APAR applied will report
   their version information correctly to the queue manager,
   which will be reflected in the information returned by
   runmqsc and the MQ Explorer.

 *  They got the message "Cannot invoke method toInteger( ) on null
   object"
   once dropping the ODR part on the pattern editor.
   It is an error only WCA which upgraded WCA from v1.1.1.0 GA code
   to v2.0.0.0 GA.
   When they use WCA 2.0 GA code with reset, this error does not
   occur.
   .
   Here is the steps taken during the migration from 1.1.1 GA.
   1. replace the firmware from v1.1.1.0 GA to v2.0.0.0 GA
   2. upload WAS HV 7.0.0.11 (RHEL) to WCA via
      CLI(cloudburst.virtualimage.create('local path of ova') )and
      Enabled IMP
   3. upload WAS HV 7.0.0.11(SLES) to WCA via CLI and Enabled IMP
   4. tried to create new pattern with ODR part, but failed with
      both RHEL and SLES ODR parts.
- `E3.S4`: LOCAL FIX
 *  reset the GA 2.0 firmware
- `E3.S5`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  Title
- `E3.S6`: The On-Demand Router part is not usable in user interface when a
   WebSphere Cloudburst Appliance is upgraded to 2.0.0.0 and the
   WebSphere Hypervisor Edition with Intelligent Management Pack
   image is imported
- `E3.S7`: Error description
   The problematic scenario is when:
   (1) WebSphere Cloudburst Appliance is upgraded to version
   2.0.0.0
   (2) Then the new WebSphere Hypervisor Edition with the
   Intelligent Management Pack virtual image is imported, the
   license is accepted, and the Intelligent Management pack support
   is enabled.
   (3) Then when you attempt to drag and drop a  On demand router
   part onto the pattern. The pattern no longer can be displayed
   and a "Cannot invoke method toInteger( ) on null object"
   message is displayed.
- `E3.S8`: Local fix
   There is no workaround for this issue.
- `E3.S9`: Problem summary
   ****************************************************************
- `E3.S10`: * USERS AFFECTED:
   Users upgrading a WebSphere CloudBurst Appliance from releases
   prior to 2.0.0.0 to 2.0.0.0, who then import a new WebSphere
   Hypervisor Edition virtual image.
   ****************************************************************
- `E3.S11`: * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION:
   In previous releases of WebSphere CloudBurst appliance, the On
   Demand Router part is no included. This is actually two parts,
   an abstract conceptual part, and a specific concrete"part
   associated with a particular WebSphere Hypervisor Edition
   virtual image. The upgrade from WebSphere CloudBurst 2.0.0.0
   does not add the conceptual part to the WebSphere CloudBurst
   Appliance. WebSphere CloudBurst Appliance is unable to construct
   a consistent pattern model, and the message "Cannot invoke
   method toInteger( ) on null object"  is the result.
   ****************************************************************
- `E3.S12`: Problem conclusion
   The WebSphere CloudBurst Appliance 2.0.0.1 upgrade includes the
   addition of the On Demand Router conceptual part to the
   WebSphere Cloudburst appliance.
   If this upgrade is applied, the problem is resolved.
- `E3.S13`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION

 IBM PureApplication System contains IBM WebSphere Application Server, which has a security vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code by connecting to a management port and executing a specific sequence of instructions.

DESCRIPTION: WebSphere Application Server could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code by connecting to a management port and executing a specific sequence of instructions.

## techqa_DEV_Q166#row-0119

Question:
Which version of the WebSphere MQ Resource Adapter is shipped with  WebSphere Application Server? Which version of WebSphere MQ JCA resource adapter is shipped with WebSphere Application Server ? 

Reference / gold answer:
WebSphere Application Server Version 7 ships with the WebSphere MQ 7.0 Resource Adapter.
- WAS 7.0.0.27 - WMQ 7.0.1.9

WebSphere Application Server Version 8 ships with the WebSphere MQ 7.0 Resource Adapter.
- WAS 8.0.0.5 - WMQ 7.0.1.9

WebSphere Application Server Version 8.5 ships with the WebSphere MQ 7.1 Resource Adapter.
- WAS 8.5.0.2 - WMQ 7.1.0.2

Reference evidence:
- `2ac`: WebSphere Application Server Version 8.5 ships with the WebSphere MQ 7.1 Resource Adapter.
- `2ad`: - WAS 8.5.0.2 - WMQ 7.1.0.2 - This level includes APAR IV14093
- `2ae`: - WAS 8.5.0.1 - WMQ 7.1.0.1
- `2ag`: WebSphere Application Server Version 8 ships with the WebSphere MQ 7.0 Resource Adapter.
- `2ah`: - WAS 8.0.0.5 - WMQ 7.0.1.9 - This level includes APAR IV14093
- `2ai`: - WAS 8.0.0.4 - WMQ 7.0.1.7
- `2aj`: - WAS 8.0.0.3 - WMQ 7.0.1.7
- `2ak`: - WAS 8.0.0.2 - WMQ 7.0.1.6
- `2al`: - WAS 8.0.0.1 - WMQ 7.0.1.5
- `2am`: WebSphere Application Server Version 7 ships with the WebSphere MQ 7.0 Resource Adapter.
- `2an`: - WAS 7.0.0.27 - WMQ 7.0.1.9 - This level includes APAR IV14093
- `2ao`: - WAS 7.0.0.25 - WMQ 7.0.1.7
- `2ap`: - WAS 7.0.0.23 - WMQ 7.0.1.7
- `2aq`: - WAS 7.0.0.21 - WMQ 7.0.1.6
- `2ar`: - WAS 7.0.0.19 - WMQ 7.0.1.5
- `3f`: The WebSphere MQ messaging provider in WebSphere Application Server Version 7 and Version 8 includes a version of the WebSphere MQ resource adapter.
- `3g`: The version of the resource adapter supplied with the Application Server should be used in these environment.

=== CANDIDATE A ===

- `E1.S1`: DOWNLOADABLE FILES ABSTRACT This SupportPac contains all the IBM MQ V9 client components. DOWNLOAD DESCRIPTION Click here to go straight to the download table. An IBM MQ client is part of the product that can be installed on its own, on a separate machine from the base product and server. You can run an IBM MQ application on an IBM MQ client and it can interact, by means of a communications protocol, with one or more IBM MQ servers and connect to their queue managers. The servers to which the client connects may or may not be part of a cluster. IBM MQ Family Platforms provides a list of which platforms are supported as IBM MQ Clients and/or Servers. An application that you want to run in the IBM MQ client environment must first be linked with the relevant client library. When the application issues an MQI call, the IBM MQ client code directs the request to a queue manager, where it is processed and from where a reply is sent back to the client. The link between the application and the client code is established dynamically at run time. The MQI is available to applications running on the client platform; the queues and other IBM MQ objects are held on a queue manager that you have installed on a server machine. Click here to go straight to the download table. Possible Uses • Why use IBM MQ clients? » Using IBM MQ clients is an efficient way of implementing IBM MQ messaging and queuing. » You can have an application that uses the MQI running on one machine and the queue manager running on a different machine, either physical or virtual. The benefits of doing this are: - There is no need for a full IBM MQ implementation on the client machine. - Hardware requirements on the client system are reduced. - System administration requirements are reduced. - An IBM MQ application, running on a client, can connect to multiple queue managers on different systems. - Alternative channels using different transmission protocols can be used. • What applications run on an IBM MQ client? » The full MQI is supported in the client environment and this enables almost any IBM MQ application to be relinked to run on an IBM MQ client. Link the application on the IBM MQ client to the MQIC library, rather than to the MQI library. The exceptions are: - An application that uses global transactions; that is, it requires sync point coordination with resource managers other than the queue manager. - Get(signal) on z/OS. » Applications which are built using various programming languages including C, C++, .NET (Windows systems only), COBOL, Java and JMS. » Applications running within application servers that are certified as having passed the JEE 7 Compatibility Test Suite can use the IBM MQ resource adapter provided in the SupportPac. For more information see IBM MQ resource adapter v9.0 statement of support [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSFKSJ_9.0.0/com.ibm.mq.dev.doc/q128150_.htm]. Note: An application running on an IBM MQ client can connect to more than one queue manager concurrently, or use a queue manager name with an asterisk (*) on an MQCONN or MQCONNX call. » Applications running within application servers that are certified as having passed the JEE 7 Compatibility Test Suite can use the IBM MQ resource adapter provided in the SupportPac. For more information see IBM MQ resource adapter v9.0 statement of support [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSFKSJ_9.0.0/com.ibm.mq.dev.doc/q128150_.htm]. Note: An application running on an IBM MQ client can connect to more than one queue manager concurrently, or use a queue manager name with an asterisk (*) on an MQCONN or MQCONNX call. If you want to link to the queue manager libraries instead of the client libraries, you have to modify the application to enable this. Applications created using this client can be used to exchange messages between other XMS applications, JMS applications or native IBM MQ applications. - `E2.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS V7.0.1.5 (or later): Failure
   Data Capture (FDC) files
   with Probe
   ID JO076001 and JO205001 are generated following a remote
   connection to a Queue Manager that has conversation sharing
   disabled:
- `E2.S5`: | Probe Id     :- JO076001
   | Component    :- RemoteFAP.MQOPEN(Hconn,MQOD,int,Phobj,Pi
   | Probe Type   :- INCORROUT
   | Comment1     :- MQOPEN reply expected
- `E2.S6`: | Probe Id     :- JO205001
   | Component    :- RemoteConnection.removeHconn(RemoteTls,R
   | Probe Type   :- INCORROUT
   | Comment1     :- Hconn is not associated with this connection
- `E2.S7`: LOCAL FIX
- `E2.S8`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   USERS AFFECTED:
   This issue affects users of the WebSphere MQ V7.0.1.5 Classes
   for Java/JMS (or later) who have established a remote connection
   to a Queue Manager via a channel that has Conversation Sharing
   disabled (SHARECNV=0 or SHARECNV=1).
- `E2.S9`: This includes users of:
- `E2.S10`: - The WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 Classes for JMS
   - The WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 Resource Adapter.
   - The WebSphere Application Server V7.0 and V8.0 WebSphere MQ
   messaging provider.
   - The WebSphere Application Server V6.1 WebSphere MQ messaging
   provider who have configured the WebSphere variable
   MQ_INSTALL_ROOT to point to a WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 installation.
- `E2.S11`: Platforms affected:
   All Distributed (iSeries, all Unix and Windows)
   ****************************************************************
   PROBLEM SUMMARY:
   By default in the WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS,
   conversation
   sharing is enabled and set to 10 on the client side. The client
   only discovers that Conversation Sharing is disabled following
   negotiation with a Queue Manager on the completion of a
   connection over a Channel that has SHARECNV=0 or SHARECNV=1.
- `E2.S12`: When a WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS application requests a
   remote connection to a Queue Manager the client first attempts
   to find an already established TCP/IP connection which can be
   shared. As part of this process the list of known TCP/IP
   connections are matched for their suitability, this list
   includes connections which are in the process of being
   established (MQCONN reply not received from the Queue Manager).
- `E2.S13`: When a WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS application requested a
   remote connection it was matched for sharing with a connection
   that was still in the process of being established. The
   WebSphere MQ Client waited for the connection to complete and
   due to a small timing window began incorrectly sharing the
   connection without confirming the connection's suitability. If
   the connection's suitability had been checked then the
   connection
   would have been marked unsuitable due to the Negotiated Channel
   specifying that Conversation Sharing was disabled (SHARECNV=0 or
   SHARECNV=1).
   As the connection (which did not support conversation sharing)
   was now shared by two threads, packets destined for one thread
   were erroneously received by the other, this led to the client
   being in an inconsistent state and the two FDCs being generated.
- `E2.S14`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  The WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS have been modified to
   correctly restrict conversation sharing when using a connection
   that does not support conversation sharing (SHARECNV=0 or
   SHARECNV=1).

- `E4.S1`: TECHNOTE (FAQ) QUESTION How can I make use of the WebSphere MQ Read Ahead functionality from an application that uses the WebSphere MQ classes for JMS to create a subscription on a topic, and then synchronously receives messages that are published on that topic? ANSWER WebSphere MQ V7 introduced a new feature called "Read Ahead [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSFKSJ_8.0.0/com.ibm.mq.dev.doc/q026310_.htm]". This performance optimization allows WebSphere MQ queue managers to stream non-persistent messages to client applications connecting via TCP/IP before the application has requested them. The client stores these messages in a Read Ahead Buffer. When an application requests a message, the client removes the message from the buffer and gives it to the application for processing. JMS applications running in one of the following environments: * The WebSphere MQ classes for JMS. * The WebSphere MQ Resource Adapter. * The WebSphere MQ OSGi bundles. that connect to a WebSphere MQ queue manager using the CLIENT transport in WebSphere MQ messaging provider normal mode, [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSFKSJ_8.0.0/com.ibm.mq.connect.doc/intro_jms_msgprov.htm] and receive messages synchronously, can make use of the new functionality. This technote will look at how applications that subscribe to a topic need to be written in order to take advantage of the Read Ahead functionality, as well as discussing what JMS Destination and WebSphere MQ properties need to be set to turn on Read Ahead. Applications running within an WebSphere Application Server environment can also make use of this functionality. Details of how to do this will be covered in a future technote. Writing a JMS application to use Read Ahead to receive messages synchronously The Read Ahead feature will only stream non-persistent messages to client applications that are getting messages outside of a transaction. In JMS terms, this means that the application must be using a non-transacted JMS session that has an acknowledgement mode of either AUTO_ACKNOWLEDGE or DUPS_OK_ACKNOWLEDGE in order to be eligible to make use of Read Ahead. Here is an example which shows an application creating a non-transacted, AUTO_ACKNOWLEDGE JMS Session: * The non-transacted JMS Session can then be used to create a MessageConsumer object for the JMS Destination that maps to the WebSphere MQ topic which the non-persistent messages will be published on. Once the MessageConsumer has been created, applications that get non-persistent messages by calling one of the following methods: * * * * * will be eligible to make use of Read Ahead, if the JMS Destination and the WebSphere MQ topic that the Destination maps to allows this functionality. Configuring the JMS Destination and WebSphere MQ to allow Read Ahead When an application uses the WebSphere MQ classes for JMS to subscribe to a WebSphere MQ topic, a managed subscription will be created. This managed subscription will either be durable or non-durable, depending upon how the application created the subscription. With managed subscriptions, the WebSphere MQ Publish/Subscribe Engine will create a managed queue for the application. Every time a message is published on the WebSphere MQ topic that the application has subscribed to, the WebSphere MQ Publish/Subscribe Engine will take a copy of that message

reportdate >= TODAY()?

The context mainly discusses technical issues, solutions, and updates related to Maximo, DB2, Oracle, Lotus Notes, and other software components. The context also includes APAR (Authorized Program Analysis Report) details, error descriptions, and temporary fixes for various reported issues.

To determine the data that has been registered today, it would be necessary to access the specific database or application where the data is stored and use appropriate query syntax to filter the data based on the registration date. The concept of `TODAY()` may or may not be directly applicable depending on the database technology and schema used for storing the data.

If you are working with Maximo, you may need to refer to the Maximo documentation or consult with the system administrators or developers familiar with the specific configuration and customization of Maximo in your environment to accurately retrieve the data that has been registered today.

- `E2.S1`: mqsireportproperties command single message flow mqsireportproperties command single message flow mqsireportproperties command single message flow; BIP2330E; mqsireportproperties; MessageFlow TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E2.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 How can I use mqsireportproperties command in IBM Integration Bus (IIB) or WebSphere Message Broker (WMB) to get information for a single message flow?
- `E2.S3`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
MessageFlow is a valid reportable entity name for the -o parameter, but the mqsireportproperties command does not have the functionality to allow the specifying of a message flow or uuid. Therefore it is not possible to request the properties for just a single message flow. 
For example: If you try to run the following command:
mqsireportproperties <brokername> -e <EGname> -o MessageFlow -r
- `E2.S4`: You would see the exception: BIP2330E MessageFlow does not exist
- `E2.S5`: As a workaround you could put one message flow in the execution group. Then report the properties for all messages flows in the execution group with the following commands:
- `E2.S6`: mqsireportproperties <brokername> -e <EGname> -o AllMessageFlows -a
mqsireportproperties <brokername> -e <EGname> -o AllMessageFlows -r

- `E3.S1`: datapower; retrieve; get; wsdl; web service proxy; web services proxy service; WSP; WS; GET method; GET; HTTP; HTTPS; front side handler; 7993; 7993; 7993; machine type 7993 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 You are looking to retrieve a WSDL from a Web Service Proxy service with the IBM WebSphere DataPower XS40 or XI50 appliance
- `E3.S3`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
A WSDL can be retrieved from a Web Service Proxy by allowing the GET method in the HTTP or HTTPS front side handler and going to the URL of the service including "?wsdl" for the query string such as:
- `E3.S4`: http://service:port/uri?wsdl
- `E3.S5`: By default, the GET method is disabled within a Web Service Proxy. If the GET method is not enabled, you will not be able to retrieve the WSDL from the URL.
- `E3.S6`: NOTE: When a WSDL contains include or import references to other documents, the WSDL that is output from DataPower will also contain include or import references. If you are unable to access your complete WSDL or if you find that something is missing when using this method, contact IBM Support [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21236322] for assistance with troubleshooting the problem.

- `E4.S1`: performance; JRules; DVS. Decision Warehouse; DWH; WODM; Decision Validation Services; improvement; Decision Center; Decision Server TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E4.S2`: QUESTION
 How can I improve the performance of Decision Validation Services (DVS) and Decision Warehouse?
- `E4.S3`: ANSWER
- `E4.S4`: Improving the performance of DVS testing and the Decision Warehouse involves reducing the size of the execution trace data generated during tests, and also some architectural and environmental configurations that might be suited to your use case. The following are recommendations you can consider incorporating:
- `E4.S5`: Reduce the size of the execution data:
- `E4.S6`: * Filter data [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21586717] using the ruleset properties: monitoring.filters and monitoring.inout.filters. 
 * Reduce the BOM serialization overhead:  * Override the toString() method for the ruleset parameters to return minimal information 
    * Set the ruleset property ruleset.bom.enabled to "false" to remove support for BOM based serialization. This property is set to "true" by default when extracting rulesets from Rule Team Server (RTS) and Decision Center, and needs to be explicitly set to "false" in order to deactivate it. (You should set it to "true" if you need to generate an Excel report from a Test Suite/Simulation in RTS.)
- `E4.S7`: Refer to the documentation Optimizing Decision Warehouse for v7.1.x or earlier [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global733.html] and WODM [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.res%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Rule_Execution_Server1571.html]. 
 * Reduce the number of columns in the Excel files by using the Ignore for DVS flag for the arguments in the DVS constructor, in Rule Studio [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global715.html] or Rule Designer [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.rulestudio%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Rule_Designer1303.html&resultof=%22Adding%22%20%22ad%22%20%22removing%22%20%22remov%22%20%22columns%22%20%22column%22%20%22from%22%20%22Excel%22%20%22excel%22%20%22file%22%20]. 
 * You can also choose to not write the traces to a database (Decision Warehouse) as shown in this sample [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21441394].
- `E4.S8`: Configure Decision Warehouse:  * Manage the production and test environments separately [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.overview%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Overview83.html], and use a different Decision Warehouse instance for each environment. 
 * Write asynchronously to Decision Warehouse:  * Using a JMS provider, such as WebSphere MQ or OpenJMS. 
    * Using MDBs or in batch using a ETL tool, such as Clover.ETL or Cognos ETL.
- `E4.S9`: * Perform an asynchronous update to Decision Warehouse, as shown in this sample [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global1781.html] for v7.1.x and earlier (and this sample [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.samples%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Samples588.html] for WODM). 
 * Capture the Decision Warehouse trace as an asynchronous operation in application servers supporting thecommonj WorkManager API, as shown in this sample [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21433167]. 
 * Estimate the database capacity [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21430461] that should be allocated.
- `E4.S10`: Refer to the documentation at Auditing executed decisions [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.overview%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Overview83.html] for detailed recommendations for configuring Decision Warehouse.
- `E4.S11`: Configure Rule Execution Server (RES):  * Do not use a production RES for your tests and simulations. Instead dedicate a separate RES instance for testing. 
 * Set the optimal XU and SSP pool sizes (in v7.1.x or earlier [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global206.html] and WODM [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dcenter.overview%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DC_Overview2884.html]). 
 * Increase the size of the database connection pool for the RES data source. 
 * Dedicate more processing resources to the handling of DVS tests:  * Deploy the SSP along with the RES console on a dedicated server. (By default tests are run on a single SSP, see Clustering Decision Validation Services [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21425487]). 
    * Otherwise, distribute the DVS tests [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21502095] on different RES instances.
- `E4.S12`: * Improve RES performance [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21589513].
- `E4.S13`: Configure Rule Team Server (RTS) or Decision Center:  * Install RTS and RES on separate computers.
- `E4.S14`: with the RES console on a dedicated server. (By default tests are run on a single SSP, see Clustering Decision Validation Services [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21425487]). 
    * Otherwise, distribute the DVS tests [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21502095] on different RES instances.
- `E4.S15`: * Improve RES performance [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21589513].
- `E4.S16`: Configure Rule Team Server (RTS) or Decision Center:  * Install RTS and RES on separate computers. 
 * Reduce the size of the Decision Warehouse trace when running scenario suites from RTS, as shown in this sample [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21438208]. 
 * Improve RTS performance [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21584855].
- `E4.S17`: Configure Rule Studio or Rule Designer:  * Increase the heap size for DVS testing [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21427125]. 
 * Improve Rule Studio or Rule Designer performance [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21589514].
- `E4.S18`: In addition, refer to the sections Enhancing the performance of Decision Warehouse and Enhancing the performance of Decision Validation Services in the IBM Redpaper: Proven Practices for Enhancing Performance: A Q&A for IBM WebSphere ILOG BRMS 7.1 [http://www.redbooks.ibm.com/redpapers/pdfs/redp4775.pdf]. - `E1.S1`: Password Passwords account lock lockout protection expiration timer TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E1.S2`: QUESTION
Does IBM Mobile Connect offer user account lockout protections or password lockouts? Yes.
- `E1.S3`: ANSWER
For complete instructions on how to install and perform an initial configuration on IBM Mobile Connect see technote 7043160 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg27043160]. For specific details on creating and configuring the resources discussed in this article see pages 6 - 9 of that same document.
- `E1.S4`: The first resource to be aware of is called the Wireless Password Policy. Why Wireless? It's a legacy thing, but really has nothing to do with something which is wireless.
- `E1.S5`: * Wireless Password Policy - Within the Gatekeeper under the Default Resources container you will find the Wireless Password Policies. There are 3 which are shipped with IMC, but as with any resource new ones could be created, or existing ones modified. This resource container was primarily used when the requirement was to have IMC local user accounts which required passwords. This resource allowed to specify the rules for passwords used to authenticate using local IMC system accounts. However, it is not common to use local IMC based system accounts, but rather to leverage existing user directories within LDAP or RADIUS servers. 
   The Wireless Password Policy still does offer a function which can be useful on a couple of fronts.  * User Account Lockouts and where they take place.
- `E1.S6`: [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21985055&amp;aid=1] 
    * The field "Number of failed connection attempts before lock" allows the IMC Administrator to specify how many failures to connect occur before IMC locks that account. 
    * It is important to understand how IMC counts failed connection attempts. In the above screen shot we have 5 failed connection attempts before lock. Traditionally that would lead one to believe that after 5 consecutive failed connections where the password was incorrect IMC would lock the account. That is not how this works. IBM Mobile Connect will ONLY count a connection attempt as FAILED if a unique password arrives on the request. That means that in order for IMC to lock an account locally the same user account would have to submit 5 requests which all had a different password. 
    * The reason that IMC operates this way is to implement another user account lockout feature and that is User Account Lockout at the Authentication Server level. It is desirable in most cases to prevent unnecessary calls from users into call centers to get their accounts unlocked in the company LDAP / RADIUS servers. To assist with this problem IMC will not resend a new request to an LDAP / RADIUS server for authentication on an account which IMC has received a return code indicating a bad password. If a new request has a different password after a failed attempt then it would go to the authentication server for validation.  * The use case here would be an IBM Verse or Connections Mobile app which has the log-in credentials stored in the app. The account password needs to be changed and is changed by the user on the company authentication server.
- `E1.S7`: the same known bad password. 
 * While the Lockout Protection is normally viewed as a positive thing, sometimes more control over the situation is desired. One use case would be where the End User successfully changes their password, but it may take X amount of time to become effective at the LDAP server. If that End User attempts to use the updated password immediately, IMC will get a failed login attempt return code from LDAP, and upon subsequent attempts which also use the same flagged incorrect password IMC will not return to LDAP. The End User is unaware of this, and if there were a configuration option allowing the same bad password counter to expire after a certain amount of time then end users might be educated that sometimes updated passwords may take some time to become effective, and IMC could still offer protection while allowing End User's with known good passwords to ultimately log in to their application via IBM Mobile Connect.
   In that case an administrator could use the Password Retry timeout (min) feature to lower the amount of time which made sense for their environment.
- `E2.S1`: performance; JRules; DVS. Decision Warehouse; DWH; WODM; Decision Validation Services; improvement; Decision Center; Decision Server TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E2.S2`: QUESTION
 How can I improve the performance of Decision Validation Services (DVS) and Decision Warehouse?
- `E2.S3`: ANSWER
- `E2.S4`: Improving the performance of DVS testing and the Decision Warehouse involves reducing the size of the execution trace data generated during tests, and also some architectural and environmental configurations that might be suited to your use case. The following are recommendations you can consider incorporating:
- `E2.S5`: Reduce the size of the execution data:
- `E2.S6`: * Filter data [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21586717] using the ruleset properties: monitoring.filters and monitoring.inout.filters. 
 * Reduce the BOM serialization overhead:  * Override the toString() method for the ruleset parameters to return minimal information 
    * Set the ruleset property ruleset.bom.enabled to "false" to remove support for BOM based serialization. This property is set to "true" by default when extracting rulesets from Rule Team Server (RTS) and Decision Center, and needs to be explicitly set to "false" in order to deactivate it. (You should set it to "true" if you need to generate an Excel report from a Test Suite/Simulation in RTS.)
- `E2.S7`: Refer to the documentation Optimizing Decision Warehouse for v7.1.x or earlier [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global733.html] and WODM [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.res%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Rule_Execution_Server1571.html]. 
 * Reduce the number of columns in the Excel files by using the Ignore for DVS flag for the arguments in the DVS constructor, in Rule Studio [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global715.html] or Rule Designer [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.rulestudio%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Rule_Designer1303.html&resultof=%22Adding%22%20%22ad%22%20%22removing%22%20%22remov%22%20%22columns%22%20%22column%22%20%22from%22%20%22Excel%22%20%22excel%22%20%22file%22%20]. 
 * You can also choose to not write the traces to a database (Decision Warehouse) as shown in this sample [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21441394].
- `E2.S8`: Configure Decision Warehouse:  * Manage the production and test environments separately [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.overview%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Overview83.html], and use a different Decision Warehouse instance for each environment. 
 * Write asynchronously to Decision Warehouse:  * Using a JMS provider, such as WebSphere MQ or OpenJMS. 
    * Using MDBs or in batch using a ETL tool, such as Clover.ETL or Cognos ETL.
- `E2.S9`: * Perform an asynchronous update to Decision Warehouse, as shown in this sample [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global1781.html] for v7.1.x and earlier (and this sample [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.samples%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Samples588.html] for WODM). 
 * Capture the Decision Warehouse trace as an asynchronous operation in application servers supporting thecommonj WorkManager API, as shown in this sample [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21433167]. 
 * Estimate the database capacity [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21430461] that should be allocated.
- `E2.S10`: Refer to the documentation at Auditing executed decisions [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.overview%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Overview83.html] for detailed recommendations for configuring Decision Warehouse.
- `E2.S11`: Configure Rule Execution Server (RES):  * Do not use a production RES for your tests and simulations. Instead dedicate a separate RES instance for testing. 
 * Set the optimal XU and SSP pool sizes (in v7.1.x or earlier [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global206.html] and WODM [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dcenter.overview%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DC_Overview2884.html]). 
 * Increase the size of the database connection pool for the RES data source. 
 * Dedicate more processing resources to the handling of DVS tests:  * Deploy the SSP along with the RES console on a dedicated server. (By default tests are run on a single SSP, see Clustering Decision Validation Services [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21425487]). 
    * Otherwise, distribute the DVS tests [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21502095] on different RES instances.
- `E2.S12`: * Improve RES performance [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21589513].
- `E2.S13`: Configure Rule Team Server (RTS) or Decision Center:  * Install RTS and RES on separate computers.

By delivering new functions and support for industry standards between product releases, you can more quickly explore and implement new technologies within your business applications in today's rapidly changing business environments.

- `E2.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 This technote explains why the IBM® Rational® Build Forge® Agent processes leave behind files in the TEMP directory on Microsoft® Windows®.
- `E2.S3`: SYMPTOM
- `E2.S4`: After a project run that performs a .bset or .retag, a number of 0-length files are left in the %TEMP% directory on the agent host.
- `E2.S5`: Directory of C:\DOCUME~1\user\LOCALS~1\Temp
- `E2.S6`: 06/03/2008 03:04 PM 0 bf2A0.tmp
06/03/2008 03:04 PM 0 bf2A2.tmp
06/03/2008 03:05 PM 0 bf2A4.tmp
06/03/2008 03:05 PM 0 bf2A6.tmp
06/03/2008 03:05 PM 0 bf2AA.tmp
06/03/2008 03:05 PM 0 bf2AC.tmp
06/03/2008 03:05 PM 0 bf2AE.tmp
06/03/2008 03:05 PM 0 bf2B1.tmp
06/03/2008 03:06 PM 0 bf2B3.tmp
- `E2.S7`: If these files build up for a while, they can lead to more severe agent failures due to Windows OS limitations, such as the following Agent error:
- `E2.S8`: ".retag encountered an error during variable expansion, value 'Check_${BF_SERVER}_${BF_BID}' expanded to 'AgentReadError'." 
command line error = "error 0 creating/accessing temporary file"
- `E2.S9`: CAUSE
- `E2.S10`: This is a resolved defect against the Build Forge Agent, APAR PK67083.
- `E2.S11`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
- `E2.S12`: This defect, APAR PK67083 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PK67083], has been resolved in Build Forge iFix3 for version 7.0.2 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?&rs=3099&uid=swg21254846]. The functionality now cleans up the files that are created in %TEMP%, but if this issue has already occurred, you will need to delete the files as detailed in the workaround.
- `E2.S13`: WORKAROUND:
- `E2.S14`: The upgrade prevents the problem from occurring, but it does not clean up files that have already been left in the %TEMP, and you will need to remove the files as detailed by this workaround.
- `E2.S15`: Delete all bf*.tmp files from %TEMP% on a regular basis. You may want to code a script to clear the %TEMP% directory on the agent host before or after each project run.

 *  Use imcl manually to install the fix as described here:

   Edition 7.1 fix package from PureApplication System maintenance

   https://developer.ibm.com/answers/questions/263001/why-am-i-unab [https://developer.ibm.com/answers/questions/263001/why-am-i-unab]

   https://developer.ibm.com/answers/questions/272058/installation- [https://developer.ibm.com/answers/questions/272058/installation-]
   manager-update-packages-dialog-does-n/
- `E2.S9`: To confirm that APAR IT14680 is the root cause of a problem
   where a fix is not listed properly on the Manage > Maintenance
   page:
- `E2.S10`: Confirm that Installation Manager lists the fix as available:
   - SSH onto the virtual machine where the fix needs to be applied
   - Update your SSH tool settings so that the commands you issue
     and their output are saved in a file
   - Issue the following commands
- `E2.S11`: sudo -u virtuser ./imcl listAvailableFixes <fix-name>
   -repositories http://IBMWorkloadDeployer:8585/IMRepository/Compo [http://IBMWorkloadDeployer:8585/IMRepository/Compo]
- `E2.S12`: where <fix-name> is the name of the fix to be applied, for
   example:
- `E2.S13`: sudo -u virtuser ./imcl listAvailableFixes
   com.ibm.websphere.liberty.ND.v85_8.5.5009.20160227_1546
   -repositories http://IBMWorkloadDeployer:8585/IMRepository/Compo [http://IBMWorkloadDeployer:8585/IMRepository/Compo]
- `E2.S14`: If an external Installation Manager Repository is also
   available, also issue
- `E2.S15`: sudo -u virtuser ./imcl listAvailableFixes <fix-name>
   -repositories http://<external-IM-repository> [http://<external-IM-repository>]
- `E2.S16`: where <fix-name> is the name of the fix to be applied, and
   <external-IM-repository>  is the URL for the external IM
   repository.
- `E2.S17`: Enable tracing to collect logs with fixpack calculation
   information included:
- `E2.S18`: - Select System > Workload Troubleshooting
   - Add a trace for
     "com.ibm.maestro.mgmt.resources.IfixMgmtResource"
   - Set the trace level to ALL
   - Recreate the problem
   - Wait 2 hours
   - Select System > Workload Troubleshooting again
   - Download All Logs
        (take care *not* to choose Download Latest Logs)
   - Provide the trace.zip file to IBM support
- `E2.S19`: To review the logs for information
   - Unzip trace.zip and look for servers.zip
   - Unzip servers.zip
   - Unzip the Kernel Services logs inside servers.zip
   - Review the Kernel Services logs for log entries from
     IfixMgmtResource.

- `E4.S3`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  Problem Description: Unable to manage LDAPx accounts. When
   loggin in as
   a regular ITIM user that manages an LDAPX account, you are
   unable to
   change the password and do other changes to the account even
   though an
   ACI is in place granting all permissions. In fact the account
   doesn't
   even show up under 'Manage Passwords' at all. To debug this
   issue both
   I and the customer ran DocTool and when we looked at the ACI for
   the
   LDAPX account type the only attribute given read/write
   permissions was
   'labeleduri'. Even though the GUI shows all permissions being
   granted.
   Customer Recreate: See steps below.
   Desired Behavior: That ACI permit ITIM users to manage their
   LDAPX
   accounts.
   Your Steps to Duplicate:
   1. Install LDAPX agent 4.5.5 build 4.5.1011
   2. Install profile on ITIM server. I recreated on 4.5.1 FP16
   IF19
   3. Go to 'My Organization'->'Control Access'. Then 'Add' a new
   ACI.
   4. Select 'Account' and then make the Customer Class '
   XLdapAccount'.
   6. IN the ACI make the scope 'Subtree', under operation grant
   everything
   and under 'Attribute Permissions' grant everything for read and
   write.
   7. Make sure "Allow Self' is set to 'Yes' and then save.
   8. Do recon to get accounts with the agent and then adopt orphan
   account
   to an ITIM user.
   9. Login as the ITIM user that adopted one of thes LDAPX
   accounts.
   10. You should not see the account under manage passwords, you
   may see
   it undermanage accounts.
   11. Run DocTool and then look at the info for the ACI you
   created.It
   will show that only the 'labeleduri' attribue has any
   permissions set.
   ITIM SERVER RELEASE: 4.5.1.5183
   Environment:
      Operating System  : Win2k/AIX5.2
      enrole/ITIM version  : enRole 4.5.1.5183
      interim release installed: IF19
      Database server   : DB2 8.1
      Directory server  : IDS 5.1
      WebServer         : WAS 5.02
      Java Version         : 1.3.1_06
      Other software?      : no
      Agent(s) installed?  : LDAPX 4.5.1011
   **********************************************
- `E4.S4`: LOCAL FIX
 *  s13213
- `E4.S5`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *   This is a documentation change for the ITIM
   Configuration Guide.  Please use the following information:
   The "CustomLabels.properties" in "$ITIM_HOME\Data" folder needs
   to be modified to correct this problem.  The LDAPX Agent has
   two password attributes, erpassword and userpassword.  Only one
   exists in the CustomLabels.properties file  To correct the
   problem, edit the CustomLabels.properties file in
   <ITIM_HOME>\Data" folder and find the line:
   userpassword=Password           and change that to:
   userpassword=User Password      also look for the line
   erpassword=Password             and ensure erpassword=Password
   Note: The solution shown above has been provided only for the
   English language. If a different language pack is installed on
   the system, then user needs to edit the
   words to accomodate the language used.
- `E4.S6`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *   The ITIM Configuration Guide will be updated
   to provide the configuration information needed.

- `E5.S1`: APM; V8.1.4; keystore; truststore; files; expired; expiring; upgrading; apmui; oidc; directory; certificate; server; installation TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E5.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 During the server upgrade processing from APM V8.1.3 to APM V8.1.4, the V8.1.3 APMUI certificate keystore and truststore files are copied to a new V8.1.4 location where they are shared by the APMUI, Server1, OIDC, and UViews servers. The default certificate contained in these files is set to expire on the 21st of April, 2019.
- `E5.S3`: SYMPTOM
How will I know if the default certificate has expired?
- `E5.S4`: When the certificate has expired, users will receive a "Secure Connection Failed" message in their browser instead of the APM Login Page.
- `E5.S5`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
To maintain valid UI certificates in your upgraded APM V8.1.4 server installations that are still using the default out of the box certificates, the existing keystore and truststore files must be replaced with the files that are attached at the end of this technote. These new keystore and truststore files contain certificates that are set to expire in March, 2028.
- `E5.S6`: The following new keystore files that are attached at the end of this technote contain certificates that will expire in 2028:
- `E5.S7`: 1. updated.8.1.4.key.jks (password: apmpass) 
2. updated.8.1.4.trust.jks (password: ccmR0cKs!)
- `E5.S8`: How do I know if I am using the default certificate files in an upgraded environment?
- `E5.S9`: 1. Identify an upgraded V8.1.4 default UI shared keystore by verifying the following:
- `E5.S10`: * The password is apmpass 
 * There is only a single certificate listed 
 * Alias is "default" 
 * Expires 4/21/19 
 * Signature Algorithm is SHA256withRSA 
 * Owner: CN=liberty, O=IBM, C=US and Issuer: CN=liberty, O=IBM, C=US

- `E5.S12`: 1.2. List the certificates in the key store by issuing the following command:

- `E5.S14`: Enter keystore password: ccmR0cKs!
- `E5.S15`: 2.3. Verify the output:
