- `E1.S2`: QUESTION
 Why am I receiving ABEND AKEA in IODM module EKCCMTOM at offset x'1A68' when trying to run in a CICS Version 3.3.0 region? The error occurs shortly after restarting IODM without the cycling region.
- `E1.S3`: In the CICS system initialization table (SIT), STGPROT is set to "No" and RENTPGM is set to NOPROTECT. System modifications (sysmods), UN54096 and UN60897, have been applied.
- `E1.S4`: ANSWER
Refer to authorized program analysis report (APAR) PN56650 for information about IODM module EKCCMTOM and program DFHZNEP. Set both programs to the EXECKEY parameter of CICS® and give them a datalocation value of "Any." Also, change the queue status field (QUESTAT) of the IDPARMTB table from 'E' to 'D'. The IDPARMTB table defines system-wide Object Distribution Manager parameters vital to the system's operation. Making this change frees you from relying on the use of the send queue processing operator commands, OAQM and OAQC, that are between OID1 and OID2. OID1 is the ImagePlus Object Distribution Manager first-stage, and OID2 the second-stage, shutdown CICS transaction. OID2 completes the Object Distribution Manager shutdown.
- `E1.S5`: The mode settings for program DFHZNEP state that DFHZNEP must be RMODE=any, AMODE=31. Relink your DFHZNEP as 31 bit so that DFHZNAC can link to ZNEP.
- `E1.S6`: When you relink DFHZNEP as 31 bit, expect to receive error message: IEW2646 for modules DFHZNEP, EKCCVECT, and EKCCFMSG. Error message: IEW2646I is issued when an RMODE value that is specified in the PARM statement is different than the one in the electrostatic discharge (ESD) record. Included is a binder message, which warns of a conflict. As a result, the RMODE value in the PARM statement will be used, based on the hierarchy specified in the Program Management Manual.
- `E1.S7`: You might get intermittent failures in OID1 in IODM module EKCCMTOM. Continue to try the failing transaction until you receive a normal completion.
- `E1.S8`: Another element to this error was revealed during its testing. The abend appears after cycling ODM but without cycling the CICS region. For example, you might first start the CICS region, then OIUP, OID1, OID2, OIUP, OID1 (which fails), OID2 (which also fails). By cycling the CICS region, the first OID1 and OID2 will function normally.
- `E1.S9`: In this situation, the second OIUP, which initializes the Object Distribution Manager, and all other functions (DISP and so on), function without incident.
- `E1.S10`: * If you use the LMODs from EKCPSTLK with the CICS330 libraries (instead of with the CICS211 libraries), OID1 and OID2 fail after the first shutdown of ODM. 
 * If you cycle the whole region, OID1 and OID2 work the first time after an OIUP. 
 * If you bring ODM up and then try to shut it down again, you will get the abends. 
 * With the CICS330 links, the failure is consistent. 
 * With the CICS211 links, the failure is intermittent. 
 * Additionally, with the CICS330 modules: 
 * DFHECI links clean 
 * error message: IEW2646I is not produced 
 * the offset of the abend moves about 8 bytes
- `E1.S11`: Note: The error described in this document was accompanied by error message: EKC0304A return code 8 reason code 00070017 after restarting IODM without a cycling region.
- `E1.S12`: * With the CICS330 links, the failure is consistent. 
 * With the CICS211 links, the failure is intermittent. 
 * Additionally, with the CICS330 modules: 
 * DFHECI links clean 
 * error message: IEW2646I is not produced 
 * the offset of the abend moves about 8 bytes
- `E1.S13`: Note: The error described in this document was accompanied by error message: EKC0304A return code 8 reason code 00070017 after restarting IODM without a cycling region. If you have an earlier release of IODM, see APAR PN14003 regarding the error message: EKC0304A 00070017.

- `E4.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 DataStage Parallel job fails with error message "too many open files" when running on Windows platform
- `E4.S3`: SYMPTOM
In the DataStage job log, error messages seen are:
- `E4.S4`: Item #: 867
Event ID: 2172
Timestamp: 2011-11-15 10:09:47
Type: Fatal
User Name: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
Message Id: IIS-DSEE-TOSO-00048
Message: APT_CombinedOperatorController(0),1: Fatal Error: Unexpected error in APT_TSort_ScratchFile::nextInputDescriptor: could not open file: E:\Data\DS_TEST\Scratchspace/tsortOggtbvxt; error: Too many open files
- `E4.S5`: Followed by the following error message a few entries later:
Item #: 873
Event ID: 2178
Timestamp: 2011-11-15 10:09:50
Type: Fatal
User Name: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
Message Id: IIS-DSEE-TOSO-00048
Message: APT_CombinedOperatorController(0),0: Fatal Error: Unexpected error in APT_TSort_ScratchFile::nextInputDescriptor: could not open file: E:\Data\DS_TEST\Scratchspace/tsort4qb08d3n; error: No such file or directory
- `E4.S6`: CAUSE
MKS Toolkit does not have sufficient free File Locks available for the number of DataStage jobs running on the Windows Server.
- `E4.S7`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
On the Windows Server, go to Start - Control Panel - Configure MKS Toolkit.
- `E4.S8`: Go to the Runtime Tab and select Category = Miscellaneous Setting.
- `E4.S9`: Under File Lock, check what has been set for "Max number of active file locks"
- `E4.S10`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
By default "Max number of active file locks" is set to 255. Increase this number to 300.
- `E4.S11`: Then click on the "OK" button. You will need to restart the Windows server for this change to take effect.

   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   Using the was_common_configure_sibus to read and
   subsequently write MQ links or SIB links was failing as
   was_common_configure_sibus uses AdminConfig to write data
   back to WAS when it should have been using AdminTask to
   perform the write back to WAS.
- `E1.S19`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  Properly capture SIB links and MQ links using
   was_common_configure_sibus in export mode.
   was_common_configure_sibus cannot be used in execute mode to
   write out the data, as AdminConfig is used instead of
   AdminTask, which is what should be used.  In order to write
   out the data base to WAS,
   was_common_configure_sibus_mq_links  or
   was_common_configure_sibus_sib_links  should be used
   instead, as they use AdminTask to write the data.

- `E3.S3`: ERROR DESCRIPTION

   command using lrcmd.[bat|sh] through the On-Demand Router (ODR),
   an IOException will be returned as follows:

   -xJCL=C:\SimpleCIxJCL.xml -port=<ODR port> -host=<ODR hostname>
- `E3.S5`: CWLRB4940I: com.ibm.ws.batch.wsbatch : -cmd=submit
   -xJCL=C:\SimpleCIxJCL.xml -port=<ODR port> -host=<ODR hostname>
- `E3.S6`: CWLRB4880E: -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\SimpleCIxJCL.xml -port=<ODR
   port>
   -host=<ODR hostname> failed:
              com.ibm.ws.batch.wsbatch: java.io.IOException:
   Connection
   close: Read failed.  Possible end of stream encountered.
- `E3.S7`: LOCAL FIX
 *  N/A
- `E3.S8`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: All users of WebSphere Extended Deployment   *
   *                 version 6.0.1.1.                             *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: When  attempting to issue a             *
   *                      long-running scheduler command using    *
   *                      lrcmd.[bat|sh] through the On-Demand    *
   *                      Router (ODR), an IOException will be    *
   *                      returned as follows:                    *
   *                                                              *
   *                      C:\IBM\WebSphere\AppServer\bin>lrcmd    *
   *                      -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\SimpleCIxJCL.xml   *
   *                      -port=<ODR port> -host=<ODR hostname>   *
   *                                                              *
   *                      CWLRB4940I: com.ibm.ws.batch.wsbatch :  *
   *                      -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\SimpleCIxJCL.xml   *
   *                      -port=<ODR port> -host=<ODR hostname>   *
   *                                                              *
   *                      CWLRB4880E: -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\Simple *
   *                      CIxJCL.xml -port=<ODR port>             *
   *                      -host=<ODR hostname> failed:            *
   *                      com.ibm.ws.batch.wsbatch: java.io.      *
   *                      IOException:Connection close: Read      *
   *                      failed.  Possible end of stream         *
   *                      encountered.                            *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   The problem was caused by assuming in the code the every SOAP
   request will have a web module with web service and operation
   node defined. Therefore for the cases where web service and
   operation nodes do not exist, trying to use the operation map
   to get a key results in a null pointer exception. To the
   caller this wrapped up exception shows up as an IO Exception.
- `E3.S9`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  For each SOAP over HTTP request, check for the definition of
   web service and web service operation nodes, if they exist use
   them to fetch the workclasses and perform further request
   classification as necessary, otherwise, use the original
   request mapping to route request.

- `E4.S2`: QUESTION
 Chapter 2 of Setting up your IBM WebSphere DataPower Appliance M/T 9235, 4195, 7199 and 7198.
- `E4.S3`: ANSWER
This technote is one of a series of technotes arranged in chapter format to provide information on setting up your IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance Machine Type 9235, 4195, 7199 and 7198
- `E4.S4`: Here are the links to the chapters:
- `E4.S5`: 1. Introduction to your WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance Machine Type 9235, 4195, 7199, and 7198 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21468463] 
 2. Planning for installation of your IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance MT/9235, 4195, 7199 and 7198 
 3. Planning worksheet for setting up your IBM WebSphere DataPower Appliance MT/9235, 4195, 7199 and 7198 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21468885] 
 4. Placing in the rack, initial configuration (with example) of your IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance M/T 9235, 4195, 7199, and 7198. [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21468886] 
 5. More on the initial configuration (startup command, manual configuration, and upgrading firmware (first time upgrade)) for your IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance. [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21469023] 
 6. Reviewing resources available from IBM to help you use your IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance. [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21469157] 
 7. Operations Planning [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21469163] 
 8. Working with IBM support to solve a problem when using your IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance. [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21469164]
- `E4.S6`: Chapter 2: Planning for installation of your IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Applaince Machine Type 9235, 4195, 7199 and 7198.
- `E4.S7`: Use the information in this section to help plan for adding the IBM WebSphere DataPower Appliance to your business network environment. We will cover the following planing steps:
- `E4.S8`: * Access to the Information Center. 
 * What you need to install the appliance in the rack or the cabinet

 * ADMIN PASSWORD Security 
 * Common Criteria Mode 
 * Secure Backup 
 * Network configuration 
 * Upgrading the firmware
- `E4.S9`: Access to the Information Center:

- `E4.S10`: What you need to install the appliance in the rack or the cabinet:  *

- `E4.S11`: What you need to configure and initialize the appliance:  *  A personal computer (PC) with:  * For a M/T 9235 on of the following:  * serial port connection 
       * docking station with a serial port connection, 
       * USB to serial port connection adapter
- `E4.S12`: * For a M/T 4195  * Either a concurrent-KVM (cKVM) or a Serial ove LAN (SOL) console connection
- `E4.S13`: * For a M/T 7199 or 7198  * Use the USB serial console cable (USB to RJ45) or DE-9 serial console cable (RJ45 to DB9) supplied with the appliance.
- `E4.S14`: The drivers for the USB to serial console cable provided with the appliance are on the IBM® WebSphere® DataPower SOA Appliances: Resource Kit CD in an archive file.
- `E4.S15`: The driver for Windows systems is in the driver/win/ directory. 
         The drivers for Mac OS systems are in the driver/mac/ directory.
         For driver installation instructions, see the readme file or Installation Guide in the archive file.

- `E4.S21`: ADMIN PASSWORD Security
- `E4.S22`: Do not misplace the new password for the admin account.
- `E4.S23`: A best practice is to secure the admin user id's password and set up back up privileged user ids. Several sections of this document describe how to set up a privileged user id. Do not copy and paste the password in to the DataPower serial connection or WebGUI. You might pick up extra characters and not be able to log in after you log out. DataPower devices are highly secure, tamper-resistant devices, often deployed within secure environments or deployed to meet high security standards. One of the Security features is the fact that we do not offer a non-authenticated / authorized appliance reset or password reset capability. In order to reset the appliance password, the appliance actually has to be re-imaged just like during the initial manufacturing process. We have one facility, a secure location in the United States, where this is done. When you receive the appliance after a password-reset, you must perform an initial setup and install the 
firmware you need and reconfigure the appliance. None of your configuration data will be on the appliance when it is returned, as this is a secure network appliance.
- `E4.S24`: Common Criteria Mode
- `E4.S25`: You would consider Common Criteria Mode when a specific authority requires the appliance to be EAL4 certified. To determine whether you will want to use Common Criteria Mode at initialization you should review the topics in the information center and this technote:
- `E4.S26`: Determining whether to use Common Criteria Mode at initialization. [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21388551]
- `E4.S27`: Secure Backup
- `E4.S28`: The information center has topics on secure backup. You can enter secure backup in the search box to see a list of topics. Developerworks has these 2 articles 
 * Secure backup-restore for WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliances [http://www.ibm.com/developerworks/websphere/library/techarticles/1009_furbee/1009_furbee.html]
- `E4.S29`: * Secure restore for WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliances [http://www.ibm.com/developerworks/websphere/library/techarticles/1006_majikes/1006_majikes.html]
- `E4.S30`: Network configuration
- `E4.S31`: Obtain the IP addresses and other network information to define the appliance to the network.  *  The IP address for the Ethernet interfaces for appliance management access (MGMT) and data traffic (ETH0, ETH1, ETH2, etc.). The IP address of the default gateways or routers that support the subnets for the Ethernet interfaces The IP address for the network services (SSH, Telnet, and so forth). A best practice is to configure the MGMT Ethernet interface on a dedicated subnet for all network and system-wide management functions.

- `E4.S1`: SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E4.S2`: SUMMARY
 OpenSSL vulnerabilities were disclosed on September 22 and 26, 2016 by the OpenSSL Project. OpenSSL is used by HP SSL on HP OpenVMS. IBM WebSphere MQ on OpenVMS Alpha and Itanium uses HP SSL and has addressed the applicable CVE ( CVE-2016-2183 ) known as “SWEET32 Birthday attack" .
- `E4.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
CVEID: CVE-2016-2183 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2016-2183]
DESCRIPTION: OpenSSL could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information, caused by an error in the in the Triple-DES on 64-bit block cipher, used as a part of the SSL/TLS protocol. By capturing large amounts of encrypted traffic between the SSL/TLS server and the client, a remote attacker able to conduct a man-in-the-middle attack could exploit this vulnerability to recover the plaintext data and obtain sensitive information. This vulnerability is known as the SWEET32 Birthday attack.
CVSS Base Score: 3.7
CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/116337 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/116337] for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)

The vulnerability affects version 6.0 of IBM WebSphere MQ on OpenVMS Alpha & Itanium.

- `E4.S6`: Product VRMF APAR Remediation/First Fix IBM WebSphere MQ on OpenVMS Alpha and Itanium.

On HP OpenVMS, IBM MQ V6.0.2.13 is a pre-requisite for applying the fix , refer to APAR IT18095 for additional details on the fix. WORKAROUNDS AND MITIGATIONS

- `E5.S1`: SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E5.S2`: SUMMARY
 OpenSSLプロジェクトから、OpenSSLの脆弱性が2016年9月22日、26日に公開されました。
IBM WebSphere MQ Advanced Message Security はIBM i プラットフォーム上でのみ、OpenSSLを使用しています。
このため IBM WebSphere MQ Advanced Message Security はこれらのCVEの影響を受けます。
- `E5.S3`: 最新の情報については下記の文書（英語）をご参照ください。 
Security Bulletin: Vulnerabilities in OpenSSL affect IBM WebSphere MQ Advanced Message Security (CVE-2016-2177, CVE-2016-2178)
http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21999724 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21999724]
- `E5.S4`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
- `E5.S5`: CVEID: CVE-2016-2177 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2016-2177] 
DESCRIPTION: OpenSSLはサービス拒否を引き起こす脆弱性を含んでいます。
これはヒープ・バッファーのバウンダリー・チェックで用いられる、ポインタ演算子の不正な利用によって引き起こされます。
予期しないmallocを使用することで、リモートの攻撃者はこの脆弱性を悪用してintegerのオーバーフローを引き起こし、アプリケーションをクラッシュさせることができます。
CVSS Base Score: 5.9
CVSS Temporal Score: 現時点のスコアは以下のサイトを参照してください。https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/113890 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/113890] 
CVSS Environmental Score*: 未定義
CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H)
- `E5.S6`: CVEID: CVE-2016-2178 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2016-2178]
DESCRIPTION: OpenSSLはDSA実装に含まれるエラーによって、リモート攻撃者に重要な情報を与えてしまう可能性があります。このエラーは特定の操作を不特定の時間に許すため、攻撃者はこの脆弱性を悪用してキャッシュタイミング攻撃を使用し、DSA秘密鍵を取得することが可能です
CVSS Base Score: 5.3
CVSS Temporal Score: 現時点のスコアは以下のサイトを参照してください。 https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/113889 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/113889]
CVSS Environmental Score*: 未定義
CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)

8.0.0.0 から 8.0.0.5 までの保守バージョンが影響を受けます。

- `E1.S2`: ABSTRACT
 This document describes how to download and install IBM Netcool Network Management V9.2 using the Passport Advantage website.
- `E1.S3`: DOWNLOAD DESCRIPTION
- `E1.S4`: Netcool Network Management provides network discovery and event and network management, including identification and resolution of root-causes and system, network, and service failures, and configuration management capabilities for network devices. Inventory and connectivity data is integrated with IBM Tivoli Netcool/OMNIbus event data. Network management staff can visualize and understand the layout of complex networks and the impact of network events and failures, and work with events to locate, diagnose, and solve network problems in real time.
- `E1.S5`: Netcool Network Management consists of the following products: IBM Tivoli Netcool/OMNIbus V7.4, IBM Tivoli Network Manager IP Edition V3.9, and IBM Tivoli Netcool Configuration Manager V6.4.
- `E1.S6`: More information
- `E1.S7`: The libraries of publications for the products in Netcool Network Management are available from this website: IBM Tivoli Network Management Information Center [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSNFET].
- `E1.S8`: Downloading and assembling the product
- `E1.S9`: 1. Navigate your browser to the Find Downloads and Media [http://www.ibm.com/software/howtobuy/passportadvantage/paocustomer/sdma/SDMA?PO=DOWNLOAD_FIND_BY_PART_NUMBER] page on the IBM Passport Advantage Online website. You must log on to continue. 
 2. Select the Find by part number search option under Download finder options. 
 3. Search for each downloadable image by part number (parts are listed and described by operating system in the tabbed section of this document). 
 4. Download all of the parts that you need.
 5. Unpack each of the parts into a single temporary directory on your system. If you want to install Tivoli Netcool/OMNIbus as part of the Network Manager installation process, you must download the Tivoli Netcool/OMNIbus installation package to a specific location and point the Network Manager installer to that location. Do not extract or rename the Tivoli Netcool/OMNIbus installation package.
 6. Open the Quick Start image and follow the instructions in the Quick Start Guide to install the base product.

- `E2.S1`: release notice; downloads; nco-p-socket-java; Socket Java Probe NEWS
- `E2.S2`: ABSTRACT
 The Netcool/OMNIbus Socket Java Probe will be available to download from December 10, 2015.
- `E2.S3`: CONTENT
- `E2.S4`: This is a new socket probe that can be configured to work in either Client mode or Server mode. In Server mode, the probe is a multiheaded probe that acts as a single process concurrent server which accepts multiple client connections. In Client mode, the probe connects to a socket to which a device writes its events.
- `E2.S5`: This probe has been created to address the following enhancement requests:
- `E2.S6`: * RFE 43179, RFE 50920, RFE 61527: A secure connection can be established using the new Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) feature. This probe supports TLSv1 protocol.
 * RFE 36469: The ParserElementDelimiter property now accepts Java Regular Expression, allowing users to specify multiple characters as delimiters. This enhancement is also applicable to the new ParserNVPDelimiter property to tokenize name-value pairs.
 * RFE 53841: The probe can now be configured to receive heartbeat messages to avoid entering into the Inactivity state.
- `E2.S7`: You can download the installation package from the IBM Passport Advantage website: 
www.ibm.com/software/howtobuy/passportadvantage/pao_customers.htm [http://www.ibm.com/software/howtobuy/passportadvantage/pao_customers.htm]
- `E2.S8`: You can access the latest version of the guide written for this probe on the IBM Knowledge Center:
- `E2.S9`: www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSSHTQ/omnibus/probes/socket_java/wip/concept/socket_java_intro.html [https://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSSHTQ/omnibus/probes/socket_java/wip/concept/socket_java_intro.html]
- `E2.S10`: Netcool/OMNIbus V8.1
- `E2.S11`: This probe is only supported on Netcool/OMNIbus V8.1. It is provided as a single package which contains versions of the probe for all supported Operating Systems. To obtain this new package, use the Find by part number field to search for part number: CN8BAEN
- `E2.S12`: Netcool/OMNIbus V7.4.0
- `E2.S13`: If you are running Netcool/OMNIbus V7.4.0, you must use the legacy Socket Probe (nco-p-socket-10_0). For details see 
www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21613418 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21613418]

- `E4.S2`: ABSTRACT
 This document describes how to download IBM Tivoli Network Manager IP Edition version 3.9 from the IBM Passport Advantage Online Web site.
- `E4.S3`: DOWNLOAD DESCRIPTION
- `E4.S4`: [http://www.ibm.com/i/c.gif] IBM Tivoli Network Manager IP Edition discovers networks, including layer 2 and 3 network devices, interfaces and connectivity. Network Manager also integrates topology and alert data with IBM Tivoli Netcool/OMNIbus so that operators can visualize and understand the layout of complex networks, and diagnose and solve network problems in real time.
- `E4.S5`: After logging into IBM's Passport Advantage Online [http://www.ibm.com/software/howtobuy/passportadvantage/pao_customers.htm] Web site, click Software download & media access, then click Download finder, then select Find by product description and type in Tivoli Network Manager. Expand the Tivoli Software eAssembly, and select the images you wish to download from that list. All Tivoli Network Manager IP Edition download images are described below.
- `E4.S6`: Downloading and assembling the product
- `E4.S7`: 1. Download all of the parts that you need, both required and optional. The parts are listed by operating system in the tabs below. 
 2. Unpack each of the parts into a single temporary directory on your system. If you want Network Manager to install IBM Tivoli Netcool/OMNIbus, do not rename the Tivoli Netcool/OMNIbus package.
 3. Follow the instructions in the Quick Start Guide to install the product.

## techqa_DEV_Q119#row-0077

Question:
Why does the Dataserver service change from Healthy to Vulnerable after logging into StoredIQ Application Stack? Why does the Dataserver service change from Healthy to Vulnerable after logging into StoredIQ Application Stack? 

Reference / gold answer:
The Dataserver service could change from Healthy to Vulnerable after logging into the StoredIQ Application Stack due to the amount of memory allocated to the dataserver. It is recommended to review the application status in the Dashboard tab, check the Controller link to confirm all services are running fine, and make changes to memory if necessary to address this issue.

Reference evidence:
- `1b`:  Why does the Dataserver service change from healthy to Vulnerable after logging into appstack? CAUSE
- `1d`: This could be due to amount of Memory allocated to the dataserver.  1.

- `E1.S2`: SUMMARY
 IBM WebSphere Application Server Liberty could allow a remote attacker to conduct phishing attacks, caused by an open redirect vulnerability. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to redirect a victim to arbitrary Web sites. IBM WebSphere Application Server Liberty is vulnerable to cross-site scripting in OpenID Connect clients caused by improper validation of input. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability using a specially-crafted URL to execute script in a victim's Web browser within the security context of the hosting Web site, once the URL is clicked. An attacker could use this vulnerability to steal the victim's cookie-based authentication credentials. There is an Information Disclosure Vulnerability in IBM WebSphere Application Server Liberty. Apache Commons Fileupload vulnerability affects WebSphere Application Server. There is a potential information disclosure in WebSphere Application Server. There are multiple vulnerabilities in the IBM® SDK Java™ Technology Edition that is shipped with IBM WebSphere Application Server. These issues were disclosed in the IBM Java SDK updates in July 2016. These may affect some configurations of Liberty for Java for IBM Bluemix.

These may affect some configurations of IBM WebSphere Application Server, IBM Business Process Manager, and IBM Tivoli System Automation Application Manager, which are shipped with IBM Cloud Orchestrator and Cloud Orchestrator Enterprise.

- `E2.S1`: SSL ; TLS/SSL; TLS 1.0; TLS 1.1; BEAST; Vulnerability; CVE-2011-3389 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E2.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 A known SSL/TLS vulnerability, CVE-2011-3389 (also known as BEAST), exists in the SSLv3 and TLS 1.0 protocols. To eliminate this vulnerability, please review the specific configuration recommendations below.
- `E2.S3`: SYMPTOM
Refer to CVE-2011-3389
- `E2.S4`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
The following describes how to prevent the CVE-2011-3389 vulnerability on any firmware version of the IBM WebSphere DataPower appliance.
- `E2.S5`: The protocol problem in this case is the use of a predictable IV (initialization vector) when block cipher CBC mode is used. There are two ways to prevent the attack.
- `E2.S6`: 1. use TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2
- `E2.S7`: The protocol problem that allows the attack was fixed completely starting in TLS 1.1 which changed the spec to use a new, random IV in each encrypted SSL record.
- `E2.S8`: DataPower firmware release 6.0.0 added support for TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 by default. To protect the appliance against the vulnerability enable support for TLS 1.1 and TLS 1.2 in the Crypto Profile while disabling support for TLS 1.0, SSLv3, and SSLv2.
- `E2.S9`: DataPower firmware releases prior to 6.0.0 do not support TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 and therefore must use option #2 below to avoid the vulnerability.
- `E2.S10`: 2. Enable the empty data record counter measure (CLI only)
- `E2.S11`: This counter measure can only be enabled using the command line interface (it is not available in the WebGUI).
- `E2.S12`: This counter measure is to send empty data records between the usual data records to effectively randomize the IV value. This behavior is legal according to the SSL/TLS specifications, but some SSL/TLS stacks are not fully compliant to this specification and will reject connections that send such records. Therefore use of this setting may result in incompatibility with SSL/TLS stacks that are not standards compliant such as the one in some versions of Microsoft Internet Explorer (IE).
- `E2.S13`: The Crypto Profile has a property called Options. Using the command line interface, set the Options field by entering crypto mode and using the profile command with an options mask of 0x10007FF:
- `E2.S14`: profile name idCred [ssl name] [ciphers cipher-string] [options mask]
- `E2.S15`: For example, a Crypto Profile named "alice-cp" uses an Identification Credential named "alice-idcred". The following CLI commands will enable the empty data record counter measure for this Crypto Profile:
- `E2.S16`: top
configure terminal
crypto
profile alice-cp alice-idcred options 0x10007FF
- `E2.S17`: This counter measure only protects one half of the duplex (outgoing data from DataPower). It is up to the SSL peer to protect the other half of the duplex with the same counter measure. If this is undesirable then use #1 or #3 instead.
- `E2.S18`: 3. Use SSL Server Profile or SSL SNI Server Profile with firmware version 7.2.0 or later
- `E2.S19`: In 7.2.0 release, IBM DataPower Gateways introduced SSL Server Profile and SSL SNI Server Profile. These 2 profiles are not vulnerable to this advisory, as they will always send empty data records between the usual data records.
- `E2.S20`: Cross reference information Segment Product Component Platform Version Edition Business Integration WebSphere DataPower B2B Appliance XB60 4.0.2, 4.0.1,
- `E2.S21`: Gateways introduced SSL Server Profile and SSL SNI Server Profile. These 2 profiles are not vulnerable to this advisory, as they will always send empty data records between the usual data records.

- `E4.S3`: APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
- `E4.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  MQ 5.3 for HP OpenVMS
   High CPU consumption is noticed while AMQZMGR0 process is
   monitoring its child processes such as command server, channel
   initiator, and listener processes.
   .
   The customer looked at the call stack, the stack shows it is
   looping as follows:
   .
    AMQZMGR0 -> MQMCS+0011CD60 -> waitpid() -> fchown()
   .
   There is no FDCs, no errors in AMQERR*.LOG, and no MQ trace
   files are generated when doing strmqtrc.
   .
   To recreate the problem, the customer executes strmqm as
   follows:
   .
      mqs_startup (Start MQ)
      crtmqm
      dspmqver
      strmqm
      ana/image  Check AMQZMGR0 ID and link date(Check build date)
      show system/proc=test* - List MQ processes
      mon proc/topc          - Show CPU 100%
      ana/sys SDA            - Show call stack information
- `E4.S5`: LOCAL FIX
- `E4.S6`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  On WMQ V6 on OpenVMS the process manager consumes high CPU even
   when queue manager is idle, while monitoring child processes.
   The queue manager works normally. When machine is loaded with
   tasks the CPU usage of the process manager comes down, because
   the system schedules other tasks. But anyway because of the
   high CPU intensive monitoring by the process manager some
   amount of CPU is always wasted.
- `E4.S7`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  WMQ has been modified so that the process manager does not do
   a CPU intensive monitoring of child processes.
   The fix for this APAR will be available through WMQ6.0 FP1
   IBM WebSphere MQ for HP OPENVMS Alpha V6.0 IC58895 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IC58895]
   IBM WebSphere MQ for HP OPENVMS Itanium V6.0 IC58896 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IC58896]

## techqa_DEV_Q267#row-0132

Question:
Can you enable the reporter feature with IBM Rational Rhapsody Architect Software Floating license? Can you enable the reporter feature with IBM Rational Rhapsody Architect Software Floating license? 

Reference / gold answer:
No, you cannot enable the reporter feature with the IBM Rational Rhapsody Architect Software Floating license. The reporter feature is part of the "Tools and Utilities" license key for IBM Rational Rhapsody, not the Architect Software Floating license.

- `E3.S12`: one limitation stay, if initializer contain generalization to
   template class the strig in the template  <> section must not
   contain the charcters   '>','<' (exept as template brackets)
   posible work around this limitations:
   - brackets around the template  expresions, exapmples:
   superclass<(template_expersion > 1)>(init_expression)
    superclass<<(expe1 >1)>,<(expe2 <1)>>(init expression)
   -use property CPP_CG::Operation::OrderedConstructorInitializer
   for correct none reorder code generation
   -use property
   CPP_CG::Operation::DisableAutoGeneratedInitializer
   for simpler code generation and Roundtrip of constructor
   initialaizer, in this case the initialazer is a simple string
   that copied as is from the initializer field to the code in code
   generation and to the model in roundtrip

   for correct none reorder code generation
   -use property

   for simpler code generation and Roundtrip of constructor
   initialaizer, in this case the initialazer is a simple string

- `E5.S6`: Error_description:
   Rhapsody slows down considerably after using for a few hours on
   Windows XP. The reason is analysed to the fact that it keeps
   occupying more and more memory after subsequent
   actions....Finally it reaches a stage when even simple actions
   such as performing an 'Add to Model' or moving the cursor takes
   2 minutes.
- `E5.S7`: Steps to Reproduce:
   Try1:
   I opened C++ model ?HomeAlarmWithPorts?. Memory used by Rhapsody
   = 17452 Kb.
   I open then OMD named: ?home alarm overview?. Memory used by
   Rhapsody = 27172 Kb.
   I close this OMD. Memory used by Rhapsody = 27160 Kb.
   I open again the same OMD (home alarm overview). Memory used by
   Rhapsody = 27204 Kb.
   I close again this OMD. Memory used by Rhapsody = 27164 Kb.
   I open again OMD named : home alarm overview. Memory used by
   Rhapsody = 27392 Kb.
   I close again this OMD. Memory used by Rhapsody = 27380 Kb.
- `E5.S8`: Try2:
   Tried to reproduce with a simple sample model and the results
   are more bad. Memory used shows as high as 47,000Kb while
   Rhapsody is launched..Opening a model shoots to 99,300 Kb.
   Closing the model brings it down to only 99,100Kb. Next time we
   open a model, it increases from 99,100 to 1,03,000 and so on...
- `E5.S9`: The cycle keeps increasing.
- `E5.S10`: This is potentially a big problem if huge models are opened.

   High risk for Rhapsody to crash.
   Decreases work efficiency.

## techqa_DEV_Q039#row-0060

Question:
How do I upgrade my virtual DataPower Appliance from 5.0 firmware to 6.0+ firmware? When attempting to upgrade my Virtual DataPower Appliance from 5.0.0.8 firmware version to 6.0+ firmware versions, I receive a failure message. 

Reference / gold answer:
To upgrade your virtual DataPower Appliance from 5.0 firmware to 6.0+ firmware, follow these steps:

1. If your virtual deployment is at the 5.0.0.8 firmware level, you must first upgrade to 5.0.0.8 or later fix pack before upgrading to 6.0.0.0 or later. The 5.0.0.8 fix pack contains critical fixes necessary for the upgrade.

2. Make sure that you have upgraded to the 5.0.0.8 fix pack or later before attempting to upgrade to 6.0.0.0 or later. 

3. Refer to the Critical Updates document for IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA appliances for guidance when migrating to a later firmware level.

4. Once you have upgraded to the required firmware level, you can proceed with upgrading to 6.0.0.0 or later. 

If you are experiencing failure messages during the upgrade process, refer to the troubleshooting steps provided in the context above. Additionally, you can reach out to DataPower Support for further assistance.

- `E1.S1`: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING) PROBLEM(ABSTRACT) How do I add the Application Optimization feature to an IBM WebSphere DataPower Type 9235 or Type 4195 appliance? The following document provides assistance on upgrading a DataPower Type 9235 or Type 4195 appliance to add the Option for Application Optimization feature. RESOLVING THE PROBLEM To add the Application Optimization feature: * The appliance must be a Type 9235 XML Security Gateway XS40 or Integration Appliance XI50 running firmware 3.7.3.0 or later or must be a Type 4195 Integration Blade XI50B running firmware 3.8.1.0 or later. Note: For Type 7199 appliances, see technote 1501194 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21501194]. * You purchased the feature and received a letter that contains the Controlled Access Key to download the firmware image. Part 1: Accessing the Web site that contains the firmware image. Using your IBM account and Controlled Access Key, access the web site to download the firmware image that contains the Application Optimization feature. 1. Identify the serial number for your appliance * From the WebGUI, click Status -> System -> Version Information. * From the command line, issue the show version command. 2. Follow the instructions in the Authorized Feature Download letter to access the WebSphere DataPower Registered Downloads portal [http://www.ibm.com/services/forms/preLogin.do?lang=en_US&source=swg-datapowerapps]. 3. Sign in using your IBM user ID and password. Register, if you do not have an ID. 4. Enter the Controlled Access Key in the letter to access the web page containing the firmware images. Ensure that the first 7-characters of the Controlled Access Key in the letter matches the serial number for the appliance that you obtained in step 1. You are now ready to continue to Part 2 to download the firmware image. Part 2: Downloading the firmware image. Determine which firmware image you need and download that image. Notes: * Starting with version 3.8.1, firmware that contain the MQ libraries do not contain .mq as part of its file name. * If you purchased the Option for Application Optimization feature after 10-June-2011, there is only a single image. Therefore, you do not need to identify libraries to determine which image to download. 1. Identify the library information for your appliance. - `E2.S1`: DOWNLOADABLE FILES
- `E2.S2`: ABSTRACT
 Download the IBM WebSphere DataPower XC10 Appliance Version 2.1 firmware upgrade. You can also download the client, which is required for WebSphere DataPower XC10 Appliance to work
- `E2.S3`: DOWNLOAD DESCRIPTION
This firmware release includes improved capability and new features for WebSphere DataPower XC10 Appliance Version 2.1.
- `E2.S4`: Caution: After you upgrade either 9235-92X or 7199-92X appliance types with Version 2.1 firmware, you cannot roll back to any previous firmware version. You must operate at the Version 2.1 or higher firmware level.
- `E2.S5`: When you are upgrading to Version 2.1, you cannot run a firmware upgrade on a collective that is currently servicing workload. When you upgrade a collective from a previous major version of DataPower XC10 Appliance, all of the data, not including your configuration, that was loaded into the data grids is lost. In addition, all members of the collective must be upgraded to the same major version (Version 2.1.0.x) before service can be restored. Upgrades between fix packs, for example, versions 2.1.0.0 to 2.1.0.1, can be done with no loss of service and while servicing workload as long as each appliance is upgraded individually and you wait for the upgraded appliance to reboot and re-replicate before proceeding to upgrade the next appliance. When you are running firmware upgrades on the appliances in a collective from a version prior to 2.1, the appliance that you upgrade does not fully restart until all of the appliances in the collective are upgraded to Version 2.1.
- `E2.S6`: You must complete the firmware upgrade process on one appliance before starting the process on another appliance within the collective. Do not make any configuration changes until all of the appliances are on the same firmware level. See Updating the firmware [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/wdpxc/v2r1/topic/com.ibm.websphere.datapower.xc.doc/aa/aat_updating_firmware.html] in the WebSphere DataPower XC10 Appliance Information Center, for more information.
- `E2.S7`: For IBM WebSphere DataPower XC10 Appliance to work with WebSphere Application Server or clients in a stand-alone environment, you must install the WebSphere eXtreme Scale Client or package the client Java archive (JAR) files with your application. You can download the client from this document as well.
- `E2.S8`: Client installation: If you have a previous version of the client, an upgrade is not available. Use IBM Installation Manager to install the full version of the client.

- `E4.S1`: SSL ; TLS/SSL; TLS 1.0; TLS 1.1; BEAST; Vulnerability; CVE-2011-3389 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E4.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 A known SSL/TLS vulnerability, CVE-2011-3389 (also known as BEAST), exists in the SSLv3 and TLS 1.0 protocols. To eliminate this vulnerability, please review the specific configuration recommendations below.
- `E4.S3`: SYMPTOM
Refer to CVE-2011-3389
- `E4.S4`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
The following describes how to prevent the CVE-2011-3389 vulnerability on any firmware version of the IBM WebSphere DataPower appliance.
- `E4.S5`: The protocol problem in this case is the use of a predictable IV (initialization vector) when block cipher CBC mode is used. There are two ways to prevent the attack.
- `E4.S6`: 1. use TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2
- `E4.S7`: The protocol problem that allows the attack was fixed completely starting in TLS 1.1 which changed the spec to use a new, random IV in each encrypted SSL record.
- `E4.S8`: DataPower firmware release 6.0.0 added support for TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 by default. To protect the appliance against the vulnerability enable support for TLS 1.1 and TLS 1.2 in the Crypto Profile while disabling support for TLS 1.0, SSLv3, and SSLv2.
- `E4.S9`: DataPower firmware releases prior to 6.0.0 do not support TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 and therefore must use option #2 below to avoid the vulnerability.
- `E4.S10`: 2. Enable the empty data record counter measure (CLI only)
- `E4.S11`: This counter measure can only be enabled using the command line interface (it is not available in the WebGUI).
- `E4.S12`: This counter measure is to send empty data records between the usual data records to effectively randomize the IV value. This behavior is legal according to the SSL/TLS specifications, but some SSL/TLS stacks are not fully compliant to this specification and will reject connections that send such records. Therefore use of this setting may result in incompatibility with SSL/TLS stacks that are not standards compliant such as the one in some versions of Microsoft Internet Explorer (IE).
- `E4.S13`: The Crypto Profile has a property called Options. Using the command line interface, set the Options field by entering crypto mode and using the profile command with an options mask of 0x10007FF:
- `E4.S14`: profile name idCred [ssl name] [ciphers cipher-string] [options mask]
- `E4.S15`: For example, a Crypto Profile named "alice-cp" uses an Identification Credential named "alice-idcred". The following CLI commands will enable the empty data record counter measure for this Crypto Profile:
- `E4.S16`: top
configure terminal
crypto
profile alice-cp alice-idcred options 0x10007FF
- `E4.S17`: This counter measure only protects one half of the duplex (outgoing data from DataPower). It is up to the SSL peer to protect the other half of the duplex with the same counter measure. If this is undesirable then use #1 or #3 instead.
- `E4.S18`: 3. Use SSL Server Profile or SSL SNI Server Profile with firmware version 7.2.0 or later
- `E4.S19`: In 7.2.0 release, IBM DataPower Gateways introduced SSL Server Profile and SSL SNI Server Profile. These 2 profiles are not vulnerable to this advisory, as they will always send empty data records between the usual data records.

- `E2.S4`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
To add the Application Optimization feature:
- `E2.S5`: * The appliance must be a Type 9235 XML Security Gateway XS40 or Integration Appliance XI50 running firmware 3.7.3.0 or later or must be a Type 4195 Integration Blade XI50B running firmware 3.8.1.0 or later.
   Note: For Type 7199 appliances, see technote 1501194 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21501194]. 
 * You purchased the feature and received a letter that contains the Controlled Access Key to download the firmware image.
- `E2.S6`: Part 1: Accessing the Web site that contains the firmware image. 
Using your IBM account and Controlled Access Key, access the web site to download the firmware image that contains the Application Optimization feature. 
 1. Identify the serial number for your appliance  * From the WebGUI, click Status -> System -> Version Information. 
     * From the command line, issue the show version command.
- `E2.S7`: 2. Follow the instructions in the Authorized Feature Download letter to access the WebSphere DataPower Registered Downloads portal [http://www.ibm.com/services/forms/preLogin.do?lang=en_US&source=swg-datapowerapps]. 
 3. Sign in using your IBM user ID and password. Register, if you do not have an ID. 
 4. Enter the Controlled Access Key in the letter to access the web page containing the firmware images. Ensure that the first 7-characters of the Controlled Access Key in the letter matches the serial number for the appliance that you obtained in step 1.
- `E2.S8`: You are now ready to continue to Part 2 to download the firmware image.
- `E2.S9`: Part 2: Downloading the firmware image. 
Determine which firmware image you need and download that image.

 * If you purchased the Option for Application Optimization feature after 10-June-2011, there is only a single image. Therefore, you do not need to identify libraries to determine which image to download.

     * From the command line, issue the show library-version command.
- `E2.S12`: 2. Download the image that corresponds to the available libraries on your appliance. For example:  * Download xs3800.tam6.scrypt2 if your XML Security Gateway XS40 has TAM 6.0

Additionally, it affects Jazz for Service Management and IBM Tivoli Monitoring, which are shipped with Cloud Orchestrator Enterprise. Question:
Help with Security Bulletin: TLS padding vulnerability affects IBM PureApplication System (CVE-2014-8730) I need to understand details regarding "Security Bulletin: TLS padding vulnerability affects IBM PureApplication System (CVE-2014-8730)". Where can I find this information? 

Reference / gold answer:
You can find detailed information about the "Security Bulletin: TLS padding vulnerability affects IBM PureApplication System (CVE-2014-8730)" in the provided context above. It includes a summary of the vulnerability, vulnerability details, affected products and versions, remediation/fixes, workarounds and mitigations, references, related information, acknowledgements, change history, and disclaimer.

Reference evidence:
- `2a`:  SECURITY BULLETIN SUMMARY
- `2b`:  Transport Layer Security (TLS) padding vulnerability via a POODLE (Padding Oracle On Downgraded Legacy Encryption) like attack affects IBM PureApplication System. VULNERABILITY DETAILS
- `2c`: CVEID: CVE-2014-8730 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2014-8730]
- `2d`: DESCRIPTION: IBM PureApplication Server bundles IBM HTTP Server, which could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information, caused by the failure to check the contents of the padding bytes when using CBC cipher suites of some TLS implementations.
- `2e`: A remote user with the ability to conduct a man-in-the-middle attack could exploit this vulnerability via a POODLE (Padding Oracle On Downgraded Legacy Encryption) like attack to decrypt sensitive information and calculate the plain text of secure connections.
- `2f`: CVSS Base Score: 4.3

- `E3.S2`: SUMMARY

- `E3.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
The affected products are shipped with a version of IBM WebSphere Application Server, which is shipped with an IBM SDK Java Technology Edition and is based on the Oracle Java Development Kit (JDK). Oracle has released the January 2014 critical patch updates (CPU), which contain security vulnerability fixes. The IBM SDK for Java Technology Edition has been updated to incorporate the critical patch updates.
The following vulnerabilities are applicable to IBM WebSphere Application Server and for the affected product.

- `E5.S2`: SUMMARY
 IBM Tivoli Monitoring is shipped as a component of IBM Cloud Orchestrator Enterprise and IBM SmartCloud Orchestrator Enterprise. Information about security vulnerabilities affecting IBM Tivoli Monitoring has been published in the security bulletins below.
- `E5.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
Consult the following security bulletins for IBM Tivoli Monitoring for vulnerability details and information about fixes.

=== CANDIDATE B ===

Model-visible evidence:
- `E1.S1`: SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E1.S2`: SUMMARY
 IBM PureApplication System contains IBM WebSphere Application Server, which has a security vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code by connecting to a management port and executing a specific sequence of instructions.
- `E1.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
CVEID: CVE-2015-1920 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2015-1920]
DESCRIPTION: WebSphere Application Server could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code by connecting to a management port and executing a specific sequence of instructions.
CVSS Base Score: 9.3
CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/102404 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/102404] for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:C/I:C/A:C)
- `E1.S4`: Please consult the security bulletin: Security Vulnerability in IBM WebSphere Application Server [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21883573]for additional vulnerability details and information
- `E1.S5`: AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND VERSIONS
IBM PureApplication Server bundles WebSphere Application Server in its Web Application Pattern.
- `E1.S6`: IBM PureApplication System V2.1
IBM PureApplication System V2.0
IBM PureApplication System V1.1
- `E1.S7`: REMEDIATION/FIXES
The solution is to apply an update to the Web Application pattern type included in IBM PureApplication System:
- `E1.S8`: IBM PureApplication System V2.1
· Web Application Pattern Type V2.0.4.2
http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/quickorder?parent=PureSystems&product=ibm/WebSphere/PureApplication+System&release=All&platform=All&function=fixId&fixids=webapp-2.0.4.2-sys&includeSupersedes=0&source=fc [http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/quickorder?parent=PureSystems&product=ibm/WebSphere/PureApplication+System&release=All&platform=All&function=fixId&fixids=webapp-2.0.4.2-sys&includeSupersedes=0&source=fc]
- `E1.S9`: · Web Application Pattern Type V1.0.4.2
http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/quickorder?parent=PureSystems&product=ibm/WebSphere/PureApplication+System&release=All&platform=All&function=fixId&fixids=webapp-1.0.4.2-sys&includeSupersedes=0&source=f [http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/quickorder?parent=PureSystems&product=ibm/WebSphere/PureApplication+System&release=All&platform=All&function=fixId&fixids=webapp-1.0.4.2-sys&includeSupersedes=0&source=f]
- `E1.S10`: IBM PureApplication System V2.0 
The solution is to upgrade to IBM PureApplication System V2.0.0.1 Interim Fix 5
- `E1.S11`: IBM PureApplication System V1.1 and earlier:
Contact IBM customer support for upgrade options.
- `E1.S12`: WORKAROUNDS AND MITIGATIONS
None

- `E2.S1`: SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E2.S2`: SUMMARY
 Log viewer vulnerability affects IBM PureApplication System.
- `E2.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
CVEID: CVE-2014-6190 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2014-6190]
DESCRIPTION: 
Defined system users without proper permissions can access the log viewer functionality by entering the log page URLs in their browser.
- `E2.S4`: CVSS Base Score: 5.0
CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/98561 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/98561] for the current score

CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:L/Au:N/C:P/I:N/A:N)

The PureSystems Managers on all IBM PureApplication Systems types are affected. Upgrade the IBM PureApplication System to the following interim fix levels:

   Upgrade to IBM PureApplication System V1.0.0.4 Interim Fix 11
- `E2.S9`: * IBM PureApplication System V1.1
   Upgrade to IBM PureApplication System V1.1.0.5 Interim Fix1
- `E2.S10`: * IBM PureApplication System V2.0
   Upgrade to IBM PureApplication System V2.0.0.1

- `E3.S2`: SUMMARY
 IBM Tivoli Monitoring is shipped as a component of IBM Cloud Orchestrator Enterprise and IBM SmartCloud Orchestrator Enterprise. Information about security vulnerabilities affecting IBM Tivoli Monitoring has been published in the security bulletins below.
- `E3.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
Consult the following security bulletins for IBM Tivoli Monitoring for vulnerability details and information about fixes.
- `E3.S4`: * Security Bulletin: Vulnerability in IBM Java SDK affect IBM Tivoli Monitoring (CVE-2015-7575)
- `E3.S5`: * Security Bulletin: Vulnerability in RC4 stream cipher affects IBM Tivoli Monitoring (CVE-2015-2808) [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21883223]
- `E3.S6`: * Security Bulletin: Vulnerability in IBM Java Runtime affects IBM Tivoli Monitoring (CVE-2015-0138) [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21701519]
- `E3.S7`: * Security Bulletin: A security vulnerabilities has been identified in Websphere Application Server shipped with Jazz for Service Management (CVE-2016-0306) [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21981087]
- `E3.S8`: * Security Bulletin: IBM Tivoli Monitoring Privileges Escalation through Authorization Bypass (CVE-2015-7411) [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21973559] 
 *  Security Bulletin: A vulnerability in the GSKit component of IBM Tivoli Monitoring (CVE-2016-0201) [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21976125]
- `E3.S9`: * Security Bulletin: IBM Tivoli Monitoring Remote Code Execution (CVE-2015-5003) [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21970361]

- `E4.S1`: SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E4.S2`: SUMMARY

- `E4.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
Please consult the security bulletins for IBM WebSphere Application Server published at

 * Security Bulletin: Vulnerability in RC4 stream cipher affects WebSphere Application Server (CVE-2015-2808) [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21701503] 
 * Security Bulletin: Multiple vulnerabilities in IBM® Java SDK affect WebSphere Application Server April 2015 CPU [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21902260]

 * Security Bulletin: Vulnerability with RSA Export Keys may affect IBM HTTP Server and WebSphere EDGE Caching Proxy (CVE-2015-0138) [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21698959] 
 * Security Bulletin: Vulnerability in Dojo Toolkit affect WebSphere Application Server (CVE-2014-8917) [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21697284]

- `E5.S1`: SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E5.S2`: SUMMARY
 There are multiple vulnerabilities in IBM® SDK Java™ Technology Edition that is used by WebSphere Application Server underneath IBM Business Process Manager and WebSphere Lombardi Edition. These issues were disclosed as part of the IBM SDK Java™ Technology Edition updates in January 2015. This bulletin also addresses the “FREAK: Factoring Attack on RSA-EXPORT keys" TLS/SSL client and server vulnerability.
- `E5.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
CVEID: CVE-2015-0138 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2015-0138]
DESCRIPTION: A vulnerability in various IBM SSL/TLS implementations could allow a remote attacker to downgrade the security of certain SSL/TLS connections. An IBM SSL/TLS client implementation could accept the use of an RSA temporary key in a non-export RSA key exchange ciphersuite. This could allow a remote attacker using man-in-the-middle techniques to facilitate brute-force decryption of TLS/SSL traffic between vulnerable clients and servers.
- `E5.S4`: This vulnerability is also known as the FREAK attack.
- `E5.S5`: CVSS Base Score: 4.3
CVSS Temporal Score: See http://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/#/vulnerabilities/100691 [http://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/#/vulnerabilities/100691] for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:N/I:P/A:N)
- `E5.S6`: CVEID: CVE-2014-6593 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2014-6593]
DESCRIPTION: An unspecified vulnerability related to the JSSE component has partial confidentiality impact, partial integrity impact, and no availability impact.
CVSS Base Score: 4
CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/100153 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/100153] for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:H/Au:N/C:P/I:P/A:N)
- `E5.S7`: CVEID: CVE-2015-0400 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2015-0400]
DESCRIPTION: An unspecified vulnerability related to the Libraries component could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information.
CVSS Base Score: 5
CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/100149 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/100149] for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:L/Au:N/C:P/I:N/A:N)
- `E5.S8`: CVEID: CVE-2015-0410 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2015-0410]
DESCRIPTION: An unspecified vulnerability related to the Security component could allow a remote attacker to cause a denial of service.
CVSS Base Score: 5
CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/100151 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/100151] for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:L/Au:N/C:N/I:N/A:P)
- `E5.S9`: AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND VERSIONS
- `E5.S10`: * IBM Business Process Manager V7.5.x through V8.5.6.0 
 * WebSphere Lombardi Edition V7.2.0.x
- `E5.S11`: For earlier unsupported versions of the products, IBM recommends upgrading to a fixed, supported version of the product. REMEDIATION/FIXES
IBM SDK Java™ Technology Edition is used in WebSphere Application Server. See the following two security bulletins for vulnerability details and information about fixes.
- `E5.S12`: * Security Bulletin: Vulnerability with RSA Export Keys may affect IBM WebSphere Application Server (CVE-2015-0138) [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21698613] 
 * Security Bulletin: Multiple vulnerabilities in IBM Java SDK affect WebSphere Application Server January 2015 CPU [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21695362]
- `E5.S13`: IBM SDK Java™ Technology Edition is also used in IBM Process Designer. Install the interim fix for APAR IT07386 for your current version of IBM Business Process Manager or WebSphere Lombardi Edition. 
 * IBM Business Process Manager Express [http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/quickorder?parent=ibm%7EWebSphere&product=ibm/WebSphere/IBM+Business+Process+Manager+Express&release=All&platform=All&function=aparId&apars=IT07386] 
 * IBM Business Process Manager Standard [http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/quickorder?parent=ibm%7EWebSphere&product=ibm/WebSphere/IBM+Business+Process+Manager+Standard&release=All&platform=All&function=aparId&apars=IT07386] 
 * IBM Business Process Manager Advanced [http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/quickorder?parent=ibm%7EWebSphere&product=ibm/WebSphere/IBM+Business+Process+Manager+Advanced&release=All&platform=All&function=aparId&apars=IT07386] 
 * WebSphere Lombardi Edition [http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/selectFixes?parent=ibm~WebSphere&product=ibm/WebSphere/WebSphere+Lombardi+Edition&release=All&platform=All&function=aparId&apars=IT07386]
- `E5.S14`: If you are on earlier unsupported releases, IBM strongly recommends to upgrade. WORKAROUNDS AND MITIGATIONS
None

## techqa_DEV_Q237#row-0031

Question:
Traffic across domains seems unexpected 

I have two Multi-Protocol Gateways (MPGWs) configured, each in their own domain:

     Domain A
     MPGW_A
     FSH_A (1.2.3.4:443)
     Domain B
     MPGW_B
     FSH_B (0.0.0.0:443)

The FSH_B is disabled, thus MPGW_B cannot take traffic. However, if I modify the config for MPGW_B (i.e. just change a Stylesheet parameter) the traffic goes to MPGW_B somehow. How is this happening? FSH_B is still disabled.

Reference / gold answer:
Based on the given context, the unexpected traffic across domains could be happening due to the configuration of cross-certification between the two domains. In the context provided, it mentions setting up cross-certification for user access and replication. 

If there is cross-certification set up between Domain A and Domain B for user access, it is possible that this cross-certification is allowing traffic to flow from Domain A to Domain B, even if the FSH_B is disabled in MPGW_B. 

To investigate further, you may need to review the cross-certification setup between the two domains and ensure that it is configured only for user access in one direction as intended. Additionally, checking the configuration of the MPGWs and the traffic routing rules within the domains may also provide insights into how the traffic is being redirected to MPGW_B despite FSH_B being disabled.

- `E3.S1`: SSL ; TLS/SSL; TLS 1.0; TLS 1.1; BEAST; Vulnerability; CVE-2011-3389 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 A known SSL/TLS vulnerability, CVE-2011-3389 (also known as BEAST), exists in the SSLv3 and TLS 1.0 protocols. To eliminate this vulnerability, please review the specific configuration recommendations below.
- `E3.S3`: SYMPTOM
Refer to CVE-2011-3389
- `E3.S4`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
The following describes how to prevent the CVE-2011-3389 vulnerability on any firmware version of the IBM WebSphere DataPower appliance.
- `E3.S5`: The protocol problem in this case is the use of a predictable IV (initialization vector) when block cipher CBC mode is used. There are two ways to prevent the attack.
- `E3.S6`: 1. use TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2
- `E3.S7`: The protocol problem that allows the attack was fixed completely starting in TLS 1.1 which changed the spec to use a new, random IV in each encrypted SSL record.
- `E3.S8`: DataPower firmware release 6.0.0 added support for TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 by default. To protect the appliance against the vulnerability enable support for TLS 1.1 and TLS 1.2 in the Crypto Profile while disabling support for TLS 1.0, SSLv3, and SSLv2.
- `E3.S9`: DataPower firmware releases prior to 6.0.0 do not support TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 and therefore must use option #2 below to avoid the vulnerability.
- `E3.S10`: 2. Enable the empty data record counter measure (CLI only)
- `E3.S11`: This counter measure can only be enabled using the command line interface (it is not available in the WebGUI).
- `E3.S12`: This counter measure is to send empty data records between the usual data records to effectively randomize the IV value. This behavior is legal according to the SSL/TLS specifications, but some SSL/TLS stacks are not fully compliant to this specification and will reject connections that send such records. Therefore use of this setting may result in incompatibility with SSL/TLS stacks that are not standards compliant such as the one in some versions of Microsoft Internet Explorer (IE).
- `E3.S13`: The Crypto Profile has a property called Options. Using the command line interface, set the Options field by entering crypto mode and using the profile command with an options mask of 0x10007FF:
- `E3.S14`: profile name idCred [ssl name] [ciphers cipher-string] [options mask]
- `E3.S15`: For example, a Crypto Profile named "alice-cp" uses an Identification Credential named "alice-idcred". The following CLI commands will enable the empty data record counter measure for this Crypto Profile:
- `E3.S16`: top
configure terminal
crypto
profile alice-cp alice-idcred options 0x10007FF
- `E3.S17`: This counter measure only protects one half of the duplex (outgoing data from DataPower). It is up to the SSL peer to protect the other half of the duplex with the same counter measure. If this is undesirable then use #1 or #3 instead.
- `E3.S18`: 3. Use SSL Server Profile or SSL SNI Server Profile with firmware version 7.2.0 or later
- `E3.S19`: In 7.2.0 release, IBM DataPower Gateways introduced SSL Server Profile and SSL SNI Server Profile. These 2 profiles are not vulnerable to this advisory, as they will always send empty data records between the usual data records.
- `E3.S20`: Cross reference information Segment Product Component Platform Version Edition Business Integration WebSphere DataPower B2B Appliance XB60 4.0.2, 4.0.1,

- `E4.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  DB2 Versions 10.1 Fix Pack 5 (APAR IT05851 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IT05851]), 10.5 Fix Pack 7
   (IT06005 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IT06005]), and 11.1 GA introduced a behavior change in the way
   asynchronous write time is accumulated.  Asynchronous writes are
   submitted in large batches using asynchronous I/O services/APIs
   provided by an operating system.  The approximate previous
   behavior apportioned a pagecleaner EDU's I/O wait time evenly
   across all pages in a batch.  For example, if a batch of 10 I/O
   requests took 10ms to complete, each I/O request/page write
   would be assigned 1ms of the overall 10ms time.
- `E4.S5`: In many cases the apportionment approach masks underlying
   response time issues, and a change was made in the
   above-mentioned DB2 levels to stop splitting a pagecleaner's
   wait time across all pages written, and instead assign the
   entire batch time to each page write request.  In the case where
   a batch of 10 I/O requests took 10ms to complete each "page
   write" would be assigned the full 10ms.  While there is some
   value in providing this information, as it may more accurately
   reflect I/O response time in some storage configurations, it can
   also cause unnecessary concern.  This is due to the much higher
   calculated average asynchronous page write time, which bubbles
   up to overall average page write time.  It is reasonable that a
   large batch of I/Os may incur some overhead and take longer than
   a single I/O, thus the higher reported time may not be a good
   indicator of underlying I/O performance.  In addition, the wait
   time for pagecleaner write activity does not typically impact
   the time a db2agent EDU spends servicing application requests.
   As such, this APAR fix will revert to the former behaviour of
   splitting pagecleaner I/O wait time across the pages involved in
   a batch of asynchronous I/O requests.

- `E5.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  You are running CICS 5.2 and have a CICS IPIC connection
   stuck in Freeing state. It never goes into Released state, and
   the region must be recycled to clear.
   A dump at the time the connection was in freeing state, shows
   a Tran number associated with an IPIC session, but this task is
   no longer in the system.  It issued the following message:
   DFHIS1025 APPLID Failed to attach mirror transaction xxxx on
            IPCONN IPIC. Error code is X'0619'
   This task tried to send an error response back to the client,
   but
   fails due to the connection being closed.
   There is a problem in this scenario, where we do not
   free up the session control block- ISSB. This leaves it on the
   active chain, preventing the IPCONN from ever getting to
   RELEASED
   state.
   Additional Symptom(s) Search Keyword(s): KIXREVEPH
- `E5.S5`: LOCAL FIX
- `E5.S6`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED:                                              *
   * All CICS users.                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION:                                         *
   * IPCONN remain in FREEing state after a                       *
   * mirror transaction failed to attach                          *
   * because it was disable.                                      *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   * .                                                            *
   ****************************************************************
   CICS region A and region B are connected via IPIC. The IPCONN is
   in ACQUIRE status. Region A send a DPL request to region B.
   The mirror transaction in region B is disabled. Transaction CSAC
   get attached instead of the mirror transaction. DFHACP attempt
   to send an IS7 with sense code 084C0000 with message DFHIS1025
   to region A. The send failed because the IPIC socket has been
   closed. The CSAC transaction terminates without FREEing the
   receive ISSB that was allocated to the task.
   .
   The SOCKET closed causes transaction CIST to be attached to
   release the IPCONN. During the IPCONN termination the orphan
   ISSB is found causing the IPCONN to remain in FREEing state.
- `E5.S7`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  DFHISZA and DFHISIS have been changed to ensure that the receive
   ISSB used to send an IS7 response to the client region is FREE
   when socket domain returned an exception.

=== CANDIDATE B ===

Model-visible evidence:
- `E1.S1`: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E1.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 A user account that was originally created in the IBM Sterling B2B Integrator (SBI) user interface was assigned an IBM Sterling File Gateway (SFG) partner's Identity in the user account. When that user account logs in to My File Gateway and clicks on the dropdown arrow for the Mailbox Path field on the Upload Files tab, there are a number of mailboxes showing instead of just the main mailbox of the SFG partner.
- `E1.S3`: SYMPTOM
Multiple, unrelated mailboxes appear as options in the dropdown list for the Mailbox Path field of the Upload Files tab in My File Gateway
- `E1.S4`: CAUSE
There are two parts to the cause. The first part is that at least one of the groups of which the User Account is a member has permissions to specific mailboxes. Those are the extra mailboxes showing in the dropdown list. The other part is that, as the user account was not created automatically by creating a partner in the SFG user interface, no virtual root was automatically assigned to it, so it shows every mailbox that the user account has permissions to either directly or through its group memberships.
- `E1.S5`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
There are two choices to resolve the problem. Choose the one that best fits your needs.
- `E1.S6`: Option 1: Create a virtual root for the user account. The advantage to this method is it is specific to the user account. The potential disadvantage is that the user account will only have access to its virtual root mailbox and its sub-mailboxes, even if it needs access to some of the other mailboxes. Create the virtual root by doing the following:
- `E1.S7`: 1. Edit the user account and write down the value in the Identity field. For this example, assume it is Partner537. 
 2. Go to Deployment > Mailboxes > Virtual Roots in the SBI menu. 
 3. Create a virtual root using /Partner537 as the mailbox.
- `E1.S8`: Option 2: Remove the specific mailbox permissions in all groups that the user account is a member of. The advantage to this is it will likely allow you to take care of multiple user accounts in one process. The potential disadvantage is that if any of the members of that group really do need access to all of the mailboxes that the group specifically has permissions to, they will lose them. Change the groups' permissions by doing the following:
- `E1.S9`: 1. Edit the User account and write down all the items showing in the Assigned box of the Groups screen, then click Cancel. 
 2. Go to Accounts > Groups in the SBI menu. 
 3. Type the name of one of the groups written down above in the Group Name field and click Go! 
 4. Click "edit" 
 5. Click the Next button until you are at the Assign Permissions screen. 
 6. Remove all mailbox entries from the Assigned box, then click Save. 
 7. Click Finish. 
 8. Repeat steps 3-7 for all the other groups that the user account is a member of.
- `E1.S10`: NOTE: No method exists for leaving the specific permissions in the groups, but also giving the user account access through My File Gateway to two or more mailboxes that have only the root mailbox as a common ancestor.
- `E1.S11`: Click "edit" 
 5. Click the Next button until you are at the Assign Permissions screen. 
 6. Remove all mailbox entries from the Assigned box, then click Save. 
 7. Click Finish. 
 8. Repeat steps 3-7 for all the other groups that the user account is a member of.
- `E1.S12`: NOTE: No method exists for leaving the specific permissions in the groups, but also giving the user account access through My File Gateway to two or more mailboxes that have only the root mailbox as a common ancestor.
