- `E3.S1`: SSL ; TLS/SSL; TLS 1.0; TLS 1.1; BEAST; Vulnerability; CVE-2011-3389 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 A known SSL/TLS vulnerability, CVE-2011-3389 (also known as BEAST), exists in the SSLv3 and TLS 1.0 protocols. To eliminate this vulnerability, please review the specific configuration recommendations below.
- `E3.S3`: SYMPTOM
Refer to CVE-2011-3389
- `E3.S4`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
The following describes how to prevent the CVE-2011-3389 vulnerability on any firmware version of the IBM WebSphere DataPower appliance.
- `E3.S5`: The protocol problem in this case is the use of a predictable IV (initialization vector) when block cipher CBC mode is used. There are two ways to prevent the attack.
- `E3.S6`: 1. use TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2
- `E3.S7`: The protocol problem that allows the attack was fixed completely starting in TLS 1.1 which changed the spec to use a new, random IV in each encrypted SSL record.
- `E3.S8`: DataPower firmware release 6.0.0 added support for TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 by default. To protect the appliance against the vulnerability enable support for TLS 1.1 and TLS 1.2 in the Crypto Profile while disabling support for TLS 1.0, SSLv3, and SSLv2.
- `E3.S9`: DataPower firmware releases prior to 6.0.0 do not support TLS 1.1 or TLS 1.2 and therefore must use option #2 below to avoid the vulnerability.
- `E3.S10`: 2. Enable the empty data record counter measure (CLI only)
- `E3.S11`: This counter measure can only be enabled using the command line interface (it is not available in the WebGUI).
- `E3.S12`: This counter measure is to send empty data records between the usual data records to effectively randomize the IV value. This behavior is legal according to the SSL/TLS specifications, but some SSL/TLS stacks are not fully compliant to this specification and will reject connections that send such records. Therefore use of this setting may result in incompatibility with SSL/TLS stacks that are not standards compliant such as the one in some versions of Microsoft Internet Explorer (IE).
- `E3.S13`: The Crypto Profile has a property called Options. Using the command line interface, set the Options field by entering crypto mode and using the profile command with an options mask of 0x10007FF:
- `E3.S14`: profile name idCred [ssl name] [ciphers cipher-string] [options mask]
- `E3.S15`: For example, a Crypto Profile named "alice-cp" uses an Identification Credential named "alice-idcred". The following CLI commands will enable the empty data record counter measure for this Crypto Profile:
- `E3.S16`: top
configure terminal
crypto
profile alice-cp alice-idcred options 0x10007FF
- `E3.S17`: This counter measure only protects one half of the duplex (outgoing data from DataPower). It is up to the SSL peer to protect the other half of the duplex with the same counter measure. If this is undesirable then use #1 or #3 instead.
- `E3.S18`: 3. Use SSL Server Profile or SSL SNI Server Profile with firmware version 7.2.0 or later
- `E3.S19`: In 7.2.0 release, IBM DataPower Gateways introduced SSL Server Profile and SSL SNI Server Profile. These 2 profiles are not vulnerable to this advisory, as they will always send empty data records between the usual data records.
- `E3.S20`: Cross reference information Segment Product Component Platform Version Edition Business Integration WebSphere DataPower B2B Appliance XB60 4.0.2, 4.0.1,
- `E4.S1`: the web.xml because the Web page URL was invalid.
- `E4.S2`: * Scenario 2 - ODR Configuration Solution
   The proxy port setting for the ODR is not mapped to the appropriate virtual host group. This can be done using the administrative console:  1. Find the ODR proxy http  1. Expand the Servers topology 
        2. Select the On Demand Routers entry. 
        3. Under Additional Properties select the End Points. 
        4. Select the PROXY_HTTP_ADDRESS entry to find the ODR host/port settings
- `E4.S3`: 2. Add a new alias for the ODR proxy http port in the interested virtual host group:  1. Expand the Environment topology. 
        2. Choose the Virtual Hosts entry. 
        3. Choose appropriate virtual host group (for example: "default_host") 
        4. Under Additional Properties select the Host Aliases. 
        5. Click New to create a new alias 
        6. Fill out the correct host/port entry (for example: the ODR proxy http port information). 
        7. Click OK. 
        8. Save and synchronize the change.
- `E4.S4`: 3. Recycle the ODR and application servers to pick up the new virtual host alias. The configuration information can be seen below. From the serverindex.xml file you can find the http proxy address used by the ODR. This port was used in the url by the user to hit the ODR so it can route the request to the running server.
- `E4.S5`: <specialEndpoints xmi:id="NamedEndPoint_#" endPointName="PROXY_HTTP_ADDRESS">
       <endPoint xmi:id="EndPoint_#" host="<hostname/ip address>" port="83"/>
       </specialEndpoints> 
       Review the web module information to determine the virtual host mapping located in the ibm-web-bnb.xmi file, search for "virtualHostName" entry. This mapping will show the actual virtual host requiring the http proxy port alias. For this example we will assume it is the "default_host" group.
- `E4.S6`: The virtualhost.xml file will show the list of port aliases for the interested virtual host group where we should find under the interested virtual host the ODR proxy http port, port 83 for this example. 
       <host:VirtualHost xmi:id="VirtualHost_#" name="default_host">
       ...
       <aliases xmi:id="HostAlias_#" hostname="*" port="83"/>
       </host:VirtualHost> 
       Note: If the port is 80, then the following entry in the virtualhost.xml file will show the following: 
       <aliases xmi:id="HostAlias_#" hostname="*"/>

## techqa_DEV_Q111#row-0130

Question:
StaleConnectionException errors with BPM databases There is much published documentation about stale connections to databases on the web, and yet stale connections continue to be a very common problem, at least with BPM databases. The condition can manifest itself in different ways. The most common experience of a stale connection is from error messages in the log or FFDCs that contain "StaleConnectionException".

Reference / gold answer:
Based on the provided context, the issue of StaleConnectionException errors with BPM databases may be caused by a problem with the JCC driver version. To resolve this issue, it is recommended to upgrade the JCC driver to version 3.59.81 that was shipped with DB2 v9.5fp6a or later and DB2 v9.7fp2 or later, as this fix incorporates a solution for the stale connection exceptions. Additionally, as a workaround, "COMMIT ON RETURN YES" can be added to the definition of stored procedures on the host. It is also suggested to check for restrictions on using this clause and ensure that the APAR IZ07301 fix is applied. If the issue persists, contacting Technical Support for additional troubleshooting options may be necessary.

Reference evidence:
- `0b`: Websphere Application aborts after calling z/OS stored procedure because of stale connection exceptions. SYMPTOM
- `0c`: StaleConnectionException may be seen after upgrade JCC driver.
- `0j`: point, 0x2413 does not match expected code point, 0x2408. ERRORCODE=-
- `0k`: 4499, SQLSTATE=null:com.ibm.db2.jcc.am.qo: [jcc][t4][2028][11149]
- `0l`: [3.58.136] Actual code point, 0x2413 does not match expected code point, 0x2408. ERRORCODE=-4499, SQLSTATE=null
- `0n`: Fix for this issue incorporated in JCC driver version 3.59.81 that was shipped with DB2 v9.5fp6a or later and DB2 v9.7fp2 or later (defect 134363): https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IC66739 [https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IC66739]
- `0o`: As a workaround, "COMMIT ON RETURN YES" can be added to the definition of stored procedure on the host.
- `0p`: You might receive SQL0751N or XAER_NOTA on XA END while using "COMMIT ON RETURN YES" if stored procedure call is a part of XA transaction.
- `0q`: Please check for restriction on using this clause in the technote 1433093: https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21433093 [https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21433093] or

=== CANDIDATE A ===

- `E4.S1`: crash; recovery; full; fail; failure; logvol; datavol TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E4.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 The SFS msg file has messages "ENC-log-0258 log volume is out of space" and "Compressing data on log volume 1 (log_Ssfs_svr) for space reclamation".
- `E4.S3`: CAUSE
An incident occurred that caused a transaction not to finish in the SFS. The incident could be a CICS region crash or a batch program abend.
- `E4.S4`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
In my experience, the problem with the log volume becoming full
- `E4.S5`: and causing the (SFS and RQS) server to crash always has the root cause
of the presence of a transaction being in the commitcomplete state.
A transaction is in the commitcomplete state when all participants
have agreed to commit, and then one of the participants has failed to
actually perform its commit. I will now explain why even one such
transaction can cause the log to fill up.
- `E4.S6`: As log records are written to the log, the log will continue to become
more full. The log regularly checks itself to see how much free space it has.
When the percent of free space is sufficiently small, say 25%, it will check
to see if it can throw away old records. When you see the log go from 75% full
to 1% full, that's because the oldest record for any transaction that is still alive
is quite recent, and virtually all of the records in the log can be thrown away and their
space reclaimed. When a transaction is in the commitcomplete state, as far as the
log is concerned, that transaction is still alive. Therefore none of the log records
put in the log since that transaction can be thrown away, and the log will fill up
until the server crashes.
- `E4.S7`: In other words, the log filling up is not really caused by too much work being
done now, but rather because there is an old unfinished transaction clogging up the log.
- `E4.S8`: The normal method of handling the log filling up to a dangerous level is 2 steps:
1) tkadmin list transaction
- `E4.S9`: Then examine the output and see if there are any transactions in the commitcomplete state.
If there are any, then for all of them, perform step 2
- `E4.S10`: 2) tkadmin force transaction <tid> -finish
- `E4.S11`: If this command succeeds, then the transaction which was stuck is now dead.
The next time the log tries to throw away old records and reclaim space,
it will detect that this oldest record for the stuck transaction is dead, and reclaim
all the space for all records until a live transaction record is reached, Usually the log
will now have most of its space free.
- `E4.S12`: However, the force tran -finish does not explicitly reclaim space, so the log may
still appear to be full.
- `E4.S13`: In some cases bringing down the CICS region may help to determine which transactions to perform the force on.
- `E4.S14`: 3) tkadmin force checkpoint
- `E4.S15`: Now the log checks its oldest record, sees that the tran for that record is dead, and
reclaims space as discussed above.
- `E4.S16`: still appear to be full.
- `E4.S17`: In some cases bringing down the CICS region may help to determine which transactions to perform the force on.
- `E4.S18`: 3) tkadmin force checkpoint
- `E4.S19`: Now the log checks its oldest record, sees that the tran for that record is dead, and
reclaims space as discussed above.
- `E4.S20`: Other DCF documents to review - 
Resolving a Stuck Transaction: 
http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21045910 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21045910]
- `E4.S21`: Expanding CICS volumes on UNIX systems 
http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21616731 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21616731]
- `E4.S22`: Expanding CICS volumes - Windows Edition
https://developer.ibm.com/answers/questions/165307/how-can-i-expand-the-txseries-sfs-volumes-on-windo.html [https://developer.ibm.com/answers/questions/165307/how-can-i-expand-the-txseries-sfs-volumes-on-windo.html]

Question:
What versions of WSAS using Oracle 12c are supported? What versions of WSAS using Oracle 12c are supported?

Reference / gold answer:
The versions of WebSphere Application Server (WSAS) using Oracle 12c that are supported are as follows:

- For IBM Emptoris Contract Management 9.5 through 10.0.2.5, WSAS version 8.0.0.x with Interim Fix PI27100 is supported.
- For IBM Emptoris Program Management 10.0.0 through 10.0.2.5, WSAS version 8.5.0.x with Interim Fix PI27099 is supported.
- For IBM Emptoris Sourcing 10.0.0 through 10.0.2.5, WSAS version 8.5.0.x with Interim Fix PI27099 is supported.
- For IBM Emptoris Spend Analysis 10.0.0 through 10.0.2.5, WSAS version 8.5.0.x with Interim Fix PI27099 is supported.
- For IBM Emptoris Supplier Lifecycle Management 9.5 through 10.0.2.5, WSAS version 8.5.0.x with Interim Fix PI27099 is supported.
- For IBM Emptoris Strategic Supply Management 10.0.0 through 10.0.2.5, WSAS version 8.5.5.x with Interim Fix PI27099 is supported.
- For IBM Emptoris Rivermine Telecom Expense Management 6.5.x through 7.0.1, WSAS version 8.5.5.x with Interim Fix PI27099 is supported.
- For IBM Emptoris Services Procurement 10.0.0, WSAS version 8.5.5.x with Interim Fix PI27099 is supported.

These versions of WSAS with the specified Interim Fixes are compatible with Oracle 12c when running IBM Emptoris applications.

- `E2.S1`: v6Rnotes; v601rnotes TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E2.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When WebSphere Application Server attempts to recover Oracle database transactions, the following exception is issued:
- `E2.S3`: WTRN0037W: The transaction service encountered an error on an xa_recover operation. The resource was com.ibm.ws.rsadapter.spi.WSRdbXaResourceImpl@1114a62. The error code was XAER_RMERR. The exception stack trace follows: javax.transaction.xa.XAException
at oracle.jdbc.xa.OracleXAResource.recover(OracleXAResource.java:726)
at com.ibm.ws.rsadapter.spi.WSRdbXaResourceImpl.recover(WSRdbXaResourceImpl.java:954)
at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.XARminst.recover(XARminst.java:137)
at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.XARecoveryData.recover(XARecoveryData.java:609)
at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.PartnerLogTable.recover(PartnerLogTable.java:511)
at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.RecoveryManager.resync(RecoveryManager.java:1784)
at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.RecoveryManager.run(RecoveryManager.java:2241)
- `E2.S4`: CAUSE
Oracle requires that you have special permissions to attempt to perform the recovery.
If there is a system crash during a distributed transaction, the WebSphere Application Server transaction manager will attempt to clean up any failed transactions which it finds in the transaction logs. 
When the recovery involves an Oracle XAResource, the Oracle JDBC driver 
oracle.jdbc.xa.OracleXAResource.recover function will make a call to DIST_TXN_SYNC.
- `E2.S5`: The above error occurs when the user trying to execute the .recover method does not have sufficient privileges to make a call to DIST_TXN_SYNC.
- `E2.S6`: ENVIRONMENT
This problem can occur with all versions of Oracle: 10g, 11g, and 12g.
- `E2.S7`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Run the following commands as user SYS:
- `E2.S8`: grant select on pending_trans$ to <user>; 
grant select on dba_2pc_pending to <user>;
grant select on dba_pending_transactions to <user>;
grant execute on dbms_system to <user>; (If using Oracle 10.2.0.3 or lower JDBC driver)
grant execute on dbms_xa to <user>; (If using Oracle 10.2.0.4 or higher JDBC driver)
- `E2.S9`: Where <user> is the username configured in the Oracle datasource's authentication alias.
- `E2.S10`: This problem is mentioned under Oracle bug: 3979190. Running the preceding commands solve the problem.
- `E2.S11`: Update: Since the SYS.DBMS_SYSTEM package contains many procedures, granting execute privileges to that package gives access to all of them. In Oracle patch 5892995 (JDBC driver) and 5945463 (server), Oracle has moved the DIST_TXN_SYNC procedure to a new package called DBMS_XA. These patches are available in 10.2.0.4 and higher. By using the new DBMS_XA package, it will reduce the security risk which DBMS_SYSTEM might cause.
- `E2.S12`: If the recovery of the inflight transactions is not important, then one possible workaround to this problem is to remove the transaction logs. (Does NOT apply to WebSphere Process Server and IBM Business Process Manager, please see note below for details)
- `E2.S13`: The transaction logs are stored in the following folder:
<WebSphere Application Server_install_root>\profiles\<PROFILE_NAME>\tranlog\<CELL_NAME>\<NODE_NAME>\<SERVER_NAME>\transaction
- `E2.S14`: To remove the transaction logs, do the following:
(1) Stop the server.
(2) Delete the '\transaction' folder and all subdirectories.
(3) Restart the server. 
The above exceptions will no longer occur.
- `E2.S15`: NOTE: Transaction logs should NOT be deleted if running in a WebSphere Process Server or IBM Business Process Manager environment. 
The WebSphere Process Server and IBM Business Process Manager systems can get into an inconsistent state because the logs are tightly coupled with information in other places like BPEDB, WPSDB, SIB messages and MQ, if it is configured.
- `E2.S16`: If WebSphere Process Server or IBM Business Process Manager is being used, follow the information in this document:
- `E2.S17`: How to resolve Transaction- and Partnerlog recovery issues in WebSphere Process Server (WPS) and IBM Business Process Manager (BPM)
https://developer.ibm.com/answers/questions/168157/how-to-resolve-transaction-and-partnerlog-recovery.html [https://developer.ibm.com/answers/questions/168157/how-to-resolve-transaction-and-partnerlog-recovery.html]
- `E2.S18`: RELATED INFORMATION
 A simplified Chinese translation is available [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21621220]
- `E2.S19`: is configured.
- `E2.S20`: If WebSphere Process Server or IBM Business Process Manager is being used, follow the information in this document:

https://developer.ibm.com/answers/questions/168157/how-to-resolve-transaction-and-partnerlog-recovery.html [https://developer.ibm.com/answers/questions/168157/how-to-resolve-transaction-and-partnerlog-recovery.html]

- `E3.S1`: admin.passwd; index.html TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Use of Installation Manager (IM) to install IBM HTTP Server (IHS webserver) starts with IHS version 8.0.0.0. Prior to use of IM, the fixpacks for IHS (V7 and V6.x) did not include files expected to be customized such as default static content files like index.html and other HTML, GIF, and ICO files installed by IHS to its <IBM HTTP Server home>/htdocs directory. More importantly the admin.passwd file (that holds the user/passsword for the IHS Admin Service) is usually configured right after install when using the Plugin Configration Tool (PCT).
- `E3.S3`: Prior to use of IM you could not install directly to a fixpack level. You had to install the base GA code (i.e. 7.0.0.0 or 6.1.0.0) and then use the Update Installer to apply fixpacks. IM supports installation directly to a fixpack level therefore all install files included with the base GA code 8.0.0.0 are applied with the fixpack. Any files that should not be overwritten must be listed in a exception list (of non-serviceable files) that the IM installer can reference. This list of non-serviceable files was ommitted or incomplete for IHS V8.0.0.0 and 8.5.0.0 so the install of the first fixpack (regardless of fixpack level) may overwrite files such as admin.passwd and index.html.
- `E3.S4`: There are two APAR related to the same event: 
. 
PM71612: ADDITIONAL NON-SERVICEABLE FILES ADDED FOR IBM HTTP SERVER. 
http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PM71612 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PM71612]
. 
PM63634: IHS CONFIG ADMIN.PASSWD FILE WAS RESET AFTER INSTALLING 
FIXPACK 3 ON WAS 8.0.0.2 or 7.0.0.25 on Windows. 
http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PM63634 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PM63634]
- `E3.S5`: . 
The technote about PM63634: IHS CONFIG ADMIN.PASSWD FILE WAS RESET advises a resolution in reseting the admin.passwd file:
- `E3.S6`: Installation of IBM HTTP Server 7.0.0.25, 8.0.0.1, 8.0.0.2, 8.0.0.3 will overlay admin.passwd:
http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21593118 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21593118]
- `E3.S7`: The main impact is that the IHS admin.passwd file gets overwritten which means the IHS Admin User/PW must be reset with the htpasswd utility in the IHS bin directory. Some customers customize the IHS splash page (index.html) or other default pages provided by IHS install so apply of first fixpack can overwrite these files and the customer's customization.
- `E3.S8`: The list of these non-serviceable files where included in 8.0.0.5 and 8.5.0.1 per the APAR links above so once that fixpack level is applied then any future fixpacks will not overwrite these files. There is no way to avoid the event if GA 8.0.0.0/8.5.0.0 IHS is installed first. The first fixpack applied (of any fixpack) could replace the files.
- `E3.S9`: This Technote defines three recommendations to avoid the problem.
- `E3.S10`: SYMPTOM
- The admin.passwd is a zero byte file after apply of fixpack
- `E3.S11`: - Any content installed under <IBM HTTP Server home>/htdocs by IHS install (default static content files) that have been customized are replaced by their default originals after apply of fixpack
- `E3.S12`: CAUSE
Files not marked as non-serviceable files for IM install of fixpacks for IHS per APAR PM71612
- `E3.S13`: ENVIRONMENT
WebSphere environments that use IHS v8.x to run the WSAS plugin for Webservers to act as proxy front to WSAS appservers.
- `E3.S14`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Support suggests one of three recommendations to avoid the problem:
- `E3.S15`: 1.
- `E3.S16`: apply of fixpack
- `E3.S17`: CAUSE
Files not marked as non-serviceable files for IM install of fixpacks for IHS per APAR PM71612
- `E3.S18`: ENVIRONMENT
WebSphere environments that use IHS v8.x to run the WSAS plugin for Webservers to act as proxy front to WSAS appservers.
- `E3.S19`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Support suggests one of three recommendations to avoid the problem:
- `E3.S20`: 1. Use IM to install IHS at fixpack 8.0.0.5/8.5.0.1 or higher bypassing the install of 8.0.0.0/8.5.0.0
- `E3.S21`: 2. Do not use PCT, configure IHS Admin or use htpasswd (or other customization/config) until after fixpack has been applied.
- `E3.S22`: 3. If you have already installed 8.0.0.0 or 8.5.0.0 then before you apply your first IHS fixpack backup these files:
- `E3.S23`: - admin.passwd
- `E3.S24`: - all content under <IBM HTTP Server home>/htdocs

- `E4.S1`: ITCAM; appservers; prerequisites; CAMJ2ALL; CAMJ2ENV TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E4.S2`: QUESTION
 What application servers are supported by ITCAM for J2EE agent v7.1.1? What has changed if compared to the previous version of this product?
- `E4.S3`: ANSWER
These application servers and J2SE applications are supported:
- Apache Tomcat 4.x, 5.x, 6.x, 7.x 
- JBoss 3.x, 4.x, and 5.x
- Oracle WebLogic Server 9.x, 10.x, and 12.x; Oracle WebLogic Portal Server 9.x and 10.x
- SAP NetWeaver 7.0 (2004s), 7.1, 7.3, and 7.4
- J2SE applications
- `E4.S4`: JBoss EAP versions 6.1.0, 6.2.0, 6.3.0, and 6.4.0 support has been introduced starting from 7.1.1.0-TIV-ITCAM_J2EE-IF0003
- `E4.S5`: Support for versions highlighted in boldface is new in release 7.1.1
- `E4.S6`: Support for versions highlighted in italics had already been introduced starting from 6.1 FP6 and later interim-fixes (typically 6.1.0.6-TIV-ITCAMfJ2EE_MP-IF000x, see their readmes for details).
In fact J2EE v6.x has gone out of support at this point, so you will have to upgrade to v7.1.1.0.x to use a supported version.
- `E4.S7`: Java 7 support has been officially introduced in version 7.1.1.
Java 8 support has been introduced starting from 7.1.1.0-TIV-ITCAM_J2EE-IF0003
- `E4.S8`: The following application servers are not supported anymore in the J2EE agent 7.1.1:
- `E4.S9`: - Oracle/BEA Application Server
- Sun JSAS
- WebSphere Application Server Community Edition

http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21593118 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21593118]
- `E2.S7`: The main impact is that the IHS admin.passwd file gets overwritten which means the IHS Admin User/PW must be reset with the htpasswd utility in the IHS bin directory. Some customers customize the IHS splash page (index.html) or other default pages provided by IHS install so apply of first fixpack can overwrite these files and the customer's customization.
- `E2.S8`: The list of these non-serviceable files where included in 8.0.0.5 and 8.5.0.1 per the APAR links above so once that fixpack level is applied then any future fixpacks will not overwrite these files. There is no way to avoid the event if GA 8.0.0.0/8.5.0.0 IHS is installed first. The first fixpack applied (of any fixpack) could replace the files.
- `E2.S9`: This Technote defines three recommendations to avoid the problem.
- `E2.S10`: SYMPTOM
- The admin.passwd is a zero byte file after apply of fixpack
- `E2.S11`: - Any content installed under <IBM HTTP Server home>/htdocs by IHS install (default static content files) that have been customized are replaced by their default originals after apply of fixpack
- `E2.S12`: CAUSE
Files not marked as non-serviceable files for IM install of fixpacks for IHS per APAR PM71612
- `E2.S13`: ENVIRONMENT
WebSphere environments that use IHS v8.x to run the WSAS plugin for Webservers to act as proxy front to WSAS appservers.
- `E2.S14`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Support suggests one of three recommendations to avoid the problem:
- `E2.S15`: 1.
- `E2.S16`: apply of fixpack

- `E4.S1`: v61rnotes; SQLException ORA-01483; v612rnotes TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E4.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 If WebSphere® Process Server is configured with Oracle 9i as the database, and Oracle Thin Driver as the database driver, failed events are not saved to the database if the event size is larger than 4 KB.
- `E4.S3`: SYMPTOM
The following exception is written to the logs:
- `E4.S4`: java.sql.SQLException: ORA-01483: invalid length for DATE or NUMBER bind variable
DSRA0010E: SQL State = 72000, Error Code = 1,483 
CAUSE
The Oracle 9i Thin Driver limits the size of data to no more than 4 KB for VARCHAR2, NVARCHAR2, BLOB, and CLOB types.
- `E4.S5`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Use either of the following solutions to solve the problem:
- `E4.S6`: * Use the Oracle 10g driver file.  1. Log on to the administrative console and navigate to Environment > WebSphere Variables.
- `E4.S7`: 2. Select the variable ORACLE_JDBC_DRIVER_PATH.
- `E4.S8`: 3. Change the variable value to the folder that contains the Oracle 10g driver (ojdbc14.jar).
- `E4.S9`: 4. Save the configuration.
- `E4.S10`: 5. Restart the server.
- `E4.S11`: Note: In a network deployment environment, change the variable value at the cell level and in all of the nodes scopes, and restart all of the servers and deployment manager processes.
- `E4.S12`: * If the Oracle server or client is installed and configured correctly on the same system as WebSphere Process Server, change the data source to use the Oracle 9i OCI driver.  1. Log on to the administrative console and navigate to Resources > JDBC > Data sources.
- `E4.S13`: 2. Select the data source with the JNDI name jdbc/WPSDB.
- `E4.S14`: 3. Change the URL format from Thin to OCI. For example, if the original URL is jdbc:oracle:thin:@localhost:1521:WPRCSDB, change it to jdbc:oracle:oci:@WPRCSDB.
- `E4.S15`: 4. Save the configuration.
- `E4.S16`: 5. Restart the server.
- `E5.S1`: v6Rnotes; v601rnotes TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E5.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When WebSphere Application Server attempts to recover Oracle database transactions, the following exception is issued:
- `E5.S3`: WTRN0037W: The transaction service encountered an error on an xa_recover operation. The resource was com.ibm.ws.rsadapter.spi.WSRdbXaResourceImpl@1114a62. The error code was XAER_RMERR. The exception stack trace follows: javax.transaction.xa.XAException
at oracle.jdbc.xa.OracleXAResource.recover(OracleXAResource.java:726)
at com.ibm.ws.rsadapter.spi.WSRdbXaResourceImpl.recover(WSRdbXaResourceImpl.java:954)
at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.XARminst.recover(XARminst.java:137)
at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.XARecoveryData.recover(XARecoveryData.java:609)
at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.PartnerLogTable.recover(PartnerLogTable.java:511)
at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.RecoveryManager.resync(RecoveryManager.java:1784)
at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.RecoveryManager.run(RecoveryManager.java:2241)
- `E5.S4`: CAUSE
Oracle requires that you have special permissions to attempt to perform the recovery.
If there is a system crash during a distributed transaction, the WebSphere Application Server transaction manager will attempt to clean up any failed transactions which it finds in the transaction logs. 
When the recovery involves an Oracle XAResource, the Oracle JDBC driver 
oracle.jdbc.xa.OracleXAResource.recover function will make a call to DIST_TXN_SYNC.
- `E5.S5`: The above error occurs when the user trying to execute the .recover method does not have sufficient privileges to make a call to DIST_TXN_SYNC.
- `E5.S6`: ENVIRONMENT
This problem can occur with all versions of Oracle: 10g, 11g, and 12g.
- `E5.S7`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Run the following commands as user SYS:
- `E5.S8`: grant select on pending_trans$ to <user>; 
grant select on dba_2pc_pending to <user>;
grant select on dba_pending_transactions to <user>;
grant execute on dbms_system to <user>; (If using Oracle 10.2.0.3 or lower JDBC driver)
grant execute on dbms_xa to <user>; (If using Oracle 10.2.0.4 or higher JDBC driver)
- `E5.S9`: Where <user> is the username configured in the Oracle datasource's authentication alias.
- `E5.S10`: This problem is mentioned under Oracle bug: 3979190. Running the preceding commands solve the problem.
- `E5.S11`: Update: Since the SYS.DBMS_SYSTEM package contains many procedures, granting execute privileges to that package gives access to all of them. In Oracle patch 5892995 (JDBC driver) and 5945463 (server), Oracle has moved the DIST_TXN_SYNC procedure to a new package called DBMS_XA. These patches are available in 10.2.0.4 and higher. By using the new DBMS_XA package, it will reduce the security risk which DBMS_SYSTEM might cause.
- `E5.S12`: If the recovery of the inflight transactions is not important, then one possible workaround to this problem is to remove the transaction logs. (Does NOT apply to WebSphere Process Server and IBM Business Process Manager, please see note below for details)
- `E5.S13`: The transaction logs are stored in the following folder:
<WebSphere Application Server_install_root>\profiles\<PROFILE_NAME>\tranlog\<CELL_NAME>\<NODE_NAME>\<SERVER_NAME>\transaction
- `E5.S14`: To remove the transaction logs, do the following:
(1) Stop the server.
(2) Delete the '\transaction' folder and all subdirectories.
(3) Restart the server. 
The above exceptions will no longer occur.
- `E5.S15`: NOTE: Transaction logs should NOT be deleted if running in a WebSphere Process Server or IBM Business Process Manager environment. 
The WebSphere Process Server and IBM Business Process Manager systems can get into an inconsistent state because the logs are tightly coupled with information in other places like BPEDB, WPSDB, SIB messages and MQ, if it is configured.
- `E5.S16`: If WebSphere Process Server or IBM Business Process Manager is being used, follow the information in this document:
- `E5.S17`: How to resolve Transaction- and Partnerlog recovery issues in WebSphere Process Server (WPS) and IBM Business Process Manager (BPM)
https://developer.ibm.com/answers/questions/168157/how-to-resolve-transaction-and-partnerlog-recovery.html [https://developer.ibm.com/answers/questions/168157/how-to-resolve-transaction-and-partnerlog-recovery.html]
- `E5.S18`: RELATED INFORMATION
 A simplified Chinese translation is available [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21621220]

ORA-01795 Error accessing Decision Center Business Console 8.7 I am working with ODM 8.7.0.0 when accessing the Business Console I am getting the below error message :
ORA-01795: maximum number of expressions in a list is 1000
The diagnostics do not contain any warning nor error.

Reference / gold answer:
Based on the provided context, it seems that the issue with ORA-01795 error accessing the Decision Center Business Console 8.7 in ODM 8.7.0.0 is related to a query using a list with more than 1000 elements as part of its query. To address this issue, a fix may be needed in the code that handles the query to ensure that it does not exceed the limit of 1000 expressions in a list. It is recommended to check if there is a fix available for ODM 8.7.0.0 that addresses this specific issue. Alternatively, you may need to follow the instructions provided in the APAR documentation for a temporary fix or workaround until a permanent solution is available.

   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: When  attempting to issue a             *
   *                      long-running scheduler command using    *
   *                      lrcmd.[bat|sh] through the On-Demand    *
   *                      Router (ODR), an IOException will be    *
   *                      returned as follows:                    *
   *                                                              *
   *                      C:\IBM\WebSphere\AppServer\bin>lrcmd    *
   *                      -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\SimpleCIxJCL.xml   *
   *                      -port=<ODR port> -host=<ODR hostname>   *
   *                                                              *
   *                      CWLRB4940I: com.ibm.ws.batch.wsbatch :  *
   *                      -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\SimpleCIxJCL.xml   *
   *                      -port=<ODR port> -host=<ODR hostname>   *
   *                                                              *
   *                      CWLRB4880E: -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\Simple *
   *                      CIxJCL.xml -port=<ODR port>             *
   *                      -host=<ODR hostname> failed:            *
   *                      com.ibm.ws.batch.wsbatch: java.io.      *
   *                      IOException:Connection close: Read      *
   *                      failed.  Possible end of stream         *
   *                      encountered.                            *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   The problem was caused by assuming in the code the every SOAP
   request will have a web module with web service and operation
   node defined. Therefore for the cases where web service and
   operation nodes do not exist, trying to use the operation map
   to get a key results in a null pointer exception. To the
   caller this wrapped up exception shows up as an IO Exception.
- `E3.S9`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  For each SOAP over HTTP request, check for the definition of
   web service and web service operation nodes, if they exist use
   them to fetch the workclasses and perform further request
   classification as necessary, otherwise, use the original
   request mapping to route request.

- `E5.S1`: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E5.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When I run a DVS test from RTS, I get the following error: "Host and port appear to be responsive but the service "/testing/repositoryService" does not exist."
- `E5.S3`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
- `E5.S4`: This might be due to user errors in configuration. For example, you could have set the URL of the Rule Execution Server to be 'http://<host>:<port>/testing' instead of 'http://<host>:<port>/res" in the RTS configuration.
- `E5.S5`: . When you add a new server to the RTS configuration ( Websphere ILOG Rule Team Server online help > Configure: Manage your project configuration > Managing servers [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brdotnet/v7r0m2/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.brdotnet.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/Rules_for_DotNET/ps_RFDN_Global716.html]), make sure you specify the URL of the Rule Execution Server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/res).
- `E5.S6`: A common mistake is to specify the URL of the SSP server (e.g.: http://localhost:8080/testing), which leads to the error above.
- `E5.S7`: This error could also indicate that the SSP is not correctly deployed or configured.
- `E5.S8`: Please check that the SSP is correctly deployed and configured.
- `E5.S9`: Examine the application server logs for error messages which indicate the root of the problem. For example, you could have multiple SSPs deployed and different XOMs integrated into different SSPs. In that case, make sure that you have one SSP deployed and active, and all the XOMs are integrated within it.
- `E5.S10`: Also note that the SSP and the RES management console are expected to be deployed on the same server outside the cluster, and no other SSP should be deployed inside the cluster, See Clustering Decision Validation Services [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21425487] for more details.
- `E5.S11`: If these recommendations do not help, please contact IBM support with a description of your set up and the server logs.

- `E1.S1`: v61rnotes; SQLException ORA-01483; v612rnotes TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E1.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 If WebSphere® Process Server is configured with Oracle 9i as the database, and Oracle Thin Driver as the database driver, failed events are not saved to the database if the event size is larger than 4 KB.
- `E1.S3`: SYMPTOM
The following exception is written to the logs:
- `E1.S4`: java.sql.SQLException: ORA-01483: invalid length for DATE or NUMBER bind variable
DSRA0010E: SQL State = 72000, Error Code = 1,483 
CAUSE
The Oracle 9i Thin Driver limits the size of data to no more than 4 KB for VARCHAR2, NVARCHAR2, BLOB, and CLOB types.
- `E1.S5`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Use either of the following solutions to solve the problem:
- `E1.S6`: * Use the Oracle 10g driver file.  1. Log on to the administrative console and navigate to Environment > WebSphere Variables.
- `E1.S7`: 2. Select the variable ORACLE_JDBC_DRIVER_PATH.
- `E1.S8`: 3. Change the variable value to the folder that contains the Oracle 10g driver (ojdbc14.jar).
- `E1.S9`: 4. Save the configuration.
- `E1.S10`: 5. Restart the server.
- `E1.S11`: Note: In a network deployment environment, change the variable value at the cell level and in all of the nodes scopes, and restart all of the servers and deployment manager processes.
- `E1.S12`: * If the Oracle server or client is installed and configured correctly on the same system as WebSphere Process Server, change the data source to use the Oracle 9i OCI driver.  1. Log on to the administrative console and navigate to Resources > JDBC > Data sources.
- `E1.S13`: 2. Select the data source with the JNDI name jdbc/WPSDB.
- `E1.S14`: 3. Change the URL format from Thin to OCI. For example, if the original URL is jdbc:oracle:thin:@localhost:1521:WPRCSDB, change it to jdbc:oracle:oci:@WPRCSDB.
- `E1.S15`: 4. Save the configuration.
- `E1.S16`: 5. Restart the server.

- `E3.S1`: performance; JRules; DVS. Decision Warehouse; DWH; WODM; Decision Validation Services; improvement; Decision Center; Decision Server TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E3.S2`: QUESTION
 How can I improve the performance of Decision Validation Services (DVS) and Decision Warehouse?
- `E3.S3`: ANSWER
- `E3.S4`: Improving the performance of DVS testing and the Decision Warehouse involves reducing the size of the execution trace data generated during tests, and also some architectural and environmental configurations that might be suited to your use case. The following are recommendations you can consider incorporating:
- `E3.S5`: Reduce the size of the execution data:
- `E3.S6`: * Filter data [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21586717] using the ruleset properties: monitoring.filters and monitoring.inout.filters. 
 * Reduce the BOM serialization overhead:  * Override the toString() method for the ruleset parameters to return minimal information 
    * Set the ruleset property ruleset.bom.enabled to "false" to remove support for BOM based serialization. This property is set to "true" by default when extracting rulesets from Rule Team Server (RTS) and Decision Center, and needs to be explicitly set to "false" in order to deactivate it. (You should set it to "true" if you need to generate an Excel report from a Test Suite/Simulation in RTS.)
- `E3.S7`: Refer to the documentation Optimizing Decision Warehouse for v7.1.x or earlier [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global733.html] and WODM [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.res%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Rule_Execution_Server1571.html]. 
 * Reduce the number of columns in the Excel files by using the Ignore for DVS flag for the arguments in the DVS constructor, in Rule Studio [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global715.html] or Rule Designer [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.rulestudio%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Rule_Designer1303.html&resultof=%22Adding%22%20%22ad%22%20%22removing%22%20%22remov%22%20%22columns%22%20%22column%22%20%22from%22%20%22Excel%22%20%22excel%22%20%22file%22%20]. 
 * You can also choose to not write the traces to a database (Decision Warehouse) as shown in this sample [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21441394].
- `E3.S8`: Configure Decision Warehouse:  * Manage the production and test environments separately [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.overview%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Overview83.html], and use a different Decision Warehouse instance for each environment. 
 * Write asynchronously to Decision Warehouse:  * Using a JMS provider, such as WebSphere MQ or OpenJMS. 
    * Using MDBs or in batch using a ETL tool, such as Clover.ETL or Cognos ETL.
- `E3.S9`: * Perform an asynchronous update to Decision Warehouse, as shown in this sample [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global1781.html] for v7.1.x and earlier (and this sample [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.samples%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Samples588.html] for WODM). 
 * Capture the Decision Warehouse trace as an asynchronous operation in application servers supporting thecommonj WorkManager API, as shown in this sample [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21433167]. 
 * Estimate the database capacity [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21430461] that should be allocated.
- `E3.S10`: Refer to the documentation at Auditing executed decisions [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.overview%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Overview83.html] for detailed recommendations for configuring Decision Warehouse.
- `E3.S11`: Configure Rule Execution Server (RES):  * Do not use a production RES for your tests and simulations. Instead dedicate a separate RES instance for testing. 
 * Set the optimal XU and SSP pool sizes (in v7.1.x or earlier [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global206.html] and WODM [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dcenter.overview%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DC_Overview2884.html]). 
 * Increase the size of the database connection pool for the RES data source. 
 * Dedicate more processing resources to the handling of DVS tests:  * Deploy the SSP along with the RES console on a dedicated server. (By default tests are run on a single SSP, see Clustering Decision Validation Services [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21425487]). 
    * Otherwise, distribute the DVS tests [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21502095] on different RES instances.
- `E3.S12`: * Improve RES performance [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21589513].
- `E3.S13`: Configure Rule Team Server (RTS) or Decision Center:  * Install RTS and RES on separate computers.
- `E3.S14`: with the RES console on a dedicated server. (By default tests are run on a single SSP, see Clustering Decision Validation Services [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21425487]). 
    * Otherwise, distribute the DVS tests [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21502095] on different RES instances.
- `E3.S15`: * Improve RES performance [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21589513].
- `E3.S16`: Configure Rule Team Server (RTS) or Decision Center:  * Install RTS and RES on separate computers. 
 * Reduce the size of the Decision Warehouse trace when running scenario suites from RTS, as shown in this sample [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21438208]. 
 * Improve RTS performance [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21584855].
- `E3.S17`: Configure Rule Studio or Rule Designer:  * Increase the heap size for DVS testing [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21427125]. 
 * Improve Rule Studio or Rule Designer performance [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21589514].
- `E3.S18`: In addition, refer to the sections Enhancing the performance of Decision Warehouse and Enhancing the performance of Decision Validation Services in the IBM Redpaper: Proven Practices for Enhancing Performance: A Q&A for IBM WebSphere ILOG BRMS 7.1 [http://www.redbooks.ibm.com/redpapers/pdfs/redp4775.pdf]. - `E4.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  When you place your inbound web service  inside a toolkit and
   one parameter is defined as a complex type list, the inbound
   web service generated WSDL contains an array type definition
   in a non-existent namespace and the runtime-generated SOAP
   message does not accomplish the WSDL definition. As a result,
   the web service client reports an error when loading the wrong
   WSDL or parsing the SOAP response message.

## techqa_DEV_Q146#row-0056

Question:
Gettting error CRIMC1020E: zip im.properties not found during BPM Fix Pack install During the BPM 7.5.1.2 Fix Pack install from the IBM Installation Manager, error window pop up with:

CRIMC1020E: zip im.properties 1.0.0.200911091101 not found ERROR: `zip im.properties 1.0.0.200911091101` not found in [path to sca.1.0.1.17.fp]. CRIMC1020E: zip config.registry 1.0.0.200911092301 not found
……

How can I resolve this error to complete the Fix Pack installation?

Reference / gold answer:
To resolve the error CRIMC1020E during the BPM 7.5.1.2 Fix Pack installation, you can follow these steps:

1. Check if the required files 'im.properties' and 'config.registry' are present in the specified path ([path to sca.1.0.1.17.fp]). If they are not found, you will need to download these files from the IBM Installation Manager repository.

2. After downloading the missing files, place them in the appropriate directory where the Fix Pack installation is looking for them.

3. Restart the Fix Pack installation process and ensure that the files 'im.properties' and 'config.registry' are correctly located and accessible to the installation process.

4. If the error persists, you may need to verify the integrity of the downloaded files and ensure that they are not corrupted.

By following these steps, you should be able to resolve the CRIMC1020E error and complete the BPM 7.5.1.2 Fix Pack installation successfully.

- `E2.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 You use IBM Packaging Utility to delete a package or fix from a repository. Then, you install a package or a fix from the same repository by using IBM Installation Manager. You receive an error that files cannot be found.
- `E2.S3`: SYMPTOM
You receive one of the following errors:
- `E2.S4`: * From the graphical user interface:
- `E2.S5`: * Failed to find all installation files.
- `E2.S6`: Message ID: CRIMA1161E
- `E2.S7`: Installation Manager was unable to find all artifacts from input repository. A package has an issue that cannot be resolved by Installation Manager.
- `E2.S8`: Check the package repository for consistency. Otherwise, identify the package that has the issue by looking at the installation history. In Installation Manager, click File > Installation History. In console mode, enter S: View Installation History. Contact IBM customer support.
- `E2.S9`: 'jar file <file name>' not found in <repository>.

- `E2.S13`: ERROR: 'zip file <file name>' not found in <repository>.
- `E2.S14`: CAUSE
Packaging Utility deletes additional files when you delete a package or fix from a repository.
- `E2.S15`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
This issue has been fixed in Packaging Utility version 1.6.
- `E2.S16`: To work around this issue, use Packaging Utility to recopy the affected package or fix from the original source to the repository that is missing files.
- `E3.S1`: admin.passwd; index.html TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Use of Installation Manager (IM) to install IBM HTTP Server (IHS webserver) starts with IHS version 8.0.0.0. Prior to use of IM, the fixpacks for IHS (V7 and V6.x) did not include files expected to be customized such as default static content files like index.html and other HTML, GIF, and ICO files installed by IHS to its <IBM HTTP Server home>/htdocs directory. More importantly the admin.passwd file (that holds the user/passsword for the IHS Admin Service) is usually configured right after install when using the Plugin Configration Tool (PCT).
- `E3.S3`: Prior to use of IM you could not install directly to a fixpack level. You had to install the base GA code (i.e. 7.0.0.0 or 6.1.0.0) and then use the Update Installer to apply fixpacks. IM supports installation directly to a fixpack level therefore all install files included with the base GA code 8.0.0.0 are applied with the fixpack. Any files that should not be overwritten must be listed in a exception list (of non-serviceable files) that the IM installer can reference. This list of non-serviceable files was ommitted or incomplete for IHS V8.0.0.0 and 8.5.0.0 so the install of the first fixpack (regardless of fixpack level) may overwrite files such as admin.passwd and index.html.
- `E3.S4`: There are two APAR related to the same event: 
. 
PM71612: ADDITIONAL NON-SERVICEABLE FILES ADDED FOR IBM HTTP SERVER. 
http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PM71612 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PM71612]
. 
PM63634: IHS CONFIG ADMIN.PASSWD FILE WAS RESET AFTER INSTALLING 
FIXPACK 3 ON WAS 8.0.0.2 or 7.0.0.25 on Windows. 
http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PM63634 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PM63634]
- `E3.S5`: . 
The technote about PM63634: IHS CONFIG ADMIN.PASSWD FILE WAS RESET advises a resolution in reseting the admin.passwd file:
- `E3.S6`: Installation of IBM HTTP Server 7.0.0.25, 8.0.0.1, 8.0.0.2, 8.0.0.3 will overlay admin.passwd:
http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21593118 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21593118]
- `E3.S7`: The main impact is that the IHS admin.passwd file gets overwritten which means the IHS Admin User/PW must be reset with the htpasswd utility in the IHS bin directory. Some customers customize the IHS splash page (index.html) or other default pages provided by IHS install so apply of first fixpack can overwrite these files and the customer's customization.
- `E3.S8`: The list of these non-serviceable files where included in 8.0.0.5 and 8.5.0.1 per the APAR links above so once that fixpack level is applied then any future fixpacks will not overwrite these files. There is no way to avoid the event if GA 8.0.0.0/8.5.0.0 IHS is installed first. The first fixpack applied (of any fixpack) could replace the files.
- `E3.S9`: This Technote defines three recommendations to avoid the problem.
- `E3.S10`: SYMPTOM
- The admin.passwd is a zero byte file after apply of fixpack
- `E3.S11`: - Any content installed under <IBM HTTP Server home>/htdocs by IHS install (default static content files) that have been customized are replaced by their default originals after apply of fixpack
- `E3.S12`: CAUSE
Files not marked as non-serviceable files for IM install of fixpacks for IHS per APAR PM71612
- `E3.S13`: ENVIRONMENT
WebSphere environments that use IHS v8.x to run the WSAS plugin for Webservers to act as proxy front to WSAS appservers.
- `E3.S14`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Support suggests one of three recommendations to avoid the problem:
- `E3.S15`: 1.
- `E3.S16`: apply of fixpack
- `E3.S17`: CAUSE
Files not marked as non-serviceable files for IM install of fixpacks for IHS per APAR PM71612
- `E3.S18`: ENVIRONMENT
WebSphere environments that use IHS v8.x to run the WSAS plugin for Webservers to act as proxy front to WSAS appservers.
- `E3.S19`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Support suggests one of three recommendations to avoid the problem:
- `E3.S20`: 1. Use IM to install IHS at fixpack 8.0.0.5/8.5.0.1 or higher bypassing the install of 8.0.0.0/8.5.0.0
- `E3.S21`: 2. Do not use PCT, configure IHS Admin or use htpasswd (or other customization/config) until after fixpack has been applied.
- `E3.S22`: 3. If you have already installed 8.0.0.0 or 8.5.0.0 then before you apply your first IHS fixpack backup these files:
- `E3.S23`: - admin.passwd
- `E3.S24`: - all content under <IBM HTTP Server home>/htdocs
- `E3.S25`: PRODUCT ALIAS/SYNONYM
 IHS

These issues were disclosed as part of the IBM SDK Java™ Technology Edition updates in January 2015. This bulletin also addresses the “FREAK: Factoring Attack on RSA-EXPORT keys" TLS/SSL client and server vulnerability. VULNERABILITY DETAILS CVEID: CVE-2015-0138 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2015-0138] DESCRIPTION: A vulnerability in various IBM SSL/TLS implementations could allow a remote attacker to downgrade the security of certain SSL/TLS connections. An IBM SSL/TLS client implementation could accept the use of an RSA temporary key in a non-export RSA key exchange ciphersuite. This could allow a remote attacker using man-in-the-middle techniques to facilitate brute-force decryption of TLS/SSL traffic between vulnerable clients and servers. This vulnerability is also known as the FREAK attack. - `E2.S1`: IBM WebSphere Application Server; WebSphere Lombardi SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E2.S2`: SUMMARY
 Multiple security vulnerabilities exist in the IBM SDK Java Technology Edition that is shipped with IBM WebSphere Application Server and included in the products that are listed in this document.
- `E2.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
The affected products are shipped with a version of IBM WebSphere Application Server, which is shipped with an IBM SDK Java Technology Edition and is based on the Oracle Java Development Kit (JDK). Oracle has released the January 2014 critical patch updates (CPU), which contain security vulnerability fixes. The IBM SDK for Java Technology Edition has been updated to incorporate the critical patch updates.
The following vulnerabilities are applicable to IBM WebSphere Application Server and for the affected product.
- `E2.S4`: CVEID: CVE-2014-0411 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2014-0411]
Description: Timing differences based on validity of TLS messages 
CVSS Base Score: 4
CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/90357 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/90357] for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:H/Au:N/C:P/I:P/A:N)
- `E2.S5`: Vulnerability fixes for other advisories are included in the IBM SDK Java™ Technology Edition but IBM WebSphere Application Server and the products listed below are not vulnerable to them. You will need to evaluate your own code to determine if you are vulnerable. Refer to the Reference section for more information on the advisories not applicable to IBM WebSphere Application Server.
- `E2.S6`: AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND VERSIONS
WebSphere Lombardi Edition V7.1.0.x, 7.2.0.x
- `E2.S7`: REMEDIATION/FIXES
Install IBM WebSphere Application Server interim fixes as appropriate for your current IBM WebSphere Application Server version as described in Security Bulletin: Multiple vulnerabilities in current IBM SDK for Java for WebSphere Application Server January 2014 CPU [https://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21663938]
- `E2.S8`: WORKAROUNDS AND MITIGATIONS
None
- `E2.S9`: GET NOTIFIED ABOUT FUTURE SECURITY BULLETINS
 Subscribe to My Notifications [ http://www-01.ibm.com/software/support/einfo.html] to be notified of important product support alerts like this.
- `E2.S10`: IMPORTANT NOTE
 IBM strongly suggests that all System z customers be subscribed to the System z Security Portal to receive the latest critical System z security and integrity service. If you are not subscribed, see the instructions on the System z Security web site [http://www.ibm.com/systems/z/solutions/security_subintegrity.html]. Security and integrity APARs and associated fixes will be posted to this portal. IBM suggests reviewing the CVSS scores and applying all security or integrity fixes as soon as possible to minimize any potential risk.

- `E4.S1`: SECURITY BULLETIN SUMMARY There are multiple vulnerabilities in IBM® SDK Java™ Technology Edition that is used by WebSphere Application Server underneath IBM Business Process Manager and WebSphere Lombardi Edition. These issues were disclosed as part of the IBM SDK Java™ Technology Edition updates in January 2015. This bulletin also addresses the “FREAK: Factoring Attack on RSA-EXPORT keys" TLS/SSL client and server vulnerability. VULNERABILITY DETAILS CVEID: CVE-2015-0138 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2015-0138] DESCRIPTION: A vulnerability in various IBM SSL/TLS implementations could allow a remote attacker to downgrade the security of certain SSL/TLS connections. An IBM SSL/TLS client implementation could accept the use of an RSA temporary key in a non-export RSA key exchange ciphersuite. This could allow a remote attacker using man-in-the-middle techniques to facilitate brute-force decryption of TLS/SSL traffic between vulnerable clients and servers. This vulnerability is also known as the FREAK attack. CVSS Base Score: 4.3 CVSS Temporal Score: See http://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/#/vulnerabilities/100691 [http://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/#/vulnerabilities/100691] for the current score CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:N/I:P/A:N) CVEID: CVE-2014-6593 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2014-6593] DESCRIPTION: An unspecified vulnerability related to the JSSE component has partial confidentiality impact, partial integrity impact, and no availability impact. CVSS Base Score: 4 CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/100153 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/100153] for the current score CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:H/Au:N/C:P/I:P/A:N) CVEID: CVE-2015-0400 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2015-0400] DESCRIPTION: An unspecified vulnerability related to the Libraries component could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information. CVSS Base Score: 5 CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/100149 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/100149] for the current score CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:L/Au:N/C:P/I:N/A:N) CVEID: CVE-2015-0410 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2015-0410] DESCRIPTION: An unspecified vulnerability related to the Security component could allow a remote attacker to cause a denial of service. CVSS Base Score: 5 CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/100151 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/100151] for the current score CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:L/Au:N/C:N/I:N/A:P) AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND VERSIONS * IBM Business Process Manager V7.5.x through V8.5.6.0 * WebSphere Lombardi Edition V7.2.0.x For earlier unsupported versions of the products, IBM recommends upgrading to a fixed, supported version of the product. REMEDIATION/FIXES IBM SDK Java™ Technology Edition is used in WebSphere Application Server. See the following two security bulletins for vulnerability details and information about fixes. * Security Bulletin: Vulnerability with RSA Export Keys may affect IBM WebSphere Application Server (CVE-2015-0138) [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21698613] * Security Bulletin: Multiple vulnerabilities in IBM Java SDK affect WebSphere Application Server January 2015 CPU [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21695362] IBM SDK Java™ Technology Edition is also used in IBM Process Designer. Install the interim fix for APAR IT07386 for your current version of IBM Business Process Manager or WebSphere Lombardi Edition. * IBM Business Process Manager Express [http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/quickorder?parent=ibm%7EWebSphere&product=ibm/WebSphere/IBM+Business+Process+Manager+Express&release=All&platform=All&function=aparId&apars=IT07386] * IBM Business Process Manager Standard [http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/quickorder?parent=ibm%7EWebSphere&product=ibm/WebSphere/IBM+Business+Process+Manager+Standard&release=All&platform=All&function=aparId&apars=IT07386] * IBM Business Process Manager Advanced [http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/quickorder?parent=ibm%7EWebSphere&product=ibm/WebSphere/IBM+Business+Process+Manager+Advanced&release=All&platform=All&function=aparId&apars=IT07386] * WebSphere Lombardi Edition [http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/selectFixes?parent=ibm~WebSphere&product=ibm/WebSphere/WebSphere+Lombardi+Edition&release=All&platform=All&function=aparId&apars=IT07386] If you are on earlier unsupported releases, IBM strongly recommends to upgrade. WORKAROUNDS AND MITIGATIONS None GET NOTIFIED ABOUT FUTURE SECURITY BULLETINS Subscribe to My Notifications [ http://www-01.ibm.com/software/support/einfo.html] to be notified of important product support alerts like this. ## techqa_DEV_Q238#row-0136

Question:
recently installed Impact 7.1.0. fixpack 3, now when ever start the secondary impact server, the primary servers logging stops?  How can I fix this? when NCI1 is running by itself, all logging is functioning. When NCI2
is started, logging stops on NCI1 and the "reader" logs indicate that
the readers have stopped. 

Reference / gold answer:
Based on the provided context, the issue you are experiencing after installing Impact 7.1.0 fixpack 3 is likely related to the clustering configuration and how the impact servers are interacting with each other. 

One potential cause for the logging issues when starting the secondary impact server could be related to the failover mechanism not functioning correctly. It seems that the servers are not properly transitioning the primary server role when the secondary server is started.

To resolve this issue, you may need to verify and update the configuration related to failover and clustering in Impact. The recent installation of the fix pack might have introduced changes that are affecting the failover process. 

You might need to review the cluster configuration settings, check the failover settings, and ensure that the servers are able to correctly transition roles from primary to secondary and vice versa. Additionally, reviewing the log files for any errors or warnings related to failover and replication can provide more insights into what might be causing the issue.

It is recommended to reach out to IBM support or refer to the Impact documentation for specific steps on configuring failover and resolving clustering issues in Impact servers.

Reference evidence:
- `0b`:  Attempting to start the Secondary ImpactServer fails.
- `0c`: Secondary ImpactServer fails to start.
- `0e`: Secondary ImpactServer fails to start, configuration not fully copied from Primary ImpactServer to Secondary file system. CAUSE
- `0h`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
- `0j`: In this instance the last thing it is attempting to replicate is the PolicyList.
- `0k`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM

- `E2.S1`: admin.passwd; index.html TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E2.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Use of Installation Manager (IM) to install IBM HTTP Server (IHS webserver) starts with IHS version 8.0.0.0. Prior to use of IM, the fixpacks for IHS (V7 and V6.x) did not include files expected to be customized such as default static content files like index.html and other HTML, GIF, and ICO files installed by IHS to its <IBM HTTP Server home>/htdocs directory. More importantly the admin.passwd file (that holds the user/passsword for the IHS Admin Service) is usually configured right after install when using the Plugin Configration Tool (PCT).
- `E2.S3`: Prior to use of IM you could not install directly to a fixpack level. You had to install the base GA code (i.e. 7.0.0.0 or 6.1.0.0) and then use the Update Installer to apply fixpacks. IM supports installation directly to a fixpack level therefore all install files included with the base GA code 8.0.0.0 are applied with the fixpack. Any files that should not be overwritten must be listed in a exception list (of non-serviceable files) that the IM installer can reference. This list of non-serviceable files was ommitted or incomplete for IHS V8.0.0.0 and 8.5.0.0 so the install of the first fixpack (regardless of fixpack level) may overwrite files such as admin.passwd and index.html.
- `E2.S4`: There are two APAR related to the same event: 
. 
PM71612: ADDITIONAL NON-SERVICEABLE FILES ADDED FOR IBM HTTP SERVER. 
http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PM71612 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PM71612]
. 
PM63634: IHS CONFIG ADMIN.PASSWD FILE WAS RESET AFTER INSTALLING 
FIXPACK 3 ON WAS 8.0.0.2 or 7.0.0.25 on Windows. 
http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PM63634 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PM63634]
- `E2.S5`: . 
The technote about PM63634: IHS CONFIG ADMIN.PASSWD FILE WAS RESET advises a resolution in reseting the admin.passwd file:
- `E2.S6`: Installation of IBM HTTP Server 7.0.0.25, 8.0.0.1, 8.0.0.2, 8.0.0.3 will overlay admin.passwd:
http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21593118 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21593118]
- `E2.S7`: The main impact is that the IHS admin.passwd file gets overwritten which means the IHS Admin User/PW must be reset with the htpasswd utility in the IHS bin directory. Some customers customize the IHS splash page (index.html) or other default pages provided by IHS install so apply of first fixpack can overwrite these files and the customer's customization.
- `E2.S8`: The list of these non-serviceable files where included in 8.0.0.5 and 8.5.0.1 per the APAR links above so once that fixpack level is applied then any future fixpacks will not overwrite these files. There is no way to avoid the event if GA 8.0.0.0/8.5.0.0 IHS is installed first. The first fixpack applied (of any fixpack) could replace the files.
- `E2.S9`: This Technote defines three recommendations to avoid the problem.
- `E2.S10`: SYMPTOM
- The admin.passwd is a zero byte file after apply of fixpack
- `E2.S11`: - Any content installed under <IBM HTTP Server home>/htdocs by IHS install (default static content files) that have been customized are replaced by their default originals after apply of fixpack
- `E2.S12`: CAUSE
Files not marked as non-serviceable files for IM install of fixpacks for IHS per APAR PM71612
- `E2.S13`: ENVIRONMENT
WebSphere environments that use IHS v8.x to run the WSAS plugin for Webservers to act as proxy front to WSAS appservers.
- `E2.S14`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Support suggests one of three recommendations to avoid the problem:
- `E2.S15`: 1.
- `E2.S16`: apply of fixpack
- `E2.S17`: CAUSE
Files not marked as non-serviceable files for IM install of fixpacks for IHS per APAR PM71612
- `E2.S18`: ENVIRONMENT
WebSphere environments that use IHS v8.x to run the WSAS plugin for Webservers to act as proxy front to WSAS appservers.
- `E2.S19`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Support suggests one of three recommendations to avoid the problem:

 *  FFDC has been modified to ensure that incidents can continue
   to be logged from other components when a given component's
   incident-handling hangs a thread.  The impact to this is that
   the FFDC summary log may indicate that the incident file of a
   bad thread was created, while the thread may not have returned
   so the incident file will not exist.  Therefore, a missing
   incident entry that might have appeared in a summary file is
   an indication that the component logging to FFDC did not
   return control.

Since they cannot select it, they can not apply the fix to the virtual machine instances. LOCAL FIX * Use imcl manually to install the fix as described here: Why am I unable to install IBM WebSphere SDK Java Technology Edition 7.1 fix package from PureApplication System maintenance operations panel? https://developer.ibm.com/answers/questions/263001/why-am-i-unab [https://developer.ibm.com/answers/questions/263001/why-am-i-unab] le-to-install-ibm-websphere-sdk-java/ See also: Installation Manager Update Packages dialog does not list WebSphere Liberty https://developer.ibm.com/answers/questions/272058/installation- [https://developer.ibm.com/answers/questions/272058/installation-] manager-update-packages-dialog-does-n/ To confirm that APAR IT14680 is the root cause of a problem where a fix is not listed properly on the Manage > Maintenance page: Confirm that Installation Manager lists the fix as available: - SSH onto the virtual machine where the fix needs to be applied - Update your SSH tool settings so that the commands you issue and their output are saved in a file - Issue the following commands sudo -u virtuser ./imcl listAvailableFixes <fix-name> -repositories http://IBMWorkloadDeployer:8585/IMRepository/Compo [http://IBMWorkloadDeployer:8585/IMRepository/Compo] where <fix-name> is the name of the fix to be applied, for example: sudo -u virtuser ./imcl listAvailableFixes com.ibm.websphere.liberty.ND.v85_8.5.5009.20160227_1546 -repositories http://IBMWorkloadDeployer:8585/IMRepository/Compo [http://IBMWorkloadDeployer:8585/IMRepository/Compo] If an external Installation Manager Repository is also available, also issue sudo -u virtuser ./imcl listAvailableFixes <fix-name> -repositories http://<external-IM-repository> [http://<external-IM-repository>] where <fix-name> is the name of the fix to be applied, and <external-IM-repository> is the URL for the external IM repository. Enable tracing to collect logs with fixpack calculation information included: - Select System > Workload Troubleshooting - Add a trace for "com.ibm.maestro.mgmt.resources.IfixMgmtResource" - Set the trace level to ALL - Recreate the problem - Wait 2 hours - Select System > Workload Troubleshooting again - Download All Logs (take care *not* to choose Download Latest Logs) - Provide the trace.zip file to IBM support To review the logs for information - Unzip trace.zip and look for servers.zip - Unzip servers.zip - Unzip the Kernel Services logs inside servers.zip - Review the Kernel Services logs for log entries from IfixMgmtResource. - `E3.S1`: admin.passwd; index.html TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING) PROBLEM(ABSTRACT) Use of Installation Manager (IM) to install IBM HTTP Server (IHS webserver) starts with IHS version 8.0.0.0. Prior to use of IM, the fixpacks for IHS (V7 and V6.x) did not include files expected to be customized such as default static content files like index.html and other HTML, GIF, and ICO files installed by IHS to its <IBM HTTP Server home>/htdocs directory. More importantly the admin.passwd file (that holds the user/passsword for the IHS Admin Service) is usually configured right after install when using the Plugin Configration Tool (PCT). Prior to use of IM you could not install directly to a fixpack level. You had to install the base GA code (i.e. 7.0.0.0 or 6.1.0.0) and then use the Update Installer to apply fixpacks. IM supports installation directly to a fixpack level therefore all install files included with the base GA code 8.0.0.0 are applied with the fixpack. Any files that should not be overwritten must be listed in a exception list (of non-serviceable files) that the IM installer can reference. This list of non-serviceable files was ommitted or incomplete for IHS V8.0.0.0 and 8.5.0.0 so the install of the first fixpack (regardless of fixpack level) may overwrite files such as admin.passwd and index.html. There are two APAR related to the same event: . PM71612: ADDITIONAL NON-SERVICEABLE FILES ADDED FOR IBM HTTP SERVER. http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PM71612 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PM71612] . PM63634: IHS CONFIG ADMIN.PASSWD FILE WAS RESET AFTER INSTALLING FIXPACK 3 ON WAS 8.0.0.2 or 7.0.0.25 on Windows. http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PM63634 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PM63634] . The technote about PM63634: IHS CONFIG ADMIN.PASSWD FILE WAS RESET advises a resolution in reseting the admin.passwd file: Installation of IBM HTTP Server 7.0.0.25, 8.0.0.1, 8.0.0.2, 8.0.0.3 will overlay admin.passwd: http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21593118 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21593118] The main impact is that the IHS admin.passwd file gets overwritten which means the IHS Admin User/PW must be reset with the htpasswd utility in the IHS bin directory. Some customers customize the IHS splash page (index.html) or other default pages provided by IHS install so apply of first fixpack can overwrite these files and the customer's customization. The list of these non-serviceable files where included in 8.0.0.5 and 8.5.0.1 per the APAR links above so once that fixpack level is applied then any future fixpacks will not overwrite these files. There is no way to avoid the event if GA 8.0.0.0/8.5.0.0 IHS is installed first. The first fixpack applied (of any fixpack) could replace the files. This Technote defines three recommendations to avoid the problem. SYMPTOM - The admin.passwd is a zero byte file after apply of fixpack - Any content installed under <IBM HTTP Server home>/htdocs by IHS install (default static content files) that have been customized are replaced by their default originals after apply of fixpack CAUSE Files not marked as non-serviceable files for IM install of fixpacks for IHS per APAR PM71612 ENVIRONMENT WebSphere environments that use IHS v8.x to run the WSAS plugin for Webservers to act as proxy front to WSAS appservers. RESOLVING THE PROBLEM Support suggests one of

ESR: The deployment code for BPEL applications does not get cleaned up after an appplication "upgrade", or application "uninstall". As a consequence, all subsequent installs will fail. However, the technote only partially describes the problem. According to the nature of the customer's application, the customer will see many different exceptions, dependinf on the features used. We have not met yet the exception described in the tech note; AppDeploymentException: [ ] com.ibm.etools.j2ee.commonarchivecore.exception.SaveFailureExce ption: IWAE0017E Unable to replace original archive: Instead, we meet a "correlation ID" exception, which is described in PMR 03677,999,834. Here is the link: http://d25dbw26.mkm.can.ibm.com/wwqa/wwqades.nsf/WWQADispItem?Op [http://d25dbw26.mkm.can.ibm.com/wwqa/wwqades.nsf/WWQADispItem?Op] enForm&u =3C5499129D032F1D85256FFB00563AE1&h&d=03677999834 This exception is much more confusing, it would not be clear at all tha the problem is related to the failure of removing old ear files. (engl.: name of the object is too long) But the cause is the same; old ear files were not removed after uninstall/re-install: it is necessary to re-boot all application servers. This may generate many different exceptions, depending on what changes were made in the new version of the EAR file. Given that this customer is using the WBISF in a clustered environment, restarting all servers is not trivial.
